Reactive Polymer-Engineered Dual-Targeting Fluorescent Lipid Nanoparticles for Enhanced saRNA Delivery.
leads.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) are widely explored as delivery vehicles for self-amplifying RNA (saRNA); however, incorporation of surface functionalities, such as fluorescent dyes for imaging and ligands for targeted delivery, remains challenging. In this study, we introduce a reactive poly(pentafluorophenyl acrylate) (PPFPA)-based copolymer platform containing a terminal C12 alkyl chain for LNP incorporation and reactive sites for modular conjugation of near-infrared dye IR775, targeting peptides, and polyethylene glycol chains. The resulting copolymers are successfully incorporated into LNPs, enabling fluorescence imaging and targeted delivery while maintaining colloidal stability and low cytotoxicity. Systematic variation of peptide loading and composition identifies an optimal loading of 8 peptides per chain for cellular targeting. Additionally, dual-peptide-functionalized LNPs exhibit higher cellular uptake than single-peptide-functionalized LNPs, with 7-fold and 5-fold increases relative to nonpeptide-functionalized LNPs, respectively. This enhanced uptake translates into increased functional saRNA delivery, with the dual-peptide-functionalized LNPs showing a 128% enhancement in protein expression. These findings establish PPFPA-C12-based copolymers as a versatile platform for designing multifunctional LNP systems for RNA delivery.

leads.title: Poly(propylene carbonate- co -thioether- co -ether) Terpolymer and Its Application as a Solid-State Electrolyte
leads.abstract: Sulfur-containing polymers, especially those with sulfur in the main chain, have attracted significant interest owing to their diverse structures and unique properties, making them promising candidates for solid-state electrolytes. However, their controllable synthesis in metal-free catalysis remains challenging. Herein, a poly(propylene carbonate-co-thioether-co-ether) (PPCTE) terpolymer was synthesized by a one-step copolymerization of carbon dioxide (CO2), epoxides, and ethylene sulfide (ES) in a metal-free catalytic system. The PPCTE polymers with high-sulfur segments of 5% content in the main chain (PPCTE0.05) were obtained by regulating the monomer concentration ratio and the types of metal-free catalysts, yielding molecular weights of 27 kg mol–1. PPCTE0.05 exhibits a relatively low glass transition temperature of 5.8 °C, good thermal decomposition stability with 5% mass loss at 190 °C, and excellent flexibility of 647% elongation at break. Notably, the PPCTE0.05-based solid-state polymer electrolyte achieves a low impedance of 99 Ω, high ionic conductivities (5.36 × 10–5 S cm–1 at room temperature, 1.77 × 10–4 S cm–1 at 60 °C), a low activation energy of 0.29 eV, and a wide electrochemical window of 5.21 V. This work establishes a simple, economical, and eco-friendly synthetic route for main-chain sulfur-containing polymers and offers a valuable reference for designing solid-state polymer electrolytes.

An in situ fabrication of chitosan-TiO2 transparent nanocomposite films from an acid stabilized TiO2 sol, and study on their photocatalytic efficiency.
leads.abstract: Chitosan-TiO 2 nanocomposites in powder form (10 to 60 wt% of chitosan) and in transparent film form (70 to 90 wt% of chitosan) have been synthesized through an in situ method by using an acid stabilized TiO 2 sol. The transparency of these films was evaluated from their optical transmittance measurements. A chitosan-TiO 2 nanocomposite opaque film (with 70 wt% of chitosan) has also been cast through an ex situ method by using TiO 2 nanoparticles, precipitated from the acid stabilized TiO 2 sol. Powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) analysis confirmed the presence of anatase TiO 2 in both the powder and film forms of the chitosan-TiO 2 nanocomposites. FT-IR analysis revealed the presence of characteristic chitosan peaks in all the synthesized composite samples. SEM-EDX analysis of the composite films substantiated the presence of a TiO 2 coating on the film surface, with a thicker coating observed in the ex situ prepared composite film sample, TC70FP. TEM analysis of the representative transparent composite film (TC70F) and the ex situ cast composite film (TC70FP) further confirmed the presence of TiO 2 in these composite samples. The in situ cast films exhibited superior mechanical properties and enhanced thermal stability, as demonstrated by tensile stress-strain and TGA analyses, respectively. They also showed lower swelling indices, while ICP-MS analysis confirmed negligible TiO 2 leaching from the representative in situ cast film TC70F. The in situ cast representative transparent film, TC-70F, was able to degrade methyl orange (MO) solution under UV light irradiation, whereas the pristine chitosan film (ChF) showed no degradation activity.
leads.authors: Prasad JK, E P P, Periyat P, Kunjalukkal Padmanabhan S, Lazar MA.

leads.title: Hop ( Humulus lupulus L.) Residual Biomass: Attributes, Past Experiences and Opportunities for Future Utilization
leads.abstract: Hop (Humulus lupulus L.), a perennial climber plant, has a significant agricultural and industrial presence, primarily valued for its cones in the beer brewing industry. However, the residual biomass, comprising leaves and bines, is often underutilized. Research has highlighted the vast utilization potential of this biomass, which can be effectively utilized as a source of bio-fertilizers through bio-composting, and traditionally for medicinal and fodder purposes, too. Additionally, hop residual biomass has been identified as a potential bast-fiber crop, comprising phloem fibers and woody core. The structural carbohydrates in the hop stem, including cellulose, can have great potential for pulping and production of nanocellulose. Furthermore, the phloem fibers can be used as a filler in natural fiber‑reinforced composites, influencing their mechanical properties. The annual discharge of hop residual biomass in the European Union alone is estimated to be around 100,000–120,000 tons, underscoring the need for sustainable utilization strategies. This review highlights the importance of utilizing hop biomass residues as a raw material for a range of applications. Additionally, by developing efficient processing technologies, the full potential of hop residual biomass can be unlocked, reducing waste and promoting a more circular and sustainable economy.

leads.title: Bio-Inspired Takeoff Mechanism for Flapping-Wing Micro Aerial Vehicles
leads.abstract: Flapping-Wing Micro Aerial Vehicles (FWMAVs) offer distinct advantages, including high thrust-to-weight ratios, low acoustic signatures, and superior maneuverability. Despite these benefits, the operational versatility of FWMAVs is strictly limited by the lack of robust takeoff mechanisms adaptable to diverse terrains. The inherent unsteady aerodynamics and low payload capacity of these vehicles make integrating such systems particularly challenging. This paper addresses this limitation by developing a spring-loaded, jumping-based takeoff mechanism fabricated from PLA. The viability was validated through indoor tethered experiments that characterized the mechanism's launch-phase performance, including a peak vertical interface force of 100 ± 5.5 N. For the given FWMAV configuration and the tested launch-angle range, 35◦ provided the best measured compromise between apex height and forward velocity. The integrated tests demonstrated flight-compatible ballistic launch conditions; sustained free flight, and the subsequent transition to powered flapping flight were not evaluated in this study. This study offers critical insights into the dynamics of ground-to-air transitions for bio-inspired robots, demonstrating that a jump-assisted strategy can overcome the energy constraints associated with vertical liftoff. Ultimately, this system provides a viable ground-launch stage that establishes the necessary kinematic initial conditions for subsequent transition to flapping flight, significantly expanding the mission profile and environmental adaptability of FWMAVs.

leads.title: Improving rainfall productivity and oil yield in camelina through the use of plastic mulch and nitrogen
Immunomodulatory potential of Syzygium cumini seed extracts: a comprehensive evaluation through ın vitro and ın vivo models
leads.abstract: This study evaluates the immunomodulatory potential of Syzygium cumini (jamun) seed extracts using safer solvents—ethyl acetate (EASC) and ethanol (ETSC)—addressing toxicity concerns of methanol. Successive solvent extraction and TLC fingerprinting to differentiate the bioactive compounds between the extracts. The extracts were assessed through in vitro assays (DPPH scavenging, NBT reduction, splenocyte proliferation, Candida albicans phagocytosis) and in vivo cyclophosphamide-induced immunosuppression in rats. The ethanolic extract (ETSC) demonstrated superior antioxidant and immunomodulatory activity compared to EASC, enhancing splenocyte proliferation, phagocytic function, neutrophil adhesion, and bone marrow cellularity. Key outcomes included the restoration of hematological parameters and immune organ indices. ETSC showed dose-dependent efficacy by modulating cytokine release and activating immune cells like macrophages and lymphocytes. The study establishes the therapeutic potential of Syzygium cumini seeds in managing oxidative stress and immune dysfunctions, highlighting ETSC as a promising candidate for further exploration.

leads.title: Cellulose-Based Superabsorbent Hydrogels for Hygiene Applications: A Study of Absorbency Properties
Reaction-Network Kinetics of Lignin Hydrothermal Liquefaction: Effect of Cu Incorporation Strategy
leads.abstract: Cu-based catalysts can enhance bio-oil production during the hydrothermal liquefaction (HTL) of lignin; however, the influence of Cu incorporation strategy on individual reaction pathways remains insufficiently understood. In this study, experimental HTL of lignin under direct Cu-assisted and Cu-impregnated conditions was investigated over 200–320 °C and residence times of 5–25 min, together with a five-pathway lumped kinetic model. Apparent kinetic parameters were estimated by nonlinear regression of the experimental product yields. The model captured the principal evolution of residual solid, bio-oil, water-soluble fraction, and gas over the investigated conditions. The maximum bio-oil yield was obtained at 280 °C and 15 min, increasing from 24.87% for the direct process to 28.74% for Cu-impregnated lignin. Kinetic analysis revealed pathway-dependent effects of Cu impregnation. At 280 °C, the apparent residual-solid-to-bio-oil rate constant (k1) increased from 0.0211 to 0.0402 min-1, whereas the fitted contribution of the direct residual-solid-to-gas pathway (k3) was substantially lower following Cu impregnation. The apparent bio-oil-to-gas rate constant (k4) also increased at elevated temperatures, indicating stronger secondary conversion of bio-oil under more severe conditions. Arrhenius analysis further showed differences in the apparent activation energies and pre-exponential factors of the dominant pathways. Overall, the results demonstrate that Cu impregnation modifies the apparent distribution of reaction pathways rather than uniformly increasing all fitted rate constants, providing a quantitative kinetic framework for understanding the influence of Cu incorporation strategy on lignin HTL.

leads.title: Decoding Polyurethane Breakdown: A QM/MM MD Exploration of UMG-SP3 Urethanase Catalysis
leads.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) low-cost production and versatility propelled its widespread daily usage. However, due to a lack of efficient end-of-life waste treatment options, this recalcitrant polymer tends to accumulate, becoming hazardous. Enzyme depolymerization emerged as a promising 2 alternative to tackle this global problem. Accordingly, three metagenome-based urethanases were discovered (UMG-SP1, 2 and 3). Despite several efforts being made to understand their catalysis, none of the studies accounted for full protein sampling. To address this, we employed an umbrella sampling-based quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics methodology to explore UMG-SP3catalyzed urethane bond hydrolysis. Our results revealed that the hydrolytic mechanism occurred in two sequential stages: i) acylation; and ii) deacylation. The first stage was rate-limiting, with an energetic barrier of 21.6 kcal.mol-1, corresponding to the formation of the acyl-enzyme state and the release of an alcohol (leaving group). Remarkably, the energetic barrier was in agreement with the previously reported values for the UMG-SP2 homolog. In addition, the enzyme shown preference for the cleavage of the C-O bond instead of the C-N bond. However, we observed that the overall reaction was endergonic, with a product-state Gibbs free energy of 8.3 kcal.mol-1. UMG-SP3 has previously been shown to be less stable than the other UMG-SPs. As a result, its more mobile active site may be less effective at stabilizing the released product, increasing the associated free energy. Hence, to improve the likelihood of industrial implementation, the mechanistic data should be leveraged to rationally engineer a more stable and efficient enzyme. Altogether, these findings can pave the way for improving enzymatic depolymerization of PU.

leads.title: A Biobased Epoxy Resin with Sequential Thermoplastic-to-Thermoset Curing Enables Removable-to-Permanent Adhesive Bonding
leads.abstract: Adhesives are commonly designed either as reworkable thermoplastics or permanently crosslinked thermosets. Here, sequential thermoplastic-to-thermoset curing enables a simple two-component formulation based on a bio-based epoxy resin to function first as a removable hot-melt adhesive and subsequently as a permanent structural adhesive. Reaction of diglycidyl ether of vanillyl alcohol (DGEVA) and anilinium methanesulfonate at 110 °C produces a thermoplastic intermediate that is solid at room temperature but flows upon reheating and dissolves in selected solvents. This intermediate forms load-bearing joints that can be thermally debonded and rebonded or disassembled by dissolution. Further heating induces crosslinking and converts the same adhesive layer into a permanent epoxy network, increasing the apparent lap-shear strength nearly eightfold and rendering the joint resistant to disassembly under the same solvent conditions. This curing sequence therefore assigns reworkability and high-strength permanent bonding to successive adhesive states within the same formulation.

leads.title: A Pyrrole-Imidazole Polyamide Targeting Human USF1 Binding Suppresses High Glucose-Induced TGF-β1 and Osteopontin Expression in Human Renal Mesangial Cells
leads.abstract: Transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1) is a key profibrotic mediator in diabetic kidney disease. Upstream stimulatory factor 1 (USF1) enhances TGF-β1 transcription through an E-box/glucose-response element in the TGF-β1 promoter under high-glucose conditions. We designed a sequence-specific pyrrole-imidazole (PI) polyamide targeting the human USF1-binding site in the TGF-β1 promoter and evaluated its activity in human renal mesangial cells (HRMCs). A target PI polyamide and a mismatch PI polyamide were synthesized. DNA binding and inhibition of the USF1-DNA interaction were assessed by gel mobility shift assays. HRMCs were exposed to high glucose with or without PI polyamides, and TGF-β1 and osteopontin expression were quantified by real-time PCR and Western blotting. The target PI polyamide bound the intended promoter sequence and reduced recombinant USF1 binding in vitro. In high-glucose-exposed HRMCs, the target PI polyamide suppressed TGF-β1 mRNA and protein expression, whereas the mismatch PI polyamide did not suppress TGF-β1 expression. The target PI polyamide also reduced osteopontin mRNA expression. These findings provide proof-of-concept that PI polyamide-mediated targeting of the human USF1-TGF-β1 axis can attenuate high-glucose-associated profibrotic responses in HRMCs.

leads.title: Advancing polyallophanate powder coating performance and function with colloidal lignin particles
leads.abstract: Polyallophanate powder coatings are increasingly attractive as sustainable, solvent-free finishing materials, yet their performance and functionality remain limited by the properties of conventional additives. Colloidal lignin particles (CLPs) offer a renewable alternative with intrinsic antioxidant, UV-absorbing, and antibacterial characteristics. In this study, CLPs were produced from organosolv lignin derived from palm oil lignocellulosic residues using three particle size-reduction approaches: sonication, antisolvent, and hybrid. The hybrid method produced the most stable dispersions, yielding spherical CLPs with reduced particle size and increased surface area compared to native lignin. CLPs were incorporated at 1-5 wt% into petroleum-based and lignin-based polyallophanate powder coating formulations to evaluate their influence on thermal, mechanical, surface, antibacterial, and UV-aging behavior. CLP addition enhanced the thermal stability of those petroleum-based coating systems and imparted measurable antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus aureus in both coating systems. CLPs also increased color change and gloss loss under UVB exposure, indicating their applicability as light-absorbing fillers. However, incorporating CLPs reduced the impact resistance of polyallophanate powder coatings, particularly at higher loadings. Overall, the results demonstrate that CLPs can impart new functional properties such as antibacterial behavior, while contributing to thermal reinforcement, highlighting their potential as bio-derived nano-additives for more sustainable and multifunctional powder-coating technologies.

Inhaled Fluorinated Polymer Triggers Pyroptosis for Lung Cancer Immunotherapy
leads.abstract: Lung cancer imposes the highest cancer-related mortality burden worldwide, while its responsiveness to immunotherapy is often constrained by the immunosuppressive pulmonary tumor microenvironment (TME) and tumor adaptations that buffer oxidative stress. Pyroptosis, a highly immunogenic form of programmed cell death that can be activated through mechanisms not strictly dependent on exogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS), offers a promising alternative for immune activation but remains challenging to induce effectively in vivo. Here, we report an inhalable fluorinated polymer nanoplatform (PFAP) that triggers mitochondrial dysfunction to initiate pyroptosis and thereby elicits potent antitumor immunity in the lung. PFAP integrates perfluoroalkyl segments with cationic domains to enhance interactions with mitochondrial membranes, while a detachable polyethylene glycol shell preserves nanoparticle stability during aerosolization and facilitates penetration of pulmonary barriers. Upon exposure to the acidic TME, PFAP restores membrane-disruptive activity, leading to mitochondrial depolarization, Cyto C release, caspase-3 activation, GSDME cleavage, and pyroptosis induction. In orthotopic and metastatic lung cancer models, inhaled PFAP achieves efficient lung delivery, elicits robust antitumor immunity, and suppresses tumor progression without detectable systemic toxicity. This work provides a nanomaterial-based approach for inducing pyroptosis in lung cancer and highlights the potential of inhalable polymer systems for localized cancer immunotherapy.

leads.title: Electrospun Graphene Oxide/Recycled Nylon 66 Nanofiber‐Reinforced Virgin Nylon 66 Composites: Recycling‐Driven Improvements in Strength and Thermal Stability
leads.abstract: Recycling nylon helps reduce plastic pollution, conserve energy and save fossil fuel. This study presents a recycling‐based approach for developing high‐performance composites by reinforcing a virgin Nylon 66 (N66) matrix with electrospun nanofiber mats fabricated from recycled Nylon 66 (RN66) cable ties containing 0.5–5 wt.% graphene oxide (GO). Compression‐molded composites with different nanofiber orientations were fabricated and characterized using FTIR, EDS, SEM, DSC, TGA, and ASTM‐standard mechanical testing. Among the investigated compositions, the cross‐ply composite containing 2 wt.% GO exhibited the highest overall mechanical performance, with 31.5% higher flexural strength, 82.7% higher Izod impact strength, and 90.4% higher Charpy impact strength than neat N66, while also showing improved ductility. The cross‐ply composite containing 5 wt.% GO demonstrated the highest compressive strength (98.5 MPa, 35.9% higher than neat N66) and enhanced thermal stability, with the degradation onset temperature increasing from 365°C for neat N66 to 398°C. These results show that GO‐reinforced recycled Nylon 66 nanofibers enhance mechanical and thermal performance while valorizing post‐industrial nylon waste, offering a promising platform for lightweight engineering applications.

leads.title: Design principles for vitrimers: Linking dynamic covalent chemistry, network architecture, and engineering performance
leads.abstract: Vitrimers are commonly classified according to the dynamic covalent bonds that enable network topology rearrangement, but their practical performance is governed by more than exchange chemistry alone. Molecular structure, network architecture, chain mobility, and exchange kinetics collectively determine whether a vitrimer can maintain mechanical stability during use while retaining sufficient mobility for processing, repair, and reprocessing. This review examines vitrimer design by considering how molecular and network structures influence material properties. Particular attention is given to how factors such as catalyst concentration, reactive‐group stoichiometry, backbone structure, cross‐link density, molecular ordering, junction mobility, and network heterogeneity influence glass‐transition behavior, modulus, creep resistance, stress relaxation, and property recovery. These relationships are then considered in the context of emerging engineering applications, where the balance between service stability and processability is often more important than maximizing exchange rate alone. By connecting molecular and network design with rheological behavior and macroscopic performance, this Review provides a framework for the rational design and evaluation of vitrimer materials.
leads.venue: Bulletin of the Korean Chemical Society

leads.title: Effect of Porosity on the Esterification Efficiency and Physicochemical Properties of Corn Starch
leads.abstract: Native starch (NS) has limited surface area and porosity, which restricts its performance in adsorption, encapsulation, and emulsification systems. We hypothesized that introducing porosity into starch granules would increase hydroxyl accessibility and enhance esterification efficiency, yielding amphiphilic derivatives with improved functional properties compared with NS. To test this hypothesis, native and porous corn starches were esterified with octanoyl chloride under mild alkaline conditions and characterized by 1 H NMR, FTIR, XRD, SEM, DSC, particle‐size analysis, zeta potential, oil absorption capacity (OAC), and enzymatic degradation. Quantitative 1 H NMR confirmed a higher degree of substitution (DS) for porous starch (DS = 0.038) than for NS (DS = 0.030), indicating enhanced reactivity toward esterification. SEM and XRD analyses showed that modification primarily occurred on the granule surface, while the crystalline structure was largely preserved, with a slight decrease in relative crystallinity (RC) after esterification. DSC analysis revealed a reduction in gelatinization enthalpy for all esterified samples, which was more pronounced in porous starch (PS), consistent with partial disruption of hydrogen bonding. Esterified PS (EPS) exhibited a greater decrease in zeta potential, as well as higher hydrophobicity, oil‐binding capacity, and enzymatic degradability than esterified NS (ENS). These findings demonstrate that starch porosity is an effective strategy for enhancing esterification efficiency and tailoring biodegradable starch derivatives with improved physicochemical and functional properties.

leads.title: Effect of carbon quantum dots on the UV-curing behavior and properties of waterborne polyurethane acrylate coatings
leads.abstract: Photoactive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are promising modifiers for waterborne polyurethane acrylate (WPUA) coatings, but their effect on UV-curing kinetics depends on how they interact with the photopolymerizable matrix. This study evaluates the influence of CQDs surface chemistry, photoluminescence quantum yield (QY), and incorporation route on curing behavior and final coating properties. Two CQDs with distinct QY values (≈23% and ≈62%) but similar surface functional groups were incorporated into WPUA dispersions via aqueous-phase addition and acetone pre-dispersion. Photo-DSC analysis revealed that CQDs broadened curing profiles, increased peak time from 4.2 s to 13.7–44.5 s, and reduced C=C conversion from 92.8% to 50.8–77.9%. A semi-quantitative analysis indicated that curing retardation arises from combined competitive UV absorption and route-dependent mobility restrictions induced by CQDs–WPUA interactions. Despite reduced conversion and gel content (97.8% to 83–93%), CQDs improved coating performance, increasing tensile strength from 4.3 MPa to 6.1–6.6 MPa (≈40–53%), and thermal stability (T 10% ) from 298.2 °C to 309.1 °C. The incorporation route affected curing and properties in a CQDs-dependent manner, while QY differences produced only minor kinetic effects, indicating that surface chemistry and matrix interactions govern the response more strongly than photoluminescence. Under air, selected formulations suggested an apparent attenuation of oxygen inhibition, consistent with auxiliary CQDs photoactivity. Hansen solubility parameter analysis further revealed a contraction of the solubility sphere, indicating a more constrained network with improved solvent resistance. CQDs act as multifunctional modifiers that tune curing efficiency and coating performance through surface functionality and incorporation route.

leads.title: Selective Laser Sintering of Bio-derived Furan-Polyester Polymer Nanocomposites with Engineered MXene-Based Tribo-interphases
Characteristics of conventional and alternative starch sources, extraction techniques and applications: A review
leads.abstract: The increasing environmental impact of synthetic plastics has intensified the search for sustainable alternatives, with bioplastics derived from renewable feedstock emerging as a promising option. Starch is a natural polymer widely distributed in plants, and it can be applied in diverse ways as a substitute for plastics, helping to reduce their environmental footprint. Conventional starch sources include corn, cassava, wheat, potato and rice, with starch contents of around 70%; however, their use in bioplastic production competes with the food supply chain. This review examines both conventional and alternative starch sources, particularly raw or waste materials with potential for valorisation, including chestnut, acorn, potato peel and sago pith waste. Although these materials generally contain lower starch levels (approximately 50%), they exhibit valuable functional properties. Various methods are available for starch extraction, and among the emerging technologies, enzymatic treatment, ultrasound- and microwave-assisted extraction, as well as pulsed electric fields, stand out as efficient and environmentally friendly options. The selection of the extraction method is critical, as it directly influences the physicochemical properties of starch and, consequently, its performance in final applications. While starch has certain limitations compared to synthetic polymers, its functionality can be improved for instance through blending with natural or synthetic polymers. Overall, starch obtained from alternative sources represents a viable and sustainable pathway to reduce dependence on conventional starch sources that compete for food supplies, as well as on petroleum-based plastics, while simultaneously promoting the valorisation of underutilised biomass and agro-industrial residues.

leads.title: Self-healing and degradable rosin-castor oil-based vitrimers containing ester bonds and disulfide bonds
Biosynthesis of citronellyl pentanoate with enhanced antifungal activity using lignin-based magnetic biocatalysts
leads.abstract: Terpenic esters are compounds of considerable industrial relevance that can be obtained through direct extraction or chemical synthesis. However, these conventional approaches present limitations, making biotechnological production a promising and sustainable alternative. In this study, it was investigated the biosynthesis of citronellyl pentanoate using lipase B from Candida antarctica (CALB) and lipase from Rhizomucor miehei (RML), either in soluble form or immobilized on magnetic cashew apple bagasse (CAB) lignin. After immobilization, the enzymes exhibited satisfactory activity (12.6 ± 0.7 U.g -1 for CALB; 13.1 ± 0.1 U.g -1 for RML) and high immobilization yields (71.5 ± 1.2% for CALB; and 79.9 ± 4.6% for RML). Biotransformation assays revealed that the optimal reaction conditions were 50 °C and a 1:1 alcohol-to-acid molar ratio, achieving conversion of citronellol above 90% within 24 h for immobilized lipases. The operational stability of the biocatalyst was evaluated over 10 reaction cycles of 24 h, verifying that the catalytic activity was maintained, with conversions above 80% at the last cycle. The citronellyl pentanoate attained chromatographic purity of 97.3% and its antimicrobial activity was evaluated. Against Staphylococcus aureus , inhibition zones were 15 mm for the ester and 19.5 mm for the citronellol, while against Escherichia coli they were 18.5 mm and 20 mm, respectively. The citronellyl pentanoate showed greater antifungal activity against Fusarium graminearum DSM 4528 than the precursor alcohol (IC 50 reduced by ~68%), while it presented less antibacterial activity effectiveness against Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000. These results highlight the selective bioactivity of terpenic esters and their potential as targeted antifungal agents. Overall, the synthesis of citronellyl pentanoate proved efficient, achieving high yields with promising biotechnological potential.

leads.title: Developing a new technique for enhanced processing of clay-based polyethylene nanocomposites to avoid and minimise defect and crack nucleation during manufacturing
leads.abstract: For the quality, homogeneity, interfacial bonding and defect avoidance of polyethylene nanocomposites reinforced with nanoclay (NC) layers (CPNCs), exfoliation and dispersion of the bonded NC layers represent critical controlling factors because NC particles readily agglomerate. Therefore, a novel dry–wet melt-blending method was developed for polymer nanocomposites reinforced with pre-exfoliated nano-layers produced using a high-shear process and stored in ice cubes to maintain the exfoliated nanolayers as separated layers ready for use. The study is based on fundamental experimental techniques designed to produce high-quality nanocomposites for different applications. Natural NC nanoparticles, montmorillonite (MMT) and Saudi halloysite nanotubes (SHNT), were used with specialised mixing and processing techniques. The developed technique minimised defects while enhancing the mechanical and fracture properties of the resulting materials, thereby producing high-quality materials with improved resistance to cracking and failure under loading. To avoid voids, inclusions, and other defects and achieve a homogeneous microstructure, the method incorporates fracture mechanics through consideration of the critical stress-intensity factor to control and prevent cracking by establishing a strong bi-interfacial bond between the exfoliated NC layers and polyethylene chains. Mechanical and fracture properties were examined using scanning electron microscopy (SEM), transmission electron microscope (TEM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), and X-ray diffraction (XRD) analyses, confirming the success of the new technique and achievement of the study objective.

leads.title: Molecular weight–dependent properties of ciprofloxacin-loaded chitosan films: An in-vitro comparative study toward localized drug delivery for wound healing
Thermally Responsive 3D Printed Polyester Networks
leads.abstract: Thermally responsive networks have been explored widely for drug delivery applications due to their ability to sequester or release payloads upon thermal triggering. Herein, we report a series of degradable, thermoresponsive polyesters synthesized via ring-opening copolymerization of succinic anhydride, an oligo(ethylene glycol)-derivatized epoxide, and allyl glycidyl ether, and used as resins for additive manufacturing. The oligomers were designed with lower critical solution temperatures such that below 10 °C, they are hydrophilic in aqueous solutions, and are hydrophobic near physiological temperature. Thermoresponsive polyester networks were fabricated via vat photopolymerization, with longer oligomers resulting in more crosslinks and therefore stiffer networks. When placed in water, substrates swelled at 4 °C, experiencing 2-fold volumetric and weight increases and decreased elongational moduli. When solutions were warmed to 37 °C, samples expelled water, recovering their dry properties. This work establishes the development of degradable, 3D printed networks with temperature-induced control over swelling, morphology, and mechanical properties.

leads.title: Bio-Based UV-Curable Resins Derived from Waste PET Glycolysis Products for LCD 3D Printing
leads.abstract: To facilitate the high-value upcycling of waste polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and the advancement of sustainable materials, a comprehensive strategy encompassing chemical recycling, functionalization, and upcycling was proposed. Initially, bis(2-hydroxyethyl) terephthalate (BHET) was derived via the glycolysis of waste PET with ethylene glycol, which subsequently served as a precursor for the synthesis of a series of bio-based polyester polyols (BPOs). These polyols, characterized by controllable branched structures, were synthesized through melt polycondensation of BHET and the bio-based platform molecule, citric acid (CA). Bio-based UV-curable resins (BUVRs) were fabricated by incorporating the BPOs into a polyurethane acrylate matrix, and the introduction of BPO significantly improved both the photocuring behavior and mechanical properties of the resulting materials. Specifically, the double-bond conversion of the resin containing 5 wt % BPO1 increased to 91.3%, representing a substantial improvement over the BPO-free control. Mechanical characterization further revealed that the tensile strength of the BUVR was nearly doubled, rising from 19.7 to 37.9 MPa with increasing BPO1 content. Furthermore, owing to their exceptional resistance to nonpolar solvents, the BUVRs were successfully utilized in LCD 3D printing to yield components characterized by high dimensional stability and precision. Consequently, this study establishes a low-carbon and efficient paradigm for the upcycling of waste PET and the fabrication of high-performance bio-based UV-curable resins.

leads.title: Mechanical performance of steel, basalt and polyamide fiber-reinforced ultra-high-performance concrete evaluated by experiments and SHAP-based machine learning
STRONG3 promotes lignin biosynthesis and culm strength in rice
leads.abstract: Summary Lodging severely reduces rice yield and quality. Culm strength, mainly determined by lignin biosynthesis and secondary cell wall (SCW) formation, is core to lodging resistance. We identified an ethylene response factor (ERF) transcription factor STRONG3 via genome‐wide association study (GWAS) of 405 rice accessions based on lignin content. Functional validation demonstrated that STRONG3 positively regulates lignin accumulation, culm diameter, and mechanical strength by promoting sclerenchyma tissue development, vascular bundle enlargement, and SCW thickening. Molecular analyses revealed that STRONG3 directly binds to the GCC‐box motif in the promoter of 4CL4 , a rate‐limiting enzyme in the phenylpropanoid pathway, to activate its transcription. Genetic complementation confirmed that 4CL4 acts downstream of STRONG3 to mediate lignin biosynthesis and culm development. Haplotype analysis identified subspecies‐specific favorable alleles: STRONG3 G in Geng rice, caused by a single nucleotide polymorphism (4349512) leading to an Ala289Thr substitution in the activation domain that enhances STRONG3's transcriptional activation of 4CL4 , and 4CL4 TC in Xian rice. Combinatorial analysis showed these alleles synergistically improve culm traits in their respective subspecies. Overexpression of STRONG3 enhanced lodging resistance without compromising grain yield. Our findings uncover a critical regulatory pathway for rice culm development and provide valuable genetic resources and molecular markers for breeding high‐yield, lodging‐resistant rice varieties.

leads.title: Chitosan film based piezoelectric nanogenerator for ambient energy harvesting
leads.abstract: Herein, we report a flexible chitosan-based piezoelectric nanogenerator (CPENG) fabricated using a simple and scalable solution-casting method from commercially available chitosan, an abundant and environmentally friendly biopolymer. The CPENG efficiently converts low-frequency mechanical stimuli into electrical energy through the piezoelectric response of the chitosan matrix. Under repeated finger tapping, the device produces an open-circuit voltage of ~ 18 V and a short-circuit current of ~ 1.0 µA. The device also shows good signal reproducibility and stable performance under repeated mechanical deformation. Furthermore, the CPENG can harvest energy from different ambient mechanical stimuli, producing electrical responses of ~ 1.6 V under finger touch, ~ 1.2-1.5 V under mechanical vibrations induced by human body movement, and ~ 200-380 mV under airflow. The practical energy-harvesting capability of the device is demonstrated by charging a 1 µF capacitor to ~ 2.3 V within 20 s and powering 13 light-emitting diodes without an external power source. The combination of flexibility, biodegradability, simple fabrication, and effective energy conversion highlights the potential of chitosan-based piezoelectric nanogenerators for sustainable energy harvesting, wearable electronics, and self-powered sensing applications.

leads.title: A Highly Proton-Tolerant Multicenter Borane/Phosphazene Catalytic System for Efficient PO/CO2 Copolymerization toward CO2-Based Poly(carbonate-ether) Polyols
leads.abstract: Low-molecular-weight CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols from ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) of propylene oxide (PO) with CO2 are highly desired as soft blocks to synthesize sustainable polyurethanes. However, such process remains great challenges because of the demanding of highly proton-tolerant catalysts. Herein, we report a binary organocatalysis system based on a nanoscopic multicenter borane Lewis acid (POSS-B8) combined with various organobases for the tunable ROCOP of PO and CO2. The confined POSS-B8 framework not only endows excellent tolerance to proton but enables cooperative activation of PO and CO2, thereby facilitating PO/CO2 ROCOP while effectively suppressing the formation of cyclic propene carbonate (cPC). Remarkably, the binary system can tolerate high loadings of chain-transfer agents (up to 400 equivalents), affording low-molecular-weight polycarbonate polyols (0.6 kDa) with narrow dispersity (Ð = 1.16). By tuning POSS-B8 loading and CO2 pressure, both the carbonate content (19-64 mol%) and glass transition temperature (-58.6 to 4.7 °C) of resulting polymers can be modulated. This metal-free and tunable platform offers a versatile strategy for the preparation of CO2-based poly(carbonate-ether) polyols with controlled structure and strong potential for industrial applications.

leads.title: Development of Lubricant Grease from Plastic Wastes for Possible Indusrial Application
leads.abstract: The increasing accumulation of polyethylene plastic waste poses a significant threat to the environment due to its non-biodegradable nature and widespread use in packaging and consumer products. With global concerns over plastic pollution and the urgent need for sustainable waste management solutions, this research proposes the formulation of lubricant grease from polyethylene waste. This made a low-value polyethylene plastic waste into high-value industrial product (lubricant). This involves subjecting shredded polyethylene waste via pyrolysis, producing low molecular weight hydrocarbon product pyro-wax by thermal decomposition, which was used as thickeners replacing metal soap in a conventional grease where 30% weight pyro-wax give a grease NLGI 4 standard value on consistency test 180mm penetration length. Other parameters analyze includes dropping point 118 oC, Oil separation 0.041%, Oil bleeding 0.013%, percentage sample wash-off 0.26%,Oxidation stability 1kPa after 1000hrs and corrosion free all performed using American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) standard and the result were within accepted limit of the ASTM standard Grease for bearings lubrication. The significance of this work demonstrates that polyethylene waste can be recycled into a functional lubricant product; these outcomes not only contribute to waste valorization efforts but also encourage innovation in the recycling and up-cycling sector, fostering greener production. It also contributes to circular economy efforts by transforming nuisance into useful engineering materials and also promoting a more sustainable industrial future.

leads.title: Suberinic Acids from Birch Outer Bark as a Renewable Feedstock for Polyurethane Polyols: Influence of Depolymerization Conditions on Structure and Reactivity
leads.abstract: Suberinic acids obtained from birch outer bark represent a promising renewable feedstock for bio-based polyols suitable for polyurethane applications. Their chemical structure and reactivity depend strongly on depolymerization conditions, reagent type, and moisture content. In this study, extracted birch outer bark was depolymerized using NaOH, KOH, and KOH followed by FeCl3 precipitation to selectively remove phenolic components. The resulting suberinic acid mixtures (SAM) were characterized by GC-FID, GC-MS and GPC, and subsequently converted into polyols via oxyalkylation with propylene carbonate. FeCl3-treated SAM produced polyols with the highest hydroxyl values (435 mg KOH/g), while NaOH-derived SAM yielded the lowest viscosity polyols (5361 mPa·s). KOH-derived SAM generated the most viscous polyols due to the presence of long-chain oxidized structures and oligomeric fragments. Moisture was identified as a critical parameter: undried SAM caused uncontrolled reaction acceleration and catalyst deactivation during oxyalkylation. The results provide mechanistic insight into how depolymerization chemistry shapes SAM composition and polyol performance, supporting the development of optimized bio-based polyurethane systems.

leads.title: From Lignin to Polyols: Combined Catalytic and Electrochemical Approach for Advanced Biomass Conversion
leads.abstract: Lignin is the largest renewable aromatic resource, yet its structural complexity limits its integration into chemical value chains. This work presents a combined catalytic and electrochemical strategy for converting technical lignins into functionalized oligomers and polyol precursors for polyurethane applications. Technical Kraft lignin was subjected to catalytic hydrogenolysis followed by controlled oxidation, reducing high-molecular-weight fractions and generating lower-molecular-weight oligomers with modified side-chain functionalities. Subsequent electrochemical upgrading in a two-compartment cell enabled targeted functionality tuning under mild conditions (20–60 °C). RuO2 electrodes promoted a-functionalization-assisted ß–O–4 cleavage, while Cu-based catalysts reduced aldehydes to al-cohols with faradaic efficiencies above 60%. Multidimensional NMR and quantitative ³¹P{¹H} NMR analyses revealed hydroxyl-rich oligomeric structures with aromatic and aliphatic functionalities relevant for polyurethane chemistry. The integrated catalytic–electrochemical route provides a modular pathway toward renewable aromatic polyols, lignin-derived resin precursors, and circular carbon value chains.

leads.title: Design and Development of a Bio-based Hybrid Polyurethane Foam for Sustainable Thermal Insulation Applications
leads.abstract: In the context of global efforts to reduce energy consumption in buildings, polyurethane insulation panels play a crucial role. The work focuses on replacing petroleum-derived components in conventional polyurethanes with bio-based alternatives sourced from lignocellulosic biomass. The developed material consists of a hybrid polyurethane foam in which conventional polyols are replaced with lignin-derived ones. A key innovative step is the incorporation of cellulose nanocrystals into the polyurethane matrix which acts as a multifunctional additive. Thermal constant characterization was conducted, accompanied by Scanning Electron Microscopy imaging analyses of cellulose nanocrystals. This methodological approach enabled a rigorous evaluation of the technical implications of lignin and cellulose nanocrystals utilization, providing a solid framework for interpreting differences in material behavior and assessing the feasibility of lignin as a functional component in advanced polyurethanes.

One‐step Synthesis of a Phosphaphenanthrene–Imidazole Phosphorus–Nitrogen Flame Retardant for Epoxy Thermosets: Degradation Pathway and Fire‐Safety Mechanism
leads.abstract: Epoxy resins (EPs) possess excellent mechanical strength, chemical resistance, and adhesion, yet their inherent flammability limits their use in fire‐sensitive applications. Under increasingly stringent safety requirements, developing simple and scalable halogen‐free flame retardants remains a significant challenge. In this work, a phosphorus–nitrogen flame retardant, 6‐(2‐(1H‐imidazol‐1‐yl)ethyl)dibenzo[c,e][1,2]oxaphosphinine 6‐oxide (DIM), was synthesized via a one‐step nucleophilic addition reaction between 9,10‐dihydro‐9‐oxa‐10‐phosphaphenanthrene‐10‐oxide (DOPO) and 1‐vinylimidazole (VIM), and subsequently incorporated into epoxy thermosets, either alone or in combination with melamine (MEL). Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) was used to evaluate the formation of DIM. The thermal degradation, fire performance, char structure, phosphorus retention, and evolved products of the resulting thermosets were investigated using thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), cone calorimetry, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), Raman spectroscopy, X‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP‐OES), TGA coupled with Fourier‐transform infrared spectroscopy (TG‐FTIR), and pyrolysis‐gas chromatography/mass spectrometry (Py‐GC/MS). Changes in the characteristic FTIR bands of the PH and vinyl groups, together with the retention of the DOPO and imidazole frameworks, supported the formation of the proposed addition product. Among the investigated formulations, EP/DIM‐MEL4 exhibited the greatest improvement in fire performance, with reductions of 31.9% and 36.0% in peak heat release rate and total heat release, respectively, relative to neat EP. Microscopic and spectroscopic analyses indicated the formation of a more expanded, continuous, and structurally ordered protective char. ICP‐OES analysis showed that approximately 31.1% of the initial phosphorus was recovered in the solid residue. TG‐FTIR and Py‐GC/MS further suggested that volatile phosphorus‐containing species contributed to gas‐phase radical inhibition, whereas nitrogen‐containing volatiles derived from the imidazole moiety and MEL contributed to flame‐zone dilution. Overall, the improved fire safety of the DIM‐containing epoxy thermosets is attributed to the combined effects of gas‐phase inhibition and condensed‐phase barrier formation. This work provides a simple strategy for developing DOPO‐based phosphorus–nitrogen flame‐retardant systems for epoxy thermosets.

Engineering multifunctional hybrid nanotubes toward fire-safe thermoplastic polyurethane nanocomposites with enhanced mechanical performance
leads.abstract: Developing thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) composites with superior flame retardancy, smoke suppression, and mechanical performance remains a significant challenge. In this work, multifunctional lanthanum/phosphorus-decorated, boron/nitrogen-doped graphitic nanotubes (La@P-BCN-GNTs, abbreviated as LPBN) were successfully fabricated and incorporated into TPU via melt blending. The introduction of phosphorus-containing groups and lanthanum species not only improved the interfacial compatibility between BCN nanotubes and the TPU matrix but also imparted intrinsic flame-retardant functionality. Owing to the synergistic effects of structural reinforcement, catalytic charring, and barrier protection, the TPU/LPBN composites exhibited significantly improved fire safety. At an LPBN loading of 15 wt%, the composite achieved a vertical burning (UL-94) V-0 rating and a limiting oxygen index (LOI) of 29.1%. Meanwhile, the peak heat release rate (pHRR), peak smoke production rate (PSPR), and total smoke production (TSP) were reduced by 65.5%, 60.5%, and 40.9%, respectively, compared with neat TPU. Notably, the composite exhibited a tensile strength of 28.2 MPa while maintaining excellent flame-retardant performance. The synergistic effects of catalytic carbonization, enhanced graphitization, and nanotube-reinforced barrier protection effectively suppressed heat and smoke release during combustion. This work presents a promising strategy for designing high fire-safety TPU composites by multifunctional hybrid nanofiller engineering.

leads.title: Microwave activation of cellulose nanocrystals surface hydroxyls drives ordered reconstruction toward 2D cellulose nanosheets.
leads.abstract: Since the discovery of cellulose nanosheets (CNSs), these two-dimensional (2D) nano-sized cellulose nanomaterials have demonstrated advantages in many applications such as barrier materials, reinforcing materials, and film materials, owing to their large lateral dimensions, thin sheet thickness, and continuous sheet-like structure. Although there is a certain structural correlation between CNSs and cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs), it still remains unclear whether CNCs can be directly assembled to obtain CNSs. Therefore, a nano-welding strategy based on microwave hydroxyl activation is proposed in this work, which realizes the reconstruction of 1D CNCs into 2D reconstructed CNSs (rCNSs) within a short reaction time of 15 min. The obtained 2D rCNSs possess sizes of several micrometers and possess structural origins and crystalline building units similar to those of naturally extracted CNSs. The results reveal that microwave treatment effectively activates the surface hydroxyl groups of CNCs, facilitates charge separation of hydroxyl groups, and increases interfacial dipole moment. Ordered hydrogen bond networks are induced via dipole interactions to further trigger the nano-welding, accomplishing the ordered reconstruction of 2D sheet structures. The O 2 and CO 2 barrier properties of the reconstructed lamellar rCNCs are 1.67 times and 1.12 times those of rod-like CNCs in the PBAT matrix, respectively. This work provides important theoretical support and technical routes for the controllable fabrication and functional application of high-performance 2D nanocellulose materials.
leads.authors: Yang J, Zhang Z, Zhang H, Xue R, Xu G, Na H, Zhu J.

leads.title: Organosolv lignin from corncob for developing Pickering emulsion: A comparative study of lignin nanoparticles and chitosan-coated lignin nanoparticles
leads.abstract: There is an increasing interest in the sustainable production of materials from lignocellulosic biomass due to the environmental concerns associated with non-renewable fossil resources. Lignin, an abundant biopolymer, has attracted attention for the preparation of nanoparticles with potential applications in emulsion stabilization. In this work, organosolv lignin obtained from corncob was used to produce lignin nanoparticles (LNPs) and chitosan-coated lignin nanoparticles (chi-LNPs). LNPs were produced at lignin concentrations of 0.39 mg/mL and 3.3 mg/mL, resulting in colloidal dispersions with relatively narrow size distributions and low polydispersity index (PDI). Coating with chitosan greatly impacted the LNPs’ charge, size and PDI, increased the contact angle, but did not significantly affect surface tension. Both nanoparticle systems were subsequently evaluated as Pickering emulsion stabilizers using different oil-in-water- ratios. The results showed that both systems were effective in stabilizing the emulsions, while chi-LNPs generally produced smaller median droplet sizes, particularly at intermediate and high nanoparticle concentrations. However, no consistent trend was observed for the distribution width. Overall, these findings suggest that chitosan coating can improve the emulsifying performance of LNPs under specific formulation conditions and support the use of surface-modified LNPs as bio-based stabilizers for Pickering emulsions.

leads.title: Controlled Ring-Opening Polymerization of 5-Phenyl-1,4-dioxan-2-one toward Stereochemically Tunable and Closed-Loop Recyclable Polyesters
leads.abstract: The practical applications of closed-loop recyclable polymers demand monomers that are readily accessible from simple feedstocks while enabling controlled polymerization and tunable physical properties. Herein, we report a one-pot synthesis of 5-phenyl-1,4-dioxan-2-one (PhDO) from methyl glycolate and styrene oxide via acid-catalyzed epoxide ring opening followed by intramolecular cyclization. The H2SO4-catalyzed route afforded pure PhDO in 62% isolated yield. At –40 °C and [M]0 = 2.0 M, MeAl[salen] (Al-1) enabled controlled ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of PhDO, affording poly(5-phenyl-1,4-dioxan-2-one) (PPhDO) with number-average molecular weights (Mn) up to 81.1 kDa and narrow dispersity. Polymerization of PhDO monomers with different enantiomeric compositions provided PPhDO samples with stereostructures ranging from essentially atactic to isotactic. Individual PPhDO samples were amorphous, whereas the complementary enantiomeric polymers formed a crystalline phase with a melting temperature of 141.6 °C and an estimated WAXS crystallinity of 72.3%, consistent with stereocomplexation. A representative high-molecular-weight P(rac-PhDO) showed appreciable tensile strength and moderate ductility. Importantly, P(rac-PhDO) underwent catalytic bulk depolymerization to regenerate rac-PhDO in 83% isolated yield. Together, these results establish a PhDO-based route to phenyl-substituted, closed-loop recyclable polyesters that integrates accessible monomer synthesis, controlled ROP, stereochemical transfer, stereocomplexation behavior, and catalytic monomer recovery.

leads.title: Investigating Topological Parameters in Polymers: Precision Synthesis of Trefoil Polymers from a Knotted Synthon
Synthesis of a castor oil-based polyurethane modifier: effects of isocyanate index and content on the thermo-oxidative aging behaviour of asphalt
leads.abstract: Castor oil-based polyurethane (COPU) has emerged as a promising bio-based modifier for asphalt, offering potential to reduce reliance on conventional petroleum-derived modifiers; however, its thermo-oxidative aging behaviour remains unclear. In this study, COPU was synthesised from castor oil and 2,4-toluene diisocyanate and used to prepare modified asphalts with different isocyanate indices (0.8-1.2) and COPU contents (3-5 wt%). FTIR, fluorescence microscopy, AFM, and rheological tests were used to evaluate chemical, microstructural, and performance evolution before and after aging. The results show that COPU formed a distinct dispersed phase in asphalt, while thermo-oxidative aging promoted microphase coalescence, reduced surface roughness, and altered the carbonyl- and sulfoxide-related absorption regions. Compared with base asphalt, COPU-modified asphalt exhibited higher strain recovery, lower irrecoverable creep compliance and creep stiffness, and improved high- and low-temperature rheological performance. After long-term aging, the rutting factor of COPU-modified asphalt was approximately 38.4%–131.2% higher than that of base asphalt over the investigated temperature range. Meanwhile, the creep stiffness was reduced by approximately 31.4%–48.5% at −12°C and 33.0%–48.8% at −18°C. An isocyanate index of 1.0 and a COPU content of 4 wt% are recommended. These findings support the formulation and application of durable bio-based asphalt materials.

leads.title: A review of natural fiber and agricultural waste fiber-based bio-composites used in building construction
leads.abstract: Bio-composites are emerging as viable alternatives to conventional building materials owing to their renewable origin, environmental benefits, and potential to reduce the carbon footprint of the construction sector. Comprising natural fibers embedded within polymer matrices, these materials have attracted considerable attention within the building industry for their capacity to mitigate environmental impact while offering functional alternatives to conventional synthetic materials. This review provides a comprehensive examination of the various classes of bio-composites, their applications in building construction, mechanical properties, manufacturing processes, associated advantages and limitations, and prospects for future development. Natural and agricultural fibers such as jute, hemp, flax, sisal, bamboo, rice husk, wheat straw, and coconut coir, combined with matrices including corn starch, arrowroot, polyethylene, polypropylene, polylactic acid, and bio-based epoxy resin, are evaluated in terms of their structural and functional performance. Particular attention is given to recent advances in bio-composite fabrication, including the incorporation of novel binder systems, hybrid fiber reinforcements, and chemical surface treatments aimed at enhancing mechanical and thermal performance. The environmental benefits of bio-composites are also discussed, including reduced greenhouse gas emissions, improved energy efficiency, and minimized construction waste, all of which align with the objectives of green building standards and sustainable construction practices. Nevertheless, several challenges continue to impede widespread adoption, including moisture sensitivity, variability in raw material properties, insufficient long-term performance data, and the absence of standardized testing protocols. The significant potential of bio-composites to advance sustainable construction practices, offering a practical pathway toward reducing the environmental footprint of the built environment.

leads.title: BRCA Mutation Carriers and Breast Implant-Associated Anaplastic Large-Cell Lymphoma: Accumulating Evidence, Proposed Mechanism, and Implications for Reconstructive Planning and Follow-Up.
leads.abstract: Background Breast implant-associated anaplastic large-cell lymphoma (BIA-ALCL) is an uncommon cluster of differentiation (CD)-30-positive T-cell lymphoma arising in the peri-implant capsule that was recognized as a definitive entity by the World Health Organization (WHO) in its 2022 fifth edition. Although historically framed as a device complication of textured implant surfaces, recent evidence suggests that germline mutations in BRCA1, BRCA2, and TP53 confer independent host-level susceptibility. These findings have yet to be synthesized for the surgical oncology audience. Methods This was a narrative review adhering to Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria. PubMed and MEDLINE were searched from January 2000 through March 2026. Evidence was ranked using the 2011 Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine levels of evidence. Discussion Four evidence streams spanning 15 years have consistently associated germline BRCA1/2 and TP53 mutations with elevated BIA-ALCL risk. The 2025 Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center prospective cohort reported a 16-fold increased age-adjusted risk in BRCA1/2 carriers (95% confidence interval 3.6-76.1). Compressed disease latency has been observed in mutation carriers. Overall, these reports suggest a gene-environment interaction model where impaired homologous recombination repair lowers the threshold for clonal T-lymphocyte expansion in the chronic inflammatory peri-implant microenvironment. Autologous reconstruction eliminates the BIA-ALCL risk. Thus, both autologous and smooth implant-based reconstruction should be explicitly discussed with BRCA carriers, and textured devices should be avoided if implant-based reconstruction is chosen. Surveillance strategies, including explicit documentation, earlier investigation thresholds, and structured long-term handoff, are recommended. Conclusions The evidence is observational and not yet sufficient for prescriptive guidelines but is consistent, biologically coherent, and of sufficient magnitude to warrant a measured adjustment in reconstructive counseling, implant selection, and follow-up in BRCA mutation carriers.

leads.title: A Dual-Tier RFID Architecture for Mold Lifecycle and Production Control in Polyurethane Manufacturing: A Simulation-Based Evaluation
leads.abstract: In polyurethane (PU) casting lines, precise tracking of mold lifecycles governs both product quality and planning efficiency. Manual monitoring produces systematic count discrepancies and offers no mechanism to prevent overproduction or the continued use of structurally expired molds. This study proposes a dual-tier radio frequency identification (RFID) architecture in which a work-order execution tier bounds output by the planned quota while a lifecycle tier tracks each mold against a structural limit of 600 passes. Validating a pass requires the elapsed curing interval to fall inside a calibrated time gate and the accumulated count to remain below the quota. Because full-scale deployment is capital-intensive and disruptive to a continuous line, the architecture is evaluated ex ante through a stochastic discrete-event simulation of a ten-line, 120-mold casting shop, benchmarked against the incumbent manual policy over 25 replications. The simulation reveals a result not evident from the specification alone: time-gated validation on strict two-reader pairing attains only 90.26% (±0.07) mold-level pass-count accuracy at realistic on-metal detection probabilities, below the manual baseline of 93.52% (±0.04), because single-sided read losses are discarded as exceptions. Adding a finite-state recovery layer that reconstructs single-sided detections raises accuracy to 98.06% (±0.03) and holds it above 96% even at a per-reader detection probability of 0.90. Over a 120-day horizon the recovered architecture reduces expired-mold exposure by 59.3%, defects from expired molds by 75.7%, overproduction by 78.9% and planning labour by 90.4%. Sensitivity analysis further requires oven residence-time standard deviation to be held below approximately 1.0 min.
leads.venue: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

leads.title: From Industrial lignin biomass waste to bio-based organic semiconductors for sustainable electronics: a proof of concept based on Vanillin
leads.abstract: Developing sustainable, bio-based organic semiconductors from renewable aromatic feedstocks opens new possibilities for sustainable electronics. Here, the present work uses vanillin as a sustainable aromatic platform extracted from industrial lignin biomass waste, which is chemically transformed into a π-conjugated semiconductor. The resulting donor–acceptor–donor molecule, IsoInd-CO-diCzBu, combines reversible redox activity with high thermal stability. Complementary space-charge-limited current measurements and organic field-effect transistors successfully demonstrate hole transport in vertical devices and p-type field-effect operation. An indepth study combining gate-bias stress, thermal annealing, and single-crystal X-ray diffraction connects device behaviour with molecular structure. These encouraging results establish vanillin as a platform for developing a series of bio-based semiconductors whose molecular architecture can be tuned to improve charge transport.

leads.title: The Potential of Marine Yeast and Its Interaction with Mold in Degrading High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE)
leads.abstract: Indonesia is one of the countries that contributes significant amounts of plastic waste to coastal environments. High-density polyethylene (HDPE) is a petroleum-based synthetic thermoplastic and the primary source of environmental plastic pollution. The stable aliphatic chains with strong C–C bonds in HDPE render it recalcitrant to microbial degradation. Bioremediation through biodegradation by microorganisms can be an effective and environmentally friendly solution for eliminating HDPE from ecosystems. Several studies have suggested that microbial consortia may enhance plastic biodegradation. However, the effectiveness of marine yeast-mold interactions in HDPE degradation remains poorly understood. This study aimed to evaluate the potential of marine yeast to degrade HDPE and assess its effectiveness when combined with molds for HDPE degradation. The biodegradation experiment was conducted over 30 days using Mineral Salt Medium Broth (MSMB) and plastic sheets. The parameters assessed during biodegradation included degradation effectiveness (%), total count of heterotrophic microorganisms (CFU/mL), and Scanning Electron Microscope (SEM) analysis. The results show that marine yeast has the potential to be used alone or in combination with molds. The highest value was achieved by the P2 treatment group in week 4, which consisted of a consortium of marine yeast and mold, with a value of 4.855%. However, this was not significantly different from P1, which consisted of a consortium of marine yeast with a value of 4.17%. The SEM test results indicated biofilm formation in all treatments, suggesting plastic biodegradation activity.
leads.venue: Indonesian Journal of Environmental Management and Sustainability

leads.title: Production, Optimization and Characterization of Biobased Itaconic Acid from Saccharomyces cerevisiae
leads.abstract: Itaconic acid (IA) is an important bio-based platform chemical with applications in the production of polymers, coatings, resins, and other value-added materials. However, its conventional microbial production relies predominantly on microorganisms that present safety and process-related limitations. This study investigated Saccharomyces cerevisiae BY4742 as a potentially safer microbial platform for the production of bio-based IA under submerged fermentation conditions. IA production was optimized using response surface methodology with a Box–Behnken design, considering glucose concentration, initial pH, and CaCI2 concentration as independent variables. The maximum IA concentration of 1133.50 ± 54.92 mg/L was obtained at 30 °C, pH 4.5, with 10% (w/v) glucose and without CaCI2 supplementation after 216 h of fermentation. The fermentation-derived IA was subsequently recovered and characterized using high-performance liquid chromatography, Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy, 1H-nuclear magnetic resonance (1H-NMR), and thermogravimetric analysis. The analytical results confirmed the molecular identity and high chromatographic purity of the recovered IA. Furthermore, the homopolymerization ability of the fermentation-derived IA was evaluated and compared with that of commercial IA under the same reaction conditions. The 1H-NMR results demonstrated changes consistent with consumption of the IA C=C double bond following polymerization, indicating that the fermentation-derived IA retained its ability to undergo homopolymerization. Overall, these findings demonstrate the potential of S. cerevisiae for producing structurally confirmed bio-based IA and provide a proof of concept for its use as a renewable monomer for poly(itaconic acid) synthesis, supporting its further investigation for the development of bio-based polymeric materials.
leads.authors: Velioglu Tosuner, Kosaca, Ozturk Urek et al.

leads.title: Plasma-Assisted and Green Routes to Silicon and Carbon Quantum Dots: A Critical Comparison of Synthesis–Structure–Property Relationships
leads.abstract: Silicon quantum dots (SiQDs) and carbon quantum dots (CQDs) are often discussed as related heavy-metal-free luminescent nanomaterials, although the mechanisms governing their formation and emission differ fundamentally. Rather than combining two parallel bodies of literature, this review uses SiQDs and CQDs as contrasting model systems to determine which synthesis-structure-property relationships are transferable and which remain material-specific. We critically compare nonthermal gas-phase plasma, plasma-liquid, and solution-phase synthesis, including green routes, with respect to precursor activation, nucleation and growth, crystallinity, surface chemistry, purification, photoluminescence, reproducibility, and scalability. Low-pressure continuous-flow radio-frequency capacitively coupled plasma (RF-CCP) is treated as the reference plasma architecture for free-standing Si nanocrystals, while atmospheric-pressure and plasma-liquid approaches are discussed according to their distinct product forms, formation mechanisms, and technological maturity. For crystalline SiQDs, quantum confinement provides a physically defined framework for interpreting size-dependent optical behavior, although oxidation, ligands, and interfacial defects remain critical. In CQDs, emission may arise from carbon-core states, surface or defect states, and molecular fluorophores, making structural assignment and fraction-resolved characterization essential. Across both material families, reported record photoluminescence efficiencies are less informative for technological translation than reproducibility, purified product yield, long-term stability, and application-specific performance. Hybrid plasma-liquid processing, operando diagnostics, standardized optical characterization, and data-guided process optimization are identified as promising directions toward scalable and reproducible quantum-dot manufacturing.

leads.title: Functional, next-generation, polymeric materials for targeted and controlled drug delivery applications
leads.abstract: Despite their broad clinical use, conventional drug delivery technologies are still limited by inadequate bioavailability, non-specific biodistribution, and uncontrolled drug release, which compromise therapeutic efficacy and safety. With their customizable molecular architecture, physicochemical adaptability, and multifunctional, stimuli-responsive design, next-generation polymeric materials overcome these constraints and allow for precise, site-specific, and regulated therapeutic action. In addition to stimuli-responsive platforms and structurally diverse nanocarriers such as nanoparticles, micelles, dendrimers, polymerases, and nanogels, this review critically examines the molecular and physicochemical design principles, nanoengineering and fabrication strategies, such as self-assembly, microfluidics, and emerging 3D/4D printing. Moreover, the passive, active, and organelle-level targeting mechanisms that govern these systems. In addition to clinical translation challenges, existing research gaps, and emerging directions like sustainable polymer chemistry, AI-driven design, adaptive 4D-printed systems, and personalized therapeutics, their disease-specific applications in cancer, neurological, cardiovascular, and infectious diseases, chronic wound healing, and regenerative medicine are critically evaluated. When taken as a whole, next-generation polymeric materials provide a flexible, clinically translatable platform for accurate, effective, and safe therapeutic intervention. However, they also highlight the crucial issues that need to be addressed in order to expedite clinical translation.
