Green Extraction of Lignin From Date Palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.) Seed Waste and Its Integration Into Alginate‐Based Films With Improved Moisture Resistance, Antioxidant Capacity, and Surface Hydrophobicity for Food Packaging Applications
leads.abstract: The aim of the current study was to extract lignin‐rich fraction from date palm ( Phoenix dactylifera L.) seeds and evaluate its application as a filler in sodium alginate‐based films for food packaging applications. Lignin was isolated through a sonication‐assisted mild alkaline hydrolytic process followed by acid precipitation. The isolated lignin was then characterized by using FTIR, XRD, SEM, and DSC analysis. FTIR analysis confirmed the presence of characteristic hydroxyl and aromatic functional groups associated with lignin. XRD analysis showed a low‐crystallinity with a broad diffraction region linked with amorphous lignin. SEM analysis showed an irregular and porous morphology. DSC demonstrated favorable thermal behavior. Sodium alginate and lignin films were developed by adding lignin into the sodium alginate matrix at various concentrations by using the solution casting method. The light transmittance and water vapor transmission rate decreased with the addition of lignin. The haze value and antioxidant activity of the films increased with the increase in lignin concentration and improved the light‐blocking ability. However, incorporating lignin did not significantly modify the mechanical properties of the films. The sample with the highest lignin concentration showed improved surface hydrophobic properties. These findings suggest that the date seed‐derived lignin could be a suitable candidate for food packaging applications.

leads.title: Accelerated Thermo‐Oxidative Aging and Shelf‐Life Prediction of PBAT / PGA / CaCO 3 Biodegradable Plastic Bags Based on Arrhenius Model
leads.abstract: With the great demand for plastic bags and the focus on microplastic pollution, biodegradable composites have become an excellent alternative approach. This study aimed to investigate the degradation behavior and predict shelf‐life of poly (butylene adipate‐co‐terephthalate) (PBAT)/Poly (glycolic acid) (PGA)/mineral powder (MD) plastic bags using thermo‐oxidative accelerated aging tests combined with the Arrhenius model. First, the effects of CaCO 3 content (5–15 wt%) on film‐blowing processability, surface microstructure, chemical structure, thermal properties, and key mechanical performance (tensile strength, elongation at break, tear strength) were systematically characterized. Results showed that an appropriate amount of CaCO 3 (≤ 10 wt%) acted as nucleating agents to promote polymer crystallization and neutralize acidic by‐products from hydrolysis, thereby extending the shelf‐life. However, an increased CaCO 3 content (15 wt%) caused agglomeration, weakened interfacial compatibility, and accelerated mechanical degradation. FTIR analysis confirmed that ester group hydrolysis was the primary aging mechanism. Based on the Arrhenius model, all formulations retained 50% of their original mechanical properties for over 2 years at 25°C, with the PBAT/PGA/10MD composite exhibiting the longest shelf‐life (> 3.4 years), which would be sufficient to meet the practical application requirements. This work provides a theoretical basis and technical support for the commercialization of biodegradable plastic bags.

leads.title: Cyclic Processability of Functional Liquid Crystalline Epoxy Networks via Dynamic Ester Bonding
leads.abstract: Lightly crosslinked liquid crystal epoxy networks (LCENs) possess stimuli responsive shape memory behavior, making them attractive materials for sensors and actuators. However, as a thermoset epoxy, there remain significant challenges in recyclability, repairability, and processability, especially relevant for typical LCENs, which are expensive and nonbiodegradable. Herein we demonstrate the repeatable, cyclic reprocessability of a catalyzed shape‐memory liquid crystal system via dynamic covalent bonding over two distinct modes of recycling, specifically as a proof‐of‐concept for the retaining of functional properties. The introduction of dynamic ester bonding to the system enables reprocessing techniques such as repair of clean fractures and reconstitution from shredded LCEN. The recycled LCEN shows retention of shape memory behavior across several cycles of reprocessing. This work demonstrates that dynamic bonding opens the door to the synthesis of recyclable functional epoxies and serves as a starting point for sustainable epoxy designs making use of bio‐derived, repairable, dynamically‐bonded systems.

leads.title: Motif‐Selective DNA Recognition and Promoter‐Dependent Transcriptional Repression by a Cyclic Pyrrole/Lysine Polyamide
leads.abstract: Sequence‐selective control of gene expression by synthetic DNA‐binding molecules is attractive for developing chemical biology tools and potential therapeutic applications. Here we report a cyclic pyrrole/lysine polyamide (cPKP) that preferentially binds AT‐rich DNA, with selective recognition of ATAT and ATGT motifs. In a HeLa nuclear extract‐based transcription system, cPKP repressed transcription in a promoter‐dependent manner, showing stronger inhibition of a cytomegalovirus (CMV) core promoter than of the human c‐ MYC promoter. RNA sequencing showed that cPKP was associated with downregulation of genes whose proximal promoters were enriched for ATAT and ATGT motifs, while causing limited perturbation of global cellular homeostasis in HeLa cells. Together, these results establish cPKP as a motif‐selective DNA‐binding scaffold that can modulate transcription in a promoter‐dependent manner with limited global transcriptomic perturbation in human cells.

leads.title: Engineering Multifunctional Polymer‐Based Electrospun Nanofibers for Sustainable Environmental Remediation and Biomedical Technologies
leads.abstract: Electrospun nanofibers based on advanced polymers have emerged as versatile materials with significant promise in environmental and biomedical domains. With an emphasis on catalytic wastewater treatment and biomedical systems, this study provides a thorough analysis of the design concepts, functionalization techniques, and real‐world uses of bio‐polymer‐based electrospun nanofibers. The use of biodegradable and sustainable polymers, such as chitosan, gelatin, cellulose, and polylactic acid (PLA), which have special physicochemical qualities including biocompatibility and high surface area, is emphasized. Their catalytic and therapeutic activity is improved when functional nanomaterials, such as metal nanoparticles, metal oxides, and enzymes, are incorporated into a nanofibrous matrix. These functionalized nanofibers show excellent efficacy in microbial inactivation, biofouling resistance, and pollutant degradation in wastewater treatment. Because of their advantageous biological interactions and adaptable architectures, they are used in biomedical applications for antibacterial activity, wound healing, medication delivery, and tissue engineering. The review also discusses surface modification methods, fabrication difficulties, and the requirement for environmentally sustainable, scalable production. The subject of multifunctional nanofibrous systems for sustainable and health‐oriented applications is further advanced by highlighting current limitations and offering insights into potential future advancements that could bridge lab research and practical implementation.

leads.title: Lignin blending modulates laccase-catalyzed polymerization of lignosulfonates using organosolv lignin from vine shoots
leads.abstract: Laccase-catalyzed repolymerization of technical lignins is an emerging biocatalytic strategy for upgrading lignin streams into polymeric systems and biomaterial precursors under mild reaction conditions. Lignosulfonates are attractive substrates for enzymatic polymerization due to their high water-solubility; however, their relatively low reactivity can limit their application. In contrast, organosolv lignin typically presents low-molecular weight and high phenolic content, which increase its susceptibility to laccase-mediated oxidation; however, its limited water solubility restricts enzymatic processing. In this work, lignin blending was evaluated as a strategy to modulate laccase-catalyzed polymerization by combining lignosulfonates (LS) with organosolv lignin from vine shoots (LVS). The effect of LVS incorporation on enzymatic oxidation was investigated through oxygen consumption measurements, viscosity evolution, molecular weight analysis and characterization of LS-based films. The presence of LVS modified oxidation kinetics, leading to prolonged oxidative activity, accelerated viscosity development and higher apparent molecular weight fractions at shorter reaction times compared to LS alone. LS-LVS films were produced to evaluate whether blending affected material surface properties. FTIR analysis supported structural changes consistent with oxidative coupling, while water contact angle measurements showed increased surface hydrophobicity in LS/LVS systems. Overall, the results demonstrate that blending lignins with different structural features can modulate enzymatic polymerization and influence the properties of LS films. This work highlights lignin blending as a simple biocatalytic strategy to modulate laccase-catalyzed polymerization and upgrade heterogeneous lignin streams toward lignin-based biomaterials within biorefinery concepts.

leads.title: Cellulose-based bioplastics for a circular bioeconomy: Properties, applications, market potential, consumer acceptance, and future perspectives
leads.abstract: Cellulose-based bioplastics have emerged as a promising alternative to conventional petroleum-derived plastics, offering a sustainable and eco-friendly solution to the growing environmental concerns associated with plastic waste. Derived from renewable resources such as wood, cotton, and agricultural residues, cellulose bioplastics exhibit biodegradability, biocompatibility, and low environmental impact. Despite their potential, several challenges impede their widespread adoption. Key challenges include the inherent hydrophilicity of cellulose, which affects the mechanical and barrier properties of the bioplastics, and the complex, energy-intensive extraction and processing methods required to convert cellulose into usable forms. Additionally, achieving the desired thermal and mechanical properties for various applications often necessitates the use of additives or blending with other biopolymers, which can complicate the production process and affect biodegradability. Future prospects for cellulose-based bioplastics hinge on advancements in materials science and processing technologies. Innovative approaches such as chemical modifications, nanocellulose reinforcement, and the development of novel cellulose derivatives are being explored to enhance the performance characteristics of cellulose bioplastics. Furthermore, integrating green chemistry principles and improving the scalability of production processes are critical for reducing costs and environmental footprint. Research into the lifecycle assessment and end-of-life scenarios of these bioplastics is essential to ensure their sustainability credentials. Incentivizing research and development, coupled with supportive regulatory frameworks, can accelerate the transition towards cellulose-based bioplastics. Ultimately, these materials hold significant potential to contribute to a circular economy by reducing reliance on fossil fuels, lowering greenhouse gas emissions, and minimizing plastic pollution. The journey towards fully realizing this potential is ongoing, necessitating continuous innovation and commitment to sustainable practices.

leads.title: Surface-functionalized niosomes using a folic acid-chitosan conjugate for delivery of capecitabine in breast cancer: In vitro and in vivo characterization.
leads.abstract: In this study, capecitabine (CAP) niosomes were prepared using the thin-film hydration method with Span 60 and cholesterol as key excipients and the formulation was optimized using a 3 2 factorial design. The synthesized folic acid-chitosan (FA-CS) conjugate was used to functionalize the niosome surface. An optimized formulation, after preliminary evaluation, was characterized for compatibility, XRD, NMR, in vitro drug release, cytotoxicity and cellular uptake, and in vivo bioavailability. Optimized niosomes achieved a particle size (PS) of 241.8 nm, a zeta potential of -22.9 mV, and an entrapment efficiency of 93.05%. After FA-CS functionalization, the PS increased to 272.9 nm, and the zeta potential shifted to 14 mV. FA-CS functionalized niosomes presented sustained drug release, attaining 86.31% cumulative drug release of CAP over 24 h. Successful CAP loading and FA-CS functionalization were confirmed by FTIR, XRD and NMR analysis, revealing significant crystalline changes. MTT assay showed 3.24- and 1.24-fold greater cytotoxicity than CAP and CAP niosomes, respectively, whereas cellular uptake increased 1.77-fold with FA-CS functionalized CAP niosomes, representing effective drug delivery. The in vivo bioavailability study of FA-CS functionalized niosomes showed a 3.18-fold increased C max and an 11.63-fold increase in AUC of CAP. Minimal changes in PS and maintained entrapment efficiency, along with Zeta potential, PDI and drug content during the stability study indicated the formulation's stability. In conclusion, enhanced cellular uptake and sustained delivery of CAP in cancer therapy were achieved using FA-CS functionalized niosomes, which displayed favourable physicochemical properties, effective drug release and enhanced effectiveness.
leads.authors: Sabale V, Pathak R, Ingole A, Sabale P.

leads.title: Sustainable composites derived from functionalized vegetable oil reinforced with waste fish scales
leads.abstract: Fish scales (FS), a major byproduct of the fish processing industry, are frequently discarded into the environment, affecting landfills and posing a threat to aquatic ecosystems. The present study aimed to minimize this waste by transforming it into value-added composite materials. In this study, biocomposites were fabricated using waste fish scales as the reinforcing filler, modified soybean oil (MAESO resin) as the matrix, and itaconic acid-glycidyl methacrylate adduct as the reactive diluent. The chemical structures of the resin and diluent were characterized using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) analyses. Composites with resin-to-filler ratios of 50:50, 60:40, and 70:30 were fabricated and comparatively evaluated. The results demonstrated that composite performance is strongly dependent on composition. The 60:40 composition exhibited a balanced combination of properties, with a tensile strength of 3.59 MPa, elongation at break (%) of 13.34 and shore D value of 72 indicating improved interfacial compatibility and surface characteristics. In contrast, the 50:50 composite showed the highest flexural strength (9.81 MPa), impact strength (47.31 J/m), attributed to increased filler content enhancing energy absorption capacity. However, excessive filler loading led to reduced dispersion and interfacial bonding as observed in SEM analysis. Thermogravimetric analysis further revealed increased char residue (48%) due to the presence of hydroxyapatite, contributing to improved thermal behavior. Overall, this study demonstrates the sustainable approach of converting fish scale waste into value added composite materials, highlighting the importance of composite optimization in tailoring specific properties.

leads.title: Self-healing kinetics and degradation assessment in vitrimers using an isoconversional methodology
leads.abstract: The ability of polymeric materials to autonomously repair damage has emerged as a key strategy to enhance durability and service lifetime in structural applications. In this framework, the self-healing capability of vitrimers positions them as a promising alternative to conventional thermosets. However, self-healing typically requires elevated temperatures at which significant degradation may occur. Consequently, the lack of a standardized methodology to experimentally characterize its kinetics remains a major barrier to defining safe reprocessing windows that minimize degradation effects. This work introduces a rheology-based approach to quantify self-healing in vitrimers. The time evolution of healing is extracted from the increase in an apparent storage modulus obtained during oscillatory tests, as two vitrimer surfaces are brought into contact and progressively weld to form a fully bonded interface. This methodology is complemented by an isoconversional kinetic analysis of a series of isothermal experiments, from which kinetic parameters are determined. A biobased epoxy vitrimer incorporating dynamic imine and disulfide bonds into the network is used as a model system. The analysis reveals an apparent activation energy that increases with the degree of healing, from 145 to 180 kJ mol⁻¹ at full recovery. Comparison with kinetic parameters obtained from stress relaxation experiments shows that both processes exhibit markedly different kinetics, underscoring the need for dedicated self-healing characterization methods. Finally, a kinetic analysis of degradation enables construction of a time–temperature–transformation diagram integrating self-healing and stress relaxation, providing a practical tool to identify safe reprocessing windows.

leads.title: Poly(2-oxazoline)- and Poly(2-oxazine)-Based Formulation Library Reveals Limits of Solubility Parameter-Based Drug-Polymer Compatibility Prediction
leads.abstract: Four structurally related poly(2-oxazoline) (POx)- and poly(2-oxazine) (POzi)-based ABA triblock copolymers were evaluated across 21 poorly water-soluble drugs to assess whether Hansen solubility parameters (HSPs) predict polymer-specific formulation performance. HSPs were calculated using Hoftyzer-Van Krevelen (HnV) and Yamamoto molecular break (YMB) methods, with semi-empirical polymer HSPs derived from solvent−solubility profiles. The polymers showed drug-specific performance, with maximum loading capacities exceeding 40 wt % for four drugs and 30 wt % for another four drugs. However, Ra showed limited discriminatory power. Among 20 drugs with YMB-derived Ra values, the lowest-Ra polymer was experimentally best for only 4 (20%), while Ra-based and experimental within-drug pairwise rankings agreed in 59 of 119 comparisons (49.6%). Significant cross-drug correlations for two polymers were positive, opposite to the expected trend. Despite this limited predictive performance, the resulting formulation library provides a broad experimental platform for identifying polymer-drug combinations for subsequent application-specific preclinical development.

leads.title: Scalable Thermoset Informatics Integrated with Autonomous Experimentation for On-Demand Discovery
leads.abstract: As photopolymer additive manufacturing matures, there is an increasing need for on-demand, application-specific materials. A major bottleneck is the limited exploration of the vast design space for new thermoset polymer formulations, which must satisfy both material property requirements and processing constraints. This challenge arises from the combinatorial complexity of formulations and the high cost of experimental evaluation. In this work, we present an end-to-end pipeline that integrates a partial self-driving laboratory (p-SDL) with informatics-driven optimization to discover and validate thermoset acrylate formulations. The pipeline begins with a thermoset acrylate database that consolidates multiple data sources, including in-house experiments, molecular dynamics simulations, and literature data. These data sets are used to train single-task and multitask predictive models, which interface directly with the p-SDL to guide experiments and measure mechanical and processing-related properties. Each component is validated independently and then deployed together to optimize a target elastomeric material with over 90% reduction in human effort. The complete optimization required only ∼40 h of active experimental time, demonstrating rapid identification of formulations that satisfy multiple target properties without exhaustive screening. This work establishes a scalable framework for embedding multifidelity machine learning within laboratory workflows, enabling autonomous, data-driven thermoset formulation discovery.

leads.title: Aqueous Ring-Opening Metathesis Polymerization for Water-Soluble Polymer Materials
leads.abstract: Aqueous ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP) has been recognized as an environmentally friendly and promising approach for synthesizing water-soluble polymer materials. However, the inevitable decomposition of Grubbs catalysts in aqueous media restricts aqueous ROMP with a low synthetic efficacy and poor control. Over the past few decades, substantial progress has been made in understanding the mechanisms behind catalyst decomposition in aqueous solution. Building on these insights, several advanced aqueous ROMP strategies have been developed, significantly facilitating the preparation of water-soluble polymer materials, including topological polymers, nanostructured polymer nano-objects, and polymer–protein bioconjugates. Encouragingly, these strategies have significantly lowered the barrier for researchers lacking a catalyst synthesis background, making aqueous ROMP a more accessible and user-friendly route to such materials. This Viewpoint focuses on the mechanisms of catalyst decomposition, highlights representative cases of aqueous ROMP from the past decade, and discusses the future prospects for this promising field.

leads.title: Thermosonication-assisted CaCl2 treatment reduces mung bean starch digestibility through cell-wall structural modification and starch reorganization
leads.abstract: Conventional processing can disrupt mung bean cell-walls, increasing enzymatic access to starch and compromising their low-glycemic potential. Ca 2+ -mediated regulation of starch digestibility has mainly focused on starch structure, whereas the contribution of the cell-wall barrier remains less clear. This study investigated whether thermosonication-assisted CaCl 2 treatment could alter cell-wall and starch structures to reduce mung bean starch digestibility. Thermosonication increased cell-wall permeability and facilitated calcium accumulation. The combined treatment increased non-methyl-esterified galacturonic acid, strengthened cell-wall barrier properties, and enhanced α -amylase adsorption and inhibition. At the starch level, the combined treatment reduced starch damage and promoted granule aggregation, accompanied by increased amylose content, short-range order, V-type diffraction features, and resistant starch, together with decreased double-helical organization and relative crystallinity. These changes were associated with reduced starch hydrolysis and estimated glycemic index. The findings provide a structural strategy for developing mung bean foods with lower predicted glycemic potential.

leads.title: Light-driven biohybrid microrobots for contact-enhanced photoenzymatic degradation of plastic debris
leads.abstract: Light-driven self-propelled microrobots offer opportunities for active environmental remediation by enabling controllable interactions with dispersed pollutants in aqueous environments. Here, we report biohybrid microrobots, composed of enzyme-functionalized, Au-decorated cubic hematite, that reversibly switch between clustered and dispersed states to enhance microrobot-substrate interactions and photoenzymatic degradation. In the dark, microrobots spontaneously assemble into interconnected filamentous clusters. Under blue-light irradiation, these clusters disassemble into self-propelled microrobots, increasing catalyst exposure and promoting broader microrobot-substrate interactions. Applied to polylactic acid (PLA) plastics, this collective-to-individual transition increases repeated microrobot-substrate contacts and promotes ester-bond hydrolysis at the polymer-water interface. Mass spectrometry identifies soluble PLA-derived oligomers, while electron microscopy reveals localized surface erosion after photoenzymatic treatment. By dynamically redistributing enzyme-functionalized microrobots across the polymer surface, reversible light-controlled switching enhances transient catalytic interactions and surface exploration. This strategy provides a general approach for optimizing photoenzymatic degradation by coupling collective organization, active motion, and catalyst accessibility in aqueous environments, while preserving reversible control over their spatial organization and activity.

leads.title: Harnessing bacterial symbionts of beetles for the valorization of lignin into value-added byproducts: Recent advances and future perspectives.
leads.abstract: Lignin is the most abundant renewable aromatic heteropolymer in nature and is highly recalcitrant due to its complex structure. The gut systems of beetles function as an evolutionarily optimized microreactor wherein mechanical pretreatment, physicochemical gradients, and selectively maintained microbial consortia act synergistically to transform, mineralize, and metabolize lignin as an energy source. Beetle-associated bacterial symbionts represent a promising yet underexploited resource for lignin valorization into value-added products. This review provides emerging evidence of lignin degradation by beetles in association with their gut symbionts and indicates the diversity of gut bacteria involved in lignin depolymerization. We further discuss the mechanisms by which beetles and their gut bacteria metabolize lignin, the lignin-transforming capacities of the bacterial symbionts and their potential application in the valorization of waste lignin into added-value byproducts. Finally, we assess the emerging research trends on the bioprospection of lignin-degrading bacteria from underexplored beetle species. Despite significant advantages, several key challenges remain unresolved, including difficulties in isolation and culturing of key gut bacteria in vitro, limited biochemical validation of candidate enzymes and the unresolved linking of specific genes or taxa to in situ lignin transformation. Future studies should integrate discovery-driven microbial ecology, multi-omics, predictive modeling and precision genome engineering to convert the complexity of beetle gut bacterial communities into a practical blueprint for scalable lignin valorization, and the biomanufacturing of high-value products from lignin-based waste.
leads.authors: Doumbia B, Luo S, Yang S, Wang C, Jia Y, Kuprin AV, Geng A, Zhu D, Sun J, Ezenwanne BC, Xie R, Dar MA.

leads.title: Wax-treated hemp fabrics to reduce water absorption in PLA/PBSA laminated composites
leads.abstract: Biocomposites with natural fibres have generated considerable interest thanks to their environmental sustainability. Nevertheless, their use in humid environments remains limited. This study investigates a blend of poly(lactic acid) (PLA) and poly(butylene succinate) (PBSA) reinforced with twill hemp fabric treated with an emulsion of waxes. The focus is to analyse the efficiency of the wax emulsion pre-treatment in decreasing the water uptake of these thermoplastic laminated composites. Two bio-based wax emulsions (from carnauba and sunflower) were used at 5, 10, and 15 wt%. Contact angle measurements on the fabrics were conducted using a Wilhelm balance setup to determine the wax treatments effectiveness. Tensile and contact angle tests demonstrated that the carnauba emulsion at 5 wt% exhibited an optimal compromise between mechanical properties and water repellence reaching a contact angle of 89.60°. The effect of the wax treatment on the final properties of the laminated composite system was evaluated through mechanical and thermal characterization. The effect of the wax treatment on the fibres adhesion with the polymeric matrix was also investigated by SEM analysis. The results demonstrated that the treatment did not cause a significant alteration in the structural integrity of the composites, contemporarily decreasing of 2% the water uptake.
leads.venue: Journal of Reinforced Plastics and Composites

Flame retardancy of polyurethane foam reinforced by hollow glass microspheres and ammonium polyphosphate
leads.abstract: Aiming at the characteristics of traditional polyurethane foam and easy combustion. In this work, a simple “one pot method” was used to prepared flame-retardant polyurethane foam through hollow glass microspheres (HGM) and ammonium polyphosphate (APP). The experimental results indicate that HGM and APP has good compatibility with polyurethane foam. The prepared polyurethane foam has rich macroporous structure and elasticity. In addition, compared with pure foam, flame retardant foam is hydrophobic. Furthermore, compared with pure PU foam, PU-FR foam has excellent flame retardancy, compared with PU foam, the peak heat release rate (pHRR) of PU-FR foam is reduced by about 12.9%. PU-FR foam has the characteristics of simple preparation process and excellent flame retardant performance, providing theoretical support for the industrial preparation of high-performance flame retardant polyurethane sponge.

leads.title: Bio-based benzoxazine electrically conductive adhesives for sustainable and epoxy-free hybrid printed electronics
leads.abstract: Electrically conductive adhesives (ECAs) are critical for the assembly of surface-mounted devices in printed and hybrid electronics; however, conventional epoxy-based systems are associated with toxicity and limited working life. In this work, we present a benzoxazine-based anisotropic conductive adhesive (ACA) derived from a bio-based diphenolic acid benzoxazine (DPA-Bz) copolymerized with 1,12-diaminododecane (DIADO), combined with environmentally preferable metallic fillers. The developed system enables reduced curing temperatures (~ 150°C) compared to conventional benzoxazines, improving compatibility with temperature-sensitive substrates. From an electrical standpoint, the optimized Cu-based ACA exhibits low contact resistance and clear anisotropic conductivity with electrical performance comparable to a commercial epoxy-based adhesive. Furthermore, the ACA maintains stable electrical behavior under accelerated aging (85°C / 85% RH) and thermal shock testing, indicating robust reliability under environmental stress. Finally, life cycle assessment reveals a reduced global warming potential (5.48 kg CO₂/kg) compared to a reference Ni-based adhesive (6.27 kg CO₂/kg), with further reduction potential through solvent-free formulations and increased recycled copper content. The presented benzoxazine-based ACA achieves comparable electrical and mechanical performance to commercial systems while delivering improved environmental performance and reduced toxicity, highlighting its potential as a sustainable alternative for next-generation electronic assembly and opening the path towards greener electronics.

leads.title: Probing Benzoxazine Dimer Formation Using Methyl-Blocked Derivatives as Mechanistic Probes
leads.abstract: The early-stage dimer formation of 1,3-benzoxazine (PH-a) was investigated as a diagnostic system for understanding the ring-opening polymerization (ROP) mechanism using a coupled FAIMS-IRMPD-MS/MS platform. High-field asymmetric waveform ion mobility spectrometry (FAIMS) resolved the protonated PH-a dimer into three distinct populations. A series of methyl-blocked benzoxazine derivatives was used to systematically eliminate individual reactive sites and assign each FAIMS population to a specific reaction route via tandem MS fragmentation patterns and IRMPD action spectroscopy, supported by theoretical vibrational spectra obtained by DFT calculations. Four dimer formation pathways were confirmed: phenolic aromatic substitution at the ortho and para positions, and arylamine aromatic substitution at the ortho and para positions of the aniline ring. Phenoxy- and nitrogen-mediated attack routes were not observed. Each pathway yields dimers in either a closed-ring (CRB) or open-ring (ROP) form, a structural duality with direct implications for the crosslinking topology and network heterogeneity of the resulting polybenzoxazine.

leads.title: 3D-Printed Gastroretentive Floating Modified-Release Device for Dual Cardiovascular Drug Delivery: Isosorbide Dinitrate and Hydralazine
leads.abstract: Background: Isosorbide dinitrate (ISDN) and hydralazine hydrochloride (HDZ) are dual cardiovascular drugs used to treat heart failure. However, the drugs have limitations such as short plasma half-life, low bioavailability, and potential for tolerance of the nitrate component. To address the need for prolonged drug release, a floating dual-compartment drug delivery system was developed to provide controlled drug release under simulated gastric dissolution conditions. Objectives: This study aimed to develop floating dual-compartment devices (FDCDs) to contain ISDN and HDZ gel and modify drug release under simulated gastric conditions. Methods: The FDCD was designed in a cylindrical shape consisting of an air chamber on the upper part for floating ability, and two compartments for loaded drug gel and controlling the drug release rate. Fused deposition modeling (FDM) was selected to fabricate FDCDs using polylactic acid (PLA) filament. The ISDN formulation varied the ratio of polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) to achieve drug release for 12 h. The HDZ formulation was optimized by varying the ratio of PVP and hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) to extend drug release at 24 h. Results: The shape dimension and weight variation in the FDCDs showed low standard deviation (SD). FDCDs exhibited immediate floating, resisted overturning, and demonstrated in vitro floating ability for more than 24 h. The formulation ISDN3 at a PVP: drug: water ratio of 5:2:3 exhibited complete release at 12 h, while the formulation of HDZ1 at an HPMC: PVP: drug: water ratio of 0.3:2.5:2:5.2 showed complete release within 24 h. The ISDN3- and HDZ1-loaded FDCDs demonstrated prolonged release behavior, with ISDN and HDZ release profiles showing the best fit to the zero-order and Higuchi models, respectively, based primarily on the coefficient of determination (R2), while root mean square error (RMSE) was used as a complementary measure of fitting error. Conclusions: These findings suggest that the developed dual-drug-loaded FDCD has potential as a dual-drug oral delivery platform for simultaneous delivery of ISDN and HDZ with prolonged drug release characteristics and further development of oral combination drug delivery systems.

leads.title: Comparative effect of physical and chemical treatments on the mechanical and barrier properties of Bambara groundnut-based protein-lipid films
leads.abstract: Aim: Increased awareness of environmentally friendly and biodegradable packaging materials and the need to reduce negative and harmful interactions of food with packaging materials have driven research efforts towards edible packaging using combinations of food-based polymeric substances. Such edible packaging materials, including protein-based, carbohydrate-based, lipid-based compounds and their combinations, have revolutionised packaging perception. In this study, protein-lipid films produced from the extract obtained via hydrothermal treatment of Bambara groundnut flour were essentially modified. Methods: The effects of chemical modification (using formaldehyde as a cross-linking agent) and exposure to ultraviolet (UV) light on the film-forming solutions were investigated. Films from the modified and pure solutions were analysed for their barrier and mechanical properties, including water vapour permeability and elongation at break, among others. Also colour parameters of the protein-lipid films were examined. Results: The findings revealed that the values for mechanical and barrier properties of the formed films were comparable to those of other composite films, and also presented an improvement over polysaccharide, protein, or lipid-only films. The film formation rate ranged from 2.92 ± 0.03 to 4.43 ± 0.03 g/10 min, while the film yield ranged from 5.46 ± 0.07 to 8.92 ± 0.02 g/100 mL. Water vapour permeability of the Bambara groundnut films ranged from 0.49–0.63 gm–1s–1Pa–1. The films had high opacity values. Elongation at break values for the UV-modified film (44.37) were higher than those of the unmodified film (43.07). Conclusions: The Bambara groundnut films had better mechanical strength compared to the reference soybean film. This indicates a possible use in the coating of brittle and light-sensitive foods.

Hydrolysis of 1,4‐Butanediol‐Derived Polyesters Into Tetrahydrofuran and Dicarboxylic Acids Over Lewis Acidic Ionic Liquids
leads.abstract: Chemical transformation of discarded polyesters into high‐value chemicals is of great significance for advancing circular economy and sustainable development. Herein, we report a facile and efficient strategy for one‐pot conversion of 1,4‐butanediol‐based polyesters (BDPs) via equivalent water hydrolysis. The reaction is achieved over 1‐butyl‐3‐methyl‐imidazolium chloride‐ZnCl 2 ‐based ionic liquids ([BMIm][Zn n Cl 2 n + 1 ]) under mild conditions (e.g., 120 °C), producing tetrahydrofuran (THF) and corresponding dicarboxylic acids. Among the designed ionic liquids, [BMIm][Zn 4 Cl 9 ] showed the optimal catalytic performance, affording dicarboxylic acids and THF in excellent yields. Moreover, the catalyst possesses excellent recyclability and can be reused for five consecutive runs without obvious activity attenuation. Mechanism investigation endorses that BDPs are first hydrolyzed to generate acyloxyl alcohol intermediates, which are further converted into THF and dicarboxylic acids through ring‐closing C─OH/C─O metathesis under the cooperation of cation‐anion pairs in the ionic liquid catalyst. This work establishes a simple, green, and novel protocol for the selective degradation and valorization of BDPs, holding great potential for practical industrial applications.

leads.title: Encapsulation of Porphyrins in Polymer Microgels and Microbeads for Heterogeneous Photooxidation
leads.abstract: Using porphyrin-mediated photocatalytic energy transfer to generate singlet oxygen is a premier strategy for green, selective chemical synthesis. However, such catalytic systems are mostly conducted in organic solvents. This work aims to explore the generation and utilization of singlet oxygen for photochemical oxidation in aqueous media. To this end, we prepared two porphyrins with reactive primary amines or charged quaternized ammonium groups for covalent and ionic crosslinking, producing TPP-loaded hydrophilic microgels and microbeads, respectively. We explored catalyst formulations to optimize singlet oxygen generation and the direct oxidation of various substrates. Both catalysts effectively facilitate the chemical conversion of thioethers, thiols, and aldehydes. In deuterium oxide, oxidation reactions of methionine, allyl sulfide, and benzaldehyde achieved high quantitative conversion due to a longer lifetime of singlet oxygen in deuterium oxide than that in water. Notably, the oxidation of thioethers stopped selectively at the sulfoxide stage, avoiding over-oxidation to sulfones. While this method offers an easy way to isolate the catalysts in aqueous media, the high cost of deuterium oxide and slower reaction rates in water suggest that future development of nanobeads via microfluidic devices could overcome molecular oxygen diffusion limitation and enhance reaction rates in water.

leads.title: Sustainable Diepoxide Monomers for Polyoxazolidinone‐Based High‐Performance Thermoplastics
leads.abstract: Owing to their outstanding mechanical, thermal, and chemical properties, polyoxazolidinones, which are accessible from the reaction of diepoxides and diisocyanates, have recently gained interest as a new class of high-performance thermoplastic materials. However, mainly bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (BADGE) has thus far served as benchmark for the diepoxide part. Herein, ten bisphenol-free diepoxides that are either bio-based or derived from chemical recycling are presented. All these epoxides selectively resulted in linear polyoxazolidinones using methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI) and p-tert-butyl phenyl glycidyl ether as chain regulators. The new polymers were characterized, and the thermal and mechanical properties were compared to the BADGE-based reference polyoxazolidinone. With three of the new diepoxide monomers, polyoxazolidinones with properties matching or surpassing those of BADGE-based polyoxazolidinone were obtained.

leads.title: Multiscale Interphase Engineering of Carbon Fiber/Epoxy Composites via Hyperbranched Epoxy Grafting
leads.abstract: A combined experimental and molecular simulation study was conducted to investigate the effect of hyperbranched epoxy (HPE) grafting on the interfacial and mechanical properties of carbon fiber/epoxy (CF/EP) composites. HPE was chemically grafted onto carbon fiber surfaces to construct an engineered interphase with enhanced physicochemical compatibility toward the epoxy matrix. Surface characterization revealed significantly increased roughness and wettability after HPE grafting. Compared with untreated CF/EP composites, the HPE‐functionalized composites exhibited improvements of 117.2%, 34.2%, and 13.5% in interfacial shear strength, interlaminar shear strength, and flexural strength, respectively, together with enhanced thermal stability. Fracture morphology analysis demonstrated substantially improved fiber/matrix adhesion and suppressed interfacial debonding. Molecular dynamics simulations further revealed increased interfacial interaction energy and reduced mean square displacement and free volume fraction, indicating restricted molecular‐chain mobility and the formation of a more compact interfacial structure. Overall, this work provides multiscale insights into the interfacial reinforcement mechanisms induced by HPE grafting and demonstrates the potential of interphase engineering for the development of high‐performance CF/EP composites.

leads.title: Preparation and Performance Study of Seamless Polyimide Tube
leads.abstract: Solutions of the corresponding polyamide acid were synthesized using different types of dianhydrides and diamines, respectively. Seamless polyimide tubes of various types were then fabricated through multistage coating, thermal imidization, annealing, and core‐pulling processes. The optical, mechanical, thermal, and electrical properties of the polyimide tubes were investigated. The results show that the PI‐T polyimide tube exhibits the best optical properties, with a light transmittance as high as 79.1% at 550 nm and 82.1% at 650 nm. At the same time, the PI‐T polyimide tube demonstrates excellent electrical properties with a breakdown voltage of 4.8 kV (thickness: 35 μm).

Affinity columns as a key to unravel the potential of biochemical pathways.
leads.abstract: The vast majority of natural metabolic pathways remain uncharacterized, limiting the ability to harness biological systems for industrial biotechnology and environmental bioremediation. Classical functional genomics and activity-guided purification protocols frequently fail to map multi-step metabolic cascades due to transient protein-substrate interactions, rapid metabolic flux, and the inherent complexity of complex cellular proteomes. Here, I present the comprehensive protocol for Sequential Affinity-Based Pathway Mapping (SAMP) an iterative, multi-phase chromatographic framework designed to systematically trace metabolic cascades across different chemical states of matter (solid, liquid, and gas). By utilizing the native or immobilized state of a metabolic substrate as an affinity bait for cellular proteomes, SAMP enables the layer-by-layer isolation, elution, and structural characterization of sequential enzymes within an uncharacterized cascade. I highlight the utility of this method using bacterial plastic degradation as an archetypal model for solid-phase systems, detail the physical encapsulation frameworks required for unstable or liquid intermediates, and propose a pressurized micro-perfusion strategy to handle volatile gaseous substrates.

leads.title: Molecular interaction of Candida albicans with polymeric materials: Correlation of single cell adhesion forces, gene expression and surface characteristics
leads.abstract: Candida albicans (C. albicans) is a commensal member of the oral microbiota that can form biofilms, contributing to denture stomatitis. Its initial adhesion to abiotic surfaces is a critical step in biofilm formation and is strongly influenced by the material's physicochemical properties. Surface roughness, surface free energy (SFE), and salivary components play key roles in mediating fungal-material interactions. Polymeric materials are components of denture materials, so understanding the interactions with C. albicans is essential to clarify the mechanisms underlying early fungal adhesion. However, the molecular and biophysical mechanisms that govern fungal adhesion to polymer materials are not well characterized. This study examined C. albicans adhesion behavior on polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) surfaces with defined roughness levels Ra = 0.2 μm and 0.04 μm) with saliva. Surface properties were characterized using profilometry and contact angle measurements, while adhesion forces and cell-surface interactions were analyzed by single-cell force spectroscopy (SCFS) using atomic force microscopy (AFM) varying contact forces. The expression of the adhesion- and biofilm-associated genes ALS1, HWP1, and EFG1 was quantified by quantitative reverse transcription PCR (qRT-PCR). Rough surfaces resulted in stronger adhesion and more contact points. In contrast, higher SFE was associated with reduced adhesion. Saliva pretreatment modulated these interactions. Gene expression analyses revealed that early adhesion is primarily regulated by polymer-dependent surface signals, while hyphae- and biofilm-specific pathways exhibited minimal activation. In summary, the results demonstrate that the surface properties of polymeric materials significantly influence the early adhesion of C. albicans and its associated molecular responses.

leads.title: Non-monotonic effect of organo-bentonite dosage on the residual foaming-pressure retention of one-component polyurethane water-sealing grout
leads.abstract: Foaming one-component polyurethane grouts are widely used to seal water leakage through cracks and joints in aging underground concrete structures, and their long-term sealing performance depends not only on initial expansion but also on the residual foaming pressure retained under confinement after curing. This study examines how the dosage of an N-type organically modified bentonite affects the constrained foaming-pressure history and internal structure of such a grout. Mixtures containing 0, 1, and 5 wt% organo-bentonite relative to the urethane base were prepared at a constant water-to-urethane mass ratio of 0.40, monitored in a constrained foaming-pressure apparatus for 18 days, and characterized by optical microscopy, SEM-EDS elemental mapping, and ATR-FTIR spectroscopy. The reference and 1 wt% mixtures reached similar peak pressures (246.2 and 248.0 kPa), whereas the 5 wt% mixture peaked at 208.0 kPa. In contrast, the 14-day residual pressure was 17.7 kPa for the reference, 2.8 kPa at 1 wt%, and 8.1 kPa at 5 wt%, and the half-pressure time was longest at 5 wt%. Bentonite addition appeared to refine the foam cells and dispersed Si- and Al-bearing clay phases throughout the matrix; the principal urethane bands were unchanged, while the C=O-normalized O–H band intensity was clearly elevated only at 5 wt%. Because each mixture was tested with a single specimen at three dosage levels, the non-monotonic dosage effect is presented as an exploratory finding, and microstructural stabilization above a threshold clay content is proposed as a hypothesis that requires replicate confirmation at intermediate dosages.
leads.authors: Inazumi, Arima, 中沢 et al.

leads.title: Alkali Lignin and Lignosulfonate Tune Strength, Extensibility, and Hydration in Multifunctional Deep Eutectic Gel Strain Sensors
leads.abstract: Integrating strength, large deformation, adhesion, self-repair, antimicrobial activity, and stable ionic sensing within a biomass-containing soft material remains difficult because these properties depend on competing network requirements. Here, alkali lignin (AL) and lignosulfonate (LS) were incorporated into an acrylic acid/choline chloride/betaine polymerizable deep eutectic matrix to regulate these trade-offs. Spectroscopic, diffraction, microscopic, thermal, and electrokinetic measurements showed that lignin chemistry altered the local chemical environment, morphology, water uptake, and degradation behavior of the resulting deep eutectic gels. AL shifted the mechanical response toward reinforcement: tensile strength increased from 0.90 MPa for AL0.5-DG to 5.75 MPa for AL2.5-DG, while strain at break decreased from approximately 960% to 435%. LS retained a deformation-tolerant window, with LS1.5-DG reaching approximately 1010% strain at break and a final swelling ratio of approximately 249%. Density functional calculations and a ChCl-centered molecular dynamics analysis identified localized lignin contacts with betaine, choline/chloride, acrylic species, and polymer-associated sites. The gels also adhered to dissimilar substrates, recovered 0.67 MPa tensile strength after 8 h of interfacial healing, reduced bacterial survival at higher lignin loading, and produced repeatable resistance responses over 10–150% strain, 3600 s cycling, and subzero deformation. The results establish lignin chemistry as a practical control variable for balancing load bearing, hydration, recovery, and ionic sensing in multifunctional deep eutectic gels.

leads.title: Sustainable PVA-Chitosan Biocomposite Films: Effects of Chitosan Loading on Material Properties and Biodegradability
leads.abstract: Global reliance on non-biodegradable petroleum-based plastics is a significant environmental concern that necessitates the development of eco-friendly alternatives. Poly(vinyl) alcohol (PVA) shows high potential, but its application is limited because of its high moisture sensitivity and intermediate strength. In this study, the effect of crosslinking chitosan (CS) at 5-35% loading on different material properties and biodegradability of poly(vinyl) alcohol-chitosan (PVA-CS) biocomposite films was investigated. FTIR analysis confirmed the successful crosslinking between the two polymers. The integration of CS in the polymer matrix of PVA improved its UV-blocking properties by 25-55%. The degree of swelling and solubility is inversely related to %CS in PVA-CS films. Pure PVA and PVA-CS films showed higher tensile strengths but lower elongation at break compared to LDPE. Thermogravimetry showed 4-stage thermal degradation, with maximum degradation at 280-380°C for the PVA-based films. Significant improvement in the biodegradability of PVA films was observed with the incorporation of CS. Based on the tested %CS loading, a minimum of 15% CS is required to see significant improvement in the biodegradation rate, UV-blocking, and mechanical properties of the PVA-CS films. These findings have direct practical implications for sustainable engineering, showing the potential of PVA-CS biocomposites as a biodegradable alternative to traditional plastics.

leads.title: Development of Instantly Dispersible Soy Protein Isolate Granules via Wet Granulation with HPMC and Crospovidone
leads.abstract: Soy protein isolate (SPI) is a highly nutritious plant-based protein essential for preventing age-related conditions like sarcopenia; however, its application is severely hindered by inherent hydrophobicity and poor water dispersibility, which causes severe lumping. This study aimed to develop dispersible SPI granules by applying pharmaceutical excipients via wet granulation. SPI was granulated using hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC; 0.5–1.5%) as a binder and crospovidone (1.0–2.0%) as a superdisintegrant. The physicochemical and reconstitution properties were evaluated. The granulation process successfully transformed fine SPI powder into large, highly porous agglomerates. The optimized formulation (1.5% HPMC and 2.0% crospovidone) significantly reduced the dispersing time to 5.33 s and lowered the equilibrium contact angle (32.08°), promoting fast capillary water uptake. FTIR and XRD analyses confirmed the protein’s chemical and structural integrity remained unaltered, indicating purely physical interactions. DSC revealed a binder-concentration-dependent decrease in denaturation temperature due to plasticization. Furthermore, the reconstituted formulations exhibited shear-thinning rheological behavior. This study shows that the application of HPMC and crospovidone as modifying excipients in wet granulation presented a chemically inert granulation approach that overcomes hydrophobic lumping and improves plant protein dispersibility. This strategy highlights a strong potential for creating convenient nutritional supplements for the elderly.

leads.title: Formulation-Dependent Physical, Mechanical, and Water-Exposure Behavior of Hemp-Based Mycelium Composites with Polymeric Additives
leads.abstract: Hemp-based mycelium composites are promising bio-based materials, but their heterogeneous structure may strongly affect mechanical performance and stability under water exposure. Six hot-pressed composites based on hemp hurds and chopped hemp straw, colonized with Pleurotus ostreatus or Ganoderma applanatum, were investigated. Depending on formulation, spent coffee grounds, thermoplastic or plasticized starch, and polymeric components introduced as granules, film flakes, or poly(ε-caprolactone) meshes were incorporated. Apparent density, water absorption, dimensional changes during immersion, compression, and three-point bending were evaluated. Mean apparent density ranged from 0.69 to 0.96 g × cm−3 and showed a positive specimen-level association with maximum compressive stress within the investigated plates (Spearman’s ρ = 0.845, n = 30). Because only one plate was manufactured per formulation, the observed formulation-specific property profiles represent exploratory observations within the investigated manufactured plates rather than population-level estimates of formulation effects or manufacturing reproducibility. The highest mean maximum compressive stress was 5.7 ± 1.2 MPa, whereas the highest mean maximum flexural stress and flexural modulus were 4.6 ± 2.1 MPa and 627 ± 285 MPa, respectively. Water uptake, dimensional swelling, and retention of measurable integrity followed different formulation-dependent trends; the greatest through-thickness swelling did not necessarily correspond to the fastest loss of cohesion. Overall, density, mechanical response, water uptake, dimensional deformation, and wet-state integrity were related but distinct descriptors of material performance, highlighting the need for multi-property optimization.

leads.title: Mass-Rearing of Insects on Food Waste to Produce Chitosan—A Bio-Based Plastic Alternative
leads.abstract: Mass-rearing of insects is being promoted to meet demands for sustainable sources of livestock and pet feed, protein, oils, pharmaceutical precursors and more. Here, we describe an industrial symbiosis, in which insect mass-rearing is based on food waste, and chitin extracted from insect exoskeleton is converted into chitosan and used to generate alternatives to conventional plastic materials—hereafter referred to as “chitosan bio-based plastics”. If so, challenges associated with synthetic plastic production, plastic pollution, greenhouse gas emissions associated with landfill waste and food waste management may be mitigated simultaneously. Such industrial symbioses align with at least 10 of the 17 United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Chitosan is a biodegradable, non-toxic polymer with potential use in a range of disposable plastic applications. We describe characteristics of chitosan, the global chitosan market, how chitosan can be modified into different types of bio-based plastics, and we highlight challenges and constraints.

leads.title: Compound polyethylene glycol electrolyte powder-based bowel preparation protects the intestinal barrier: A retrospective controlled study
leads.abstract: Background: Preoperative bowel preparation is a crucial perioperative step in gastrointestinal surgery. Traditional mannitol combined with soap enema regimens can easily damage the intestinal mucosa and disrupt the intestinal barrier. Compound polyethylene glycol electrolyte powder (PGEP) has the potential to protect the intestinal barrier; however, multidimensional clinical evidence remains limited. Objectives: From the perspective of intestinal barrier protection, this study compares the effects of PGEP and traditional regimens in elective gastrointestinal surgery, analyzing their influence on the intestinal barrier, microecology, stress, intestinal function and anastomotic healing. Methods: In this retrospective controlled study, 100 patients undergoing elective surgery at the Department of Gastrointestinal Surgery, Wenzhou Central Hospital, from June 2021 to June 2024 were allocated into an observation group (PGEP group, n=50;28 males, 22 females) and a control group (traditional regimen group, n=50;26 males, 24 females;) Patients were assigned to groups according to the bowel preparation regimen used in routine clinical practice. Relevant laboratory indicators were measured and clinical outcomes were recorded. Results: The primary endpoint, serum diamine oxidase (DAO) level on the 1st day after surgery, was significantly lower in the observation group than in the control group (p < 0.05). For the secondary endpoints, the observation group also showed superior bowel preparation quality (assessed by BBPS), better preservation of intestinal barrier function, greater gut microbiota stability (higher fecal short-chain fatty acids and more stable pH), a reduced stress response, faster recovery of intestinal function, reduced anastomotic edema, a higher primary healing rate and a lower overall postoperative complication rate (all p < 0.05). Conclusion: PGEP is clinically superior to traditional methods for preoperative bowel preparation in elective gastrointestinal surgeries. It effectively protects the intestinal mucosal barrier, stabilizes the gut microbiota and reduces stress, aligning with the principles of enhanced recovery after surgery (ERAS) and these results suggest potential clinical value.

leads.title: Development of Sustainable Thermoplastic Zein by Partial Substitution of Glycerol with Olive Oil or Oleic Acid: a New Route for Injection-Molded Biopolymers
leads.abstract: Thermoplastic zein formulations containing 25 wt% total modifier were processed by extrusion and injection molding. Glycerol was progressively replaced with oleic acid (OA) or olive oil (OO) at substitution levels ranging from 2.5 to 10 wt%, while maintaining the zein and total modifier contents at 75 and 25 wt%, respectively. The formulation containing 10 wt% OO could not be successfully processed. Partial substitution with OO increased tensile stiffness and strength, reaching 1294 MPa and 25.5 MPa, respectively, for ZEI-GLY-7.5OO, while maintaining elongation at break close to, but below, that of the glycerol-only control. Conversely, substitution with OA generally reduced tensile strength and elongation at break. All modified formulations exhibited lower impact strength than the control. Differential scanning calorimetry revealed low-temperature calorimetric transitions at 2.0–6.3 °C for the OA-containing formulations and − 17.4 to -14.2 °C for the OO-containing formulations, whereas DMTA showed a principal thermomechanical relaxation around 50–60 °C. Thermogravimetric analysis showed onset degradation temperatures of approximately 198 °C for the OO-containing materials, compared with 173 °C for the control and 154–172 °C for the OA-containing formulations. Water contact angles increased from 26° for the control to approximately 30–50° after OA or OO incorporation, indicating reduced surface wettability. Most formulations achieved complete disintegration within four weeks under simulated composting conditions, and all materials were completely disintegrated by week 5. Overall, among the compositions investigated, partial substitution of glycerol with OO produced a favorable tensile-property profile while retaining rapid disintegration. However, these responses reflect the combined effects of OO incorporation and the simultaneous reduction in glycerol content.

leads.title: Molecular catalysts for CO2/epoxide copolymerization to polycarbonates: From metal selection to performance benchmarks
leads.abstract: The rising atmospheric CO 2 levels have intensified global efforts to mitigate climate change and limit its associated impacts. CO 2 utilization provides a sustainable route to value-added chemicals, fuels, and materials, and catalytic CO 2 /epoxide ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP) to polycarbonates is among the most promising pathways. Recently, metal complexes have emerged as highly efficient molecular catalysts for polycarbonate synthesis, enabling tunable activity and polymer properties through metal choice, ligand design, cocatalyst/ion-pair engineering, and control over epoxide scope. This review surveys molecular catalysts based on cobalt(III), zinc(II), aluminum(III), chromium(III), iron(III), nickel(II), and magnesium(II) for CO 2 /epoxide ROCOP, with emphasis on recent advances. Particular attention is given to how the coordination environment, ligand structure, and cocatalyst interactions govern catalytic activity, selectivity, and polymer microstructure. A benchmarking approach is presented to enable comparison of catalysts across different metal families and operating conditions. Representative systems operate under 1–60 bar CO 2 and 20–120 °C, achieving TON values up to 55,000 and TOF up to 155,000 h −1 , with number-average molecular weights (M n ) up to 300 kg/mol. Hybrid strategies combining molecular and heterogeneous catalysis can further increase M n to ∼700 kg/mol. Finally, remaining challenges, including enhancing activity under mild conditions, suppressing by-product formation, and achieving precise control over polymer molecular weight and microstructure, are discussed. By identifying key coordination-chemistry relationships, this review provides guidelines for the rational design of next-generation catalysts for CO 2 -derived polycarbonates.

leads.title: From MOF to polyMOF: Incorporation of Poly(itaconic acid) into a Cu-Ellagate Framework
leads.abstract: The incorporation of flexible coordinating polymers into crystalline metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) remains challenging because the conformational freedom of macromolecular ligands can interfere with the development of long-range order. Here, we report IEF-35(Cu), a new Cu–ellagate MOF whose crystal structure was resolved by electron diffraction, and its extension to a polymer-containing framework, PolyIEF-35(Cu), through the incorporation of poly(itaconic acid) (PIA) as a co-ligand. The resulting hybrid retained the characteristic features of the parent framework while displaying pronounced changes in particle morphology and gas sorption. Variation of the ellagic acid (EA) to PIA ratio showed that the crystalline hybrid could be obtained over a relatively broad compositional range. Both materials retained their crystallinity upon heating up to 250 °C and exhibited substantial stability toward the investigated solvents. Finally, biological studies showed cytocompatibility under the investigated conditions and antibacterial activity against Staphylococcus epidermidis .

leads.title: Modifying Mechanical Polymer Composite by Using Hybrid Materials
leads.abstract: This study investigates the characteristics of polymer resin reinforced with sunflower shell particles (SSP) with the aim of exploring the mechanical properties of hybrid composites. First, prepare an epoxy sample, then reinforce the matrix with a glass fiber at a 5% weight fraction, before preparing hybrid composite samples (5% fiber glass + 0.1% polypropylene chopped fibers + different concentrations of sunflower shell particles), and finally test the samples' tensile, flexural, impact, and hardness to determine their mechanical properties. The reason for choosing this study was its practical use in prosthetic feet. The results revealed that increasing the particle concentration improved the tensile, flexural, and impact capabilities, but decreased the hardness (Shore D). The hybrid composite specimens with 94.6% EP, 5% E-glass, 0.1% PMM, and 0.3% SSP had the determined tensile strength, flexural strength, and impact strength (38 and 92) Mpa, & (1.4 KJ/m2).

leads.title: Ionically Counter‐Programmable Phase‐Separation of Superstable Star‐Biopolyamide Coacervates for Electrothermally‐Responsive Pseudosolid Smart Windows
leads.abstract: Thermoresponsive polymers are highly anticipated for passive thermochromic smart windows, yet the instability and too‐high mobility of their light‐scattering states for separated phases remain significant hurdles. To address these challenges, we report a design concept for pyrrolidone‐based star‐polyamides synthesized from itaconic acid and cadaverine, whose architecture provides exceptional sensitivity to external stimuli. In a stark departure from the classical Hofmeister series, Ca 2+ initiates an anomalous salting‐in effect that contrasts with the Na + ‐induced salting‐out. DFT/MD calculations reveal that pyrrolidone moderately coordinates with Ca 2+ without disrupting its hydration shell, thereby imparting a dense positive charge to the coacervate surfaces. Crucially, the cationic surface charge endows the coacervates with light‐scattering bodies with superior dispersion stability, surpassing conventional PNIPAM by over 20‐fold. The system maintains robust stability at 5 mol/L, a regime where conventional thermoresponsive polymers inevitably fail. An applied electric field enables spatial control of transparency, creating a dual electro‐thermal responsive system for energy‐efficient, sustainable smart windows. Furthermore, the Ca 2+ salting‐in effects enable coacervation in a high polymer concentration range over 50% to establish pseudosolidity, which provides a versatile platform for next‐generation electro‐thermal soft systems, ranging from implantable biosensors to battery‐operated smart windows.
leads.authors: Liu J, Zhu X, Hou J, Du J, Ali M, Okajima M, Kaneko T.

leads.title: Study of the Physicochemical Properties of Technical Starch for Molding and Core Materials
leads.abstract: This article investigates the composition, moisture content, rheological, and physicochemical properties of modified technical starch used as a binder for molding and core mixtures in foundry production. The polysaccharide structure of starch composed of amylose and amylopectin, its swelling and gelatinization in water, the formation of carboxyl and carbonyl groups during modification, and the effect of these changes on adhesive and rheological properties were analyzed. During mechanochemical treatment in the presence of an oxidizing agent, the content of carboxyl groups was found to increase from 0,17% to 0,41%. An increase in viscosity with increasing starch concentration and a decrease in viscosity as the temperature increased from 20°C to 50°C were observed in technical starch solutions. The results demonstrate the potential of locally sourced technical starch as an effective polysaccharide binder for foundry molding and core mixtures.

Integrated Electromicrobial Production of Itaconic Acid From CO 2 at Liter‐Scale Using Komagataella phaffii
leads.abstract: Coupling electrochemical CO 2 reduction showing high selectivity with microbial biosynthesis offering metabolic versatility offers a promising strategy for converting CO 2 into value‐added products. We present proof‐of‐concept of electromicrobially producing the platform chemical itaconic acid (IA) from CO 2 using a robust yeast chassis. The hybrid systems integrates in a single reactor electrochemical CO 2 reduction with microbial synthesis using a synthetic autotrophic Komagataella phaffii strain. Thereby CO 2 serves as carbon source while electrochemically generated formate from CO 2 provides reducing power to sustain microbial growth and drive IA production, reaching average titres of 110.1 mg·L −1 . While demonstrating the feasibility of directly coupling electrochemical and microbial processes within a single reactor, we reveal key challenges associated with integration, including limited system performance, variability in product titers, anodic oxidation of cathodic products, and constraints in energy efficiency. Despite these current limitations, our results establish the operational feasibility of integrated electromicrobial CO 2 conversion using industrial yeast and highlight critical parameters for process intensification.
leads.authors: Izadi, Severinsen Zijlstra, Kas et al.

leads.title: Thermal Stability of Aliphatic and Semiaromatic Polyamides: Tailoring the Choice of Isothermal Aging Temperature by Using Kinetic Models of Degradation
leads.abstract: The objective of this work is to develop an analytical method for determining an accelerated aging temperature for polymers. This study presents the process used to address the aging temperature by using isoconversional methods for polyamides based polymers. These methods are based on several thermogravimetric analyses at different heating rates. The activation energies, associated with the degradation phenomenon of an aliphatic polyamide and a semiaromatic one, were determined by the Friedman method. Thanks to these activation energies and Toop's model, we have been able to propose kinetic models of degradation and temperature's domain well‐suited for accelerated thermal aging. This method, which combines both an experimental approach and the use of phenomenological models, turns out to be a rigorous tool for choosing aging temperatures.

leads.title: Synergistic Effects of Boron‐Based Derivatives via Triple Char‐Forming Effects: Simultaneously Conferring High Flame Retardancy and Mechanical Toughening to Epoxy Resins
leads.abstract: To overcome the flammability, poor charring, and brittleness of epoxy resin (EP), a flame‐retardant additive, BPD, was synthesized from N‐aminoethylpiperazine, 4‐acetylphenylboronic acid, and DOPO, and then incorporated into EP to obtain EP/BPD composites. With 3 wt% BPD, the LOI increased from 25.7% to 28.3%, and the UL‐94 rating improved from NR to V‐0. At 5 wt% BPD loading, pHRR, THR, SPR, TSR, COP, and CO 2 P decreased by 39.1%, 10.2%, 42.8%, 74.3%, 30.0%, and 39.3%, respectively, versus pure EP, demonstrating excellent flame retardancy, smoke suppression, and fire safety. Moreover, 1 wt% BPD raised impact strength to 28.79 kJ/m 2 (65.9% increase), while tensile (51.98 MPa) and flexural strengths (69.78 MPa) remained nearly unchanged, achieving a synergistic balance of flame retardancy and mechanical toughness.

leads.title: Preparation and Characterization of Recyclable Basalt Fiber Composites
leads.abstract: Although epoxy (EP) based composites possess excellent mechanical properties, their highly cross‐linked network structure makes it difficult to recycle once discarded, resulting in significant waste of resources, and an environmental burden. In this study, biobased tannic acid was used as the raw material to synthesize carboxylate tannic acid (TACOOH) via carboxylation modification, which was then combined with methyl hexahydro phthalic anhydride (MeHHPA) to construct a biodegradable epoxy curing system rich in ester bonds. Concurrently, basalt fibers (BF) were surface‐modified using the silane coupling agent KH560 to prepare TACOOH/EP/BF composites. The mechanical properties, thermal stability, and feasibility of fiber recovery and reuse of the composites were investigated. The results indicate that modification with KH560 enhanced the interfacial bond strength between the fibers and the resin matrix; the flexural strength of the modified composite (MBF/EP@TACOOH) reached 254.30 MPa, representing a 12.15% increase compared to the unmodified system; following degradation and recovery in a 180°C ethylene glycol/water mixture, the flexural strength of the composite fabricated from the recovered fibers (RBF) still reached 248.40 MPa, with a retention rate of 97.7%, and its thermal decomposition behavior was consistent with that of the virgin fiber system. Scanning electron microscopy and monofilament tensile tests indicated that the recovery process caused only minor damage to the fiber's internal structure, and the silane active sites remaining on the surface were still able to effectively ensure interfacial performance. This study provides a green and feasible technical pathway for the high‐value recovery of epoxy composites and the recycling of fibers.

leads.title: Additive manufacturing of thermosetting bio-composites by temperature-controlled paste extrusion: application to honeycomb sandwich panels
leads.abstract: A temperature-controlled paste-extrusion process was developed to enable additive manufacturing of otherwise unprintable thermosetting bio-composites. Bioepoxy was combined with lignin-containing cellulose particles to form a high-viscosity paste. Ambient partial curing raised the apparent viscosity to approximately 10⁵ mPa·s at 1 s⁻¹, after which the premix was cooled to 5–10 °C to retard further crosslinking during loading and deposition. The resulting formulations exhibited pronounced shear-thinning behaviour, were cost-effective, and contained a high bio-based fraction (58–71%). Systematic printability trials demonstrated that direct extrusion of the uncooled paste produced failed specimens, whereas the delayed-deposition route yielded stable, geometrically accurate honeycomb cores. Printed objects displayed good machinability under computer numerical control. As a representative application, hexagonal honeycomb cores were fabricated and bonded between plywood face sheets to produce bio-based sandwich panels. Tensile characterisation of the core material and three-point bending tests of the completed panels confirmed that the printed bio-composite provides adequate stiffness and load-bearing capacity for lightweight structural use. Overall, the process offers a practical route for valorising lignocellulosic fillers in thermosetting matrices and for achieving on-demand solidification in layer-wise fabrication of sustainable cellular structures.

leads.title: Development of alginate, cellulose and chitosan-based hybrid multicomponent films containing TAB@CuBTC MOFs: morphological features, surface properties and antimicrobial activity.
leads.abstract: Here, we report alginate (ALG), carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC), and chitosan (CHS) hybrid films incorporating CuBTC metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) containing a bioactive 2-aminothiophene derivative (TAB). Crystallite sizes estimated by the Debye-Scherrer and Williamson-Hall methods were 49.47/49.84 nm for CuBTC and 45.96/58.71 nm for TAB@CuBTC, respectively, suggesting possible strain-related broadening in TAB@CuBTC. UV-Vis mass-balance analysis gave a TAB loading capacity of 19.98 ± 0.92 wt% for the 45 mg feed. Nitrogen physisorption showed decreases in BET surface area from ~581.3 to ~123.2 m 2 /g and total pore volume from ~0.257 to ~0.086 cm 3 /g after TAB incorporation, indicating reduced accessible porosity. TAB release was pH-dependent, with the apparent zero-order rate constant (k 0 ) increasing from 0.0983%·h -1 at pH 8.5 to 0.1514%·h -1 at pH 4.5, corresponding to an approximately 54% higher apparent release rate under acidic conditions. The hybrid films showed formulation- and time-dependent cytocompatibility, with cell viability at 10 wt% ranging from 57.6 ± 6.5% to 98.7 ± 0.3%. Antibacterial activity depended on polymer matrix and bacterial strain. CHS/TAB@CuBTC produced inhibition zones of 12.7 ± 1.1 mm against Pseudomonas sp. and 14.8 ± 2.5 mm against Serratia marcescens, whereas CMC/TAB@CuBTC showed 18.2 ± 1.7 mm against Bacillus subtilis and 11.0 ± 0.5 mm against Klebsiella sp. Overall, the results demonstrate a multicomponent hybrid-film platform combining pH-dependent TAB release with matrix-dependent cytocompatibility and antibacterial performance.
leads.authors: Shipilovskikh SA, Vu THN, Cam TS, Brodskaia A, Nosova NA, Kuzminova A, Dmitrenko M, Penkova A, Timin AS.
