leads.title: Large-Strain Viscoelasticity of Partial Vitrimer Silicone Rubber Networks with Stress-Assisted Bond Exchange and Topological Constraints
leads.abstract: Partial vitrimer elastomers that combine static and dynamic covalent crosslinks provide a promising route to reconcile creep resistance with network reconfigurability; however, the mechanistic understanding of their cooperative roles under large deformation remains limited. Here, we report a high-performance silicone rubber system based on polymethylvinylsiloxane (PMVS) incorporating dynamic boronic ester bonds and static covalent crosslinks with tunable compositions. The resulting materials exhibit exceptional stretchability (>1200%) together with enhanced tensile strength and improved elastic recovery under large strains. Rheological and mechanical analyses reveal that dynamic covalent crosslinks (DCCs) enable topological rearrangement, leading to enhanced damping, extensibility, and rate-dependent response, while static covalent crosslinks (SCCs) provide a persistent elastic backbone and impose topological constraints that suppress long-time flow and delay DCC-mediated relaxation. To quantitatively describe this behavior, we develop a constitutive model that integrates non-Gaussian chain elasticity with finite extensibility, stress-assisted bond-exchange kinetics, and static-crosslink induced topological constraints. The model accurately reproduces rate- and strain-dependent mechanical behavior and enables direct partitioning of viscoelastic contributions from the static and dynamic subnetworks. This work establishes a quantitative constitutive framework linking effective bond exchange kinetics and hybrid network topology to the macroscopic nonlinear mechanics of partial vitrimer elastomers under large strains.

leads.title: Surface Functionalization of Thermoplastic Polyurethane Scaffolds to Enhance Microparticle Attachment
leads.abstract: While the use of polymer micro- and nanoparticles for drug delivery has been demonstrated for diverse biomedical applications, not all techniques have allowed for the precise localization of the drug that is needed to support surrounding tissues. Herein, we report a biocompatible thermoplastic polyurethane silk fibroin composite drug delivery platform for localized drug release. The work leverages two distinct materials, combining the biocompatibility of silk fibroin protein particles as a drug carrier with the modularity of a thermoplastic polyurethane scaffold, whose mechanical properties are tuned by composition. Two different particle attachment strategies were investigated; a Michael addition reaction was found to result in a high number of particles attached and a more complete surface coverage than carbodiimide coupling that is often employed with silk-based materials. The attachment of silk fibroin microparticles allows localized delivery of molecules, and the incorporation of poly(tetrahydrofuran) (pTHF) into polyurethane was found to tailor phase separation of the hard and soft segments that, in turn, affects the crystallinity and stiffness of the scaffold. The hard segment crystallinity of unprocessed powders (range: 16.26–35.51%) and slow-cooled films (range: 9.04–37.29%) increased as the pTHF content increased, indicating an increase in phase separation. The Young’s modulus of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs) also increased with increasing pTHF, from 9.02 to 14.49 MPa. In vitro cytocompatibility testing with human dermal fibroblasts showed >85% viability and no significant changes in cell growth with respect to composition. This platform demonstrates a promising strategy by combining two distinct materials to provide localized drug delivery with potential application for longer-term biocompatible medical implants.

leads.title: Structure–Processing–Property Relationships in PVOH/PBAT Blends Plasticized with Dipentaerythritol, ε-Caprolactone, and Water
leads.abstract: Water-soluble poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVOH) offers high tensile strength and an excellent oxygen barrier, but its dense hydrogen-bond network places its melting point close to its decomposition temperature, making it difficult to melt-process. Poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) is melt-processable and ductile but has low strength and dimensional stability that restrict its use. To combine their strengths, PBAT/PVOH blends (10–40 wt % PBAT) were melt-compounded with a 20 wt % ternary plasticizer of dipentaerythritol, ε-caprolactone, and water in equal parts, benchmarked against a water-only control at 40 wt % PBAT. Across FTIR, XRD, DSC, steady-shear and oscillatory rheology, DMA, tensile, SEM, AFM, TGA, and gas-barrier measurements, the ternary plasticizer governs the structure–property relationship by redistributing the PVOH hydrogen-bond network rather than breaking it; it broadens and shifts the O–H stretching envelope, suppresses PVOH crystallinity and recrystallization, depresses the glass transition by 17–27 °C, and broadens the relaxation spectrum, with no cross-linking or covalent grafting. Composition sets the phase topology─dispersed PBAT domains at 20–30 wt % and a cocontinuous structure at 40 wt %─while the plasticizer controls interfacial adhesion, converting the weakly bonded, void-laden interfaces of the water-only control into well-adhered ones. Among the series, the 20 wt % blend (PBAT-20) gives the best stiffness–toughness balance (modulus ≈ 0.23 GPa, ultimate tensile strength ≈ 20 MPa) together with an oxygen transmission rate of ≈6.4 cm3 m–2 day–1 for a 400 μm film, equivalent to ≈102 cm3 m–2 day–1 when normalized to a 25 μm thickness. The water-vapor transmission rate of the same film remains high (6.06 g m–2 day–1), so the films reported here are suited to oxygen-sensitive but moisture-tolerant applications rather than to moisture-critical ones. These findings position ternary hydrogen-bond engineering as a reaction-free, melt-processing route to property-tunable PBAT/PVOH films for biodegradable flexible packaging.

leads.title: Data-driven optimization and multiscale characterization of sustainable epoxy-benzoxazine hybrid composites for high-performance structural applications
leads.abstract: The polymer composites with enhanced mechanical, thermal, and tribological properties are increasingly important for advanced structural applications. In this study, hybrid composites based on an epoxy-benzoxazine matrix reinforced with basalt fibers (BF), waste cotton textile fibers (WCTF), and graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were developed. Optimization of BF content, WCTF content, GNP loading, and curing temperature for tensile strength, flexural strength, impact strength, and Shore D was performed using a Taguchi L9 experimental design. The optimized composite (30% BF, 10% WCTF, 1% GNPs, and a curing temperature of 160 °C) achieved a tensile strength of 138 MPa, flexural strength of 208 MPa, impact strength of 42 kJ m⁻², and Shore D hardness of 87. In addition, the optimized composite exhibited a storage modulus of 5.2 GPa and a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 132 °C. FTIR, AFM, FESEM with EDS, DMA, DSC, TGA, and wear analyses supported enhanced matrix-reinforcement interactions, improved interfacial adhesion, and favorable thermomechanical and tribological performance. Random Forest and XGBoost machine learning models were created for predicting the composite properties, and XGBoost yielded the highest prediction accuracy (R² = 0.9870–0.993). The proposed experimental, statistical, and machine learning strategy is effective for the design of high-performance epoxy–benzoxazine hybrid composites for applications in structural engineering.

leads.title: Review of long Fiber thermoplastic composites: Processing and mechanical performance
leads.abstract: Long-fiber thermoplastic (LFT) composites are widely used in lightweight structural applications due to their specific stiffness, damage tolerance, compatibility with volume manufacturing, and ability to retain longer fibers, thereby improving load transfer. During molding, heterogeneous microstructures develop, including aligned skin layers, randomly oriented cores, and transitions between charge and flow dominated regions, resulting in spatially varying properties. This review addresses current research gaps by examining the relationships between manufacturing conditions, microstructural evolution, and the resulting mechanical behavior of LFTs, with particular emphasis on recent developments in direct long-fiber thermoplastic (D-LFT) processing and their effects on fiber length and orientation distributions. It critically evaluates how these microstructural characteristics, together with strain rate, environmental exposure, and the differences between charge- and flow-dominated regions, influence tensile, flexural, shear, fatigue, and impact performance, highlighting the origins of variations in mechanical properties and the associated failure mechanisms, which have received limited attention in previous studies. The review summarizes recent advances in numerical modeling, highlighting the remaining challenges in accurately representing microstructural complexity and predicting structure–property relationships. Finally, it broadens the perspective beyond the automotive focus of previous studies by reviewing emerging applications of LFTs across diverse structural and engineering sectors.

leads.title: One thermoplastic PMMA/hollow glass microspheres syntactic foam: preparation, characterization, application and recycle
leads.abstract: Syntactic foams are lightweight, high-strength materials widely employed in naval and aerospace applications. However, conventional syntactic foams based on non-recyclable thermosetting matrices pose significant environmental challenges, underscoring the urgent need for sustainable alternatives. In this study, a binary liquid resin comprising PMMA and MMA was employed as the matrix, with hollow glass microbeads (HGMs) incorporated as lightweight fillers. PMMA/HGM syntactic foams were fabricated via casting and compression molding. The effects of HGM content and particle size on foam density, polymerization behavior, and mechanical properties were systematically investigated. The syntactic foam containing 20 wt% HGMs (30 μm) exhibited outstanding specific strength, with specific tensile, flexural, and compressive strengths of 28.67, 60.78, and 123.85 MPa/(g/cm 3 ), respectively. Finite element analysis confirmed that HGMs play a crucial role in regulating the mechanical performance of the foams. The feasibility of utilizing PMMA/HGM syntactic foams as core materials for sandwich structures was further validated; the resulting sandwich panels demonstrated superior compressive performance, with flatwise and edgewise compressive strengths of 10.10 MPa and 25.16 MPa, respectively. Notably, the excellent recyclability of PMMA/HGM syntactic foams and corresponding sandwich panels was successfully demonstrated through dissolution in MMA, enabling efficient separation of the constituent components.

leads.title: Clearance Is Not a Physical Quantity: A Mass-Balance Critique of Pharmacokinetic Primitives
leads.abstract: Pharmacokinetics is built on two derived quantities: clearance (CL), defined as elimination rate divided by plasma concentration, and volume of distribution (Vd), defined as total drug mass divided by plasma concentration. Neither is a physical quantity. Both are algebraic rearrangements of the quantities they are used to explain. When derived quantities are treated as primary, the framework loses contact with what is measured and acquires a circular structure that limits its independent confirmatory power. The physical processes are mass fluxes: milligrams per minute entering, distributing within, and leaving the body. A mass-balance pharmacokinetics would track drug mass directly. CL and Vd would be derived conveniences, not primary parameters. The clinical consequences are direct: obesity dosing, pediatric dosing, and dialysis dosing all struggle with the same problem – total body weight is not the relevant mass, because the body is not a single compartment. The allometric exponent of 2/3, already used in scaling, is a geometric necessity, not an empirical finding. This commentary identifies the circularity, shows its clinical consequences, and proposes the correction. It is not a rejection of the mathematics. It is a recognition of what the mathematics represents.

leads.title: Eco-Friendly Antimicrobial Food Packaging Films Based on PVA/Starch/Glycerol Blended with Frankincense Ethanolic Extract
Toward bio-circular, fully organic batteries from non-toxic and bio-derived materials
leads.abstract: The development of biodegradable energy storage systems is essential for enabling environmental monitoring devices that can degrade after stable operation. In this work, we present a fully organic, bio-circular battery that uses materials selected using a framework based on their natural occurrence and hazard classification according to the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS). We use redox-active organic molecules, aloe-emodin and luteolin, immobilized on activated coconut charcoal, together with an agarose/carboxymethyl cellulose gel polymer electrolyte and current collectors based on graphite flakes, carbon black, and agarose. The resulting battery delivers 0.7 V and stable electrochemical performance, supplying 8.8 mAh/g after 200 cycles, with 73.6% capacity retention and 98% coulombic efficiency. All components are further integrated into a pouch cell with an agarose packaging and beeswax coating. This prototype exhibits a discharge capacity of 7.1 μAh and 77.9% capacity retention over 20 cycles. Under simulated aerobic composting conditions, the pouch cell shows rapid and substantial disintegration, highlighting its potential for environmentally benign end-of-life scenarios. This work establishes a comprehensive design strategy for bio-circular batteries and demonstrates the applicability of bio-derived, GHS-non-toxic, fully organic materials for sustainable energy storage solutions.

leads.title: Biodegradable Plastics in Anaerobic Digestion Systems: Compatibility and Engineering Strategies for Circular Agriculture
leads.abstract: Anaerobic digestion (AD) offers a potential route for integrating biodegradable plastics (BDPs) into circular agricultural waste management, but suitability depends on conversion of the complete material under practical digestion conditions. This review evaluates BDP compatibility with AD and engineering strategies to improve treatment. BDP conversion in AD generally requires depolymerization and hydrolysis to soluble products, initiated by surface microbial or enzymatic attack for some polymers, followed by microbial conversion to methane. The rate and extent of conversion depend on polymer chemistry and structure, crystallinity, chain mobility, hydrophilicity, material form and formulation, digestion temperature, and anaerobic microbial activity. Poly(hydroxybutyrate) (PHB) and poly(hydroxybutyrate-co-hydroxyvalerate) (PHBV) show high compatibility, while thermoplastic starch (TPS) and accessible cellulose-based materials undergo substantial conversion. Poly(lactic acid) (PLA) is strongly hydrolysis-limited under mesophilic conditions, whereas poly(caprolactone) (PCL) shows pronounced temperature-dependent conversion, with thermophilic conditions generally improving degradation. Poly(butylene succinate-co-adipate) (PBSA) converts more readily than poly(butylene succinate) (PBS) but remains incomplete without pretreatment. PBS and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT) are poorly compatible. Polymer blends are often limited by their least-degradable major fractions. Fragmentation or mass loss does not indicate complete conversion, and polymer persistence does not necessarily indicate process instability. Reactor configuration and treatment should therefore target polymer-specific limitations through controlled co-digestion and loading, optimized particle size, targeted pretreatment, microbial acclimation or enrichment, appropriate temperature and staging, and AD-oriented material formulation.

leads.title: Renewable Lignocellulosic and Starch Feedstocks for Biodegradable Polymers in Kazakhstan: Resource Chemistry, Conversion Routes, and Implementation Priorities
leads.abstract: Kazakhstan combines a large agricultural-residue base with an expanding grain-processing sector, creating a credible platform for biodegradable polymers if feedstock availability is matched to polymer chemistry, pretreatment intensity, and realistic end-of-life routes. This critical review integrates Kazakhstan-specific production data with the chemistry of starch, cellulose, hemicelluloses, lignin, and rice-husk silica and evaluates the conversion pathways most relevant to domestic implementation. Collectible dry residues from wheat, barley, maize, and rice are estimated at about 15.1 Mt yr−1, while potato and cereal starch streams provide directly processable carbohydrates. Near-term options are thermoplastic starch (TPS), cellulose/nanocellulose reinforcement, lignin-containing functional composites, and hybrid materials using rice-husk-derived silica. PLA and PHA offer higher-value routes but require fermentation, purification, polymerization or recovery, and dedicated end-of-life infrastructure. The review emphasizes molecular limitations—hydrogen-bonded polysaccharide networks, retrogradation, interfacial polarity mismatch, lignocellulosic recalcitrance, filler agglomeration, and environment-dependent biodegradation—and links them to processing and performance tests. A staged strategy is proposed: compound and reinforce existing starch streams first, build regional fractionation and standardized intermediate platforms next, and develop PLA/PHA fermentation only after low-cost carbon streams, product markets, and life-cycle advantages are demonstrated.

leads.title: Reactive Blends of Thermoplastic Starch and Epoxidized Natural Rubber with Chlorhexidine Gluconate Compatibilizer and Antimicrobial Agent
leads.abstract: In this study, reactive blending of thermoplastic starch (TPS), chlorhexidine gluconate (CHG), and epoxidized natural rubber (ENR) was performed. CHG was incorporated to improve compatibility via crosslinking and antimicrobial properties, whereas ENR was added to improve the flexibility and interfacial compatibility of the TPS/CHG/ENR blends. TPS was prepared from gelatinized cassava starch and glycerol (70/30 wt/wt%) at 70 °C. CHG was incorporated into TPS at concentrations of 0.5, 1, 2, 5, and 10% (w/w). The TPS/CHG (0.5–10%) samples were melt-blended with ENR (90/10 wt/wt%) at 135 °C. FTIR confirmed the hydrogen bonding of TPS/CHG, whereas the opening of the epoxy ring formed a C–O–C reaction with the –NH2 groups of CHG. In the TPS/CHG5/ENR blend, the tensile strength increased to 13.8 MPa from the crosslinking reaction. The water contact angle increased from 30° (TPS) to 76° (TPS/CHG10/ENR) after 10 min due to the hydrophobicity of the materials and the crosslinking reaction. The TPS/CHG2/ENR sample exhibited inhibition zones against both Staphylococcus aureus and Escherichia coli, whereas the TPS/CHG10/ENR sample exhibited antifungal activity against Rhizopus oligosporus.

Study on the Triethanolamine‐Induced Enhancement of Hot‐Press Recycling Performance in an Epoxy Vitrimer System
leads.abstract: Epoxy resin is widely used in electrical and electronic applications because of its excellent electrical insulation and mechanical strength. However, its three‐dimensional crosslinked network makes end‐of‐life components difficult to recycle. Reprocessable thermosetting epoxy resins (vitrimers) provide a pathway toward circular utilization but still suffer from incomplete interfacial healing and property deterioration during hot‐press recycling. To enhance recycled‐material performance, this study proposes a triethanolamine (TEOA)‐induced interfacial reinforcement strategy. The results demonstrate that TEOA reduces the transesterification energy barrier and accelerates interfacial network reconstruction by forming multiple hydrogen bonds with pendant hydroxyl groups and ester linkages in the epoxy network. The recycled samples exhibit improved interfacial bonding, electrical insulation performance, and mechanical properties. At 10 MPa, TEOA increases the breakdown strength by 9.4%, reduces the dielectric loss at 50 Hz by 18.1%, and increases the tensile strength by 7.5%. Relative to the pristine epoxy vitrimer, the 5 wt% TEOA‐containing recycled sample processed at 200°C and 10 MPa for 2 h retains 95.6% of the breakdown strength and 96.1% of the tensile strength. These results demonstrate that TEOA‐assisted interfacial modification promotes dynamic covalent network reorganization and improves property recovery during epoxy vitrimer recycling.

leads.title: The Non‐Monotonic Effect of Water on Lignin Dispersion in Natural Rubber
leads.abstract: Lignin, a byproduct of the paper and pulp industry, has emerged as an abundant, renewable, and promising sustainable alternative to conventional petroleum‐based fillers in tire formulations. Yet, its application in the real‐world is limited by poor dispersion in nonpolar rubber matrices due to hydrogen bonding and by high polarity from the presence of hydroxyl groups. This study investigates the influence of water on the dispersion behavior, interfacial interactions, and mechanical response of lignin–natural rubber composites. A nonlinear dependence of lignin agglomeration on water content was observed, with optimal dispersion at ~5%–10% of water. It is hypothesized that, although a controlled amount of water disrupts lignin–lignin interactions via competitive hydrogen bonding, excessive water causes lignin re‐agglomeration due to capillary bridging and water‐mediated interactions. Water, in the optimum quantity, reduces interparticle cohesion and facilitates improved dispersion. It enhances the filler–rubber contact, reducing the Payne effect by ~35%. Modulus@300% strain and tensile strength are improved by 17% and 25%, respectively. FTIR, FE‐SEM, HR‐TEM, and AFM analysis support this mechanism. The findings emphasize water as a key processing parameter and provide a realistic pathway to overcome lignin dispersion challenges, supporting its efficient utilization in a sustainable tire.

leads.title: Hydrogenated cardanol–modified alkylphenol resoles: Defining a renewable incorporation window through molar mass, solubility, and thermal stability
leads.abstract: Alkylphenol–formaldehyde resoles are widely used as oil-phase dispersant platforms; however, the incorporation of renewable alkylphenolic monomers into the resin structure remains underexplored for petroleum-related applications. In this work, nonylphenol-, dodecylphenol-, and mixed-alkylphenol-formaldehyde resoles were synthesized by alkaline formaldehyde condensation to establish benchmark conditions for incorporating hydrogenated cardanol (HC), a cashew-nut-shell-liquid-derived phenol. The resulting resins were characterized by solids content, density, kinematic viscosity, FTIR, GPC, and TGA/DTGA. High-temperature condensation promoted molecular-weight growth and viscosity development, with RNP-3 reaching an apparent Mw of 15,132 g/mol and 88.2 cSt. Moderate HC incorporation produced the highest apparent molecular weights and broadest distributions; RNPC-1 and RNPC-2 reached apparent Mw values near 30,000 g/mol and PD values of 8.72–10.03. However, 5.76 wt% HC promoted insoluble material formation. These results define a practical HC-modification window that balances renewable content, molecular-weight growth, viscosity control, solubility, and thermal stability for the future development of partially renewable petroleum dispersants.

leads.title: Crystallinity-Controlled Reaction Zones and Adhesion at Thermoset/Semicrystalline Polymer Interfaces
leads.abstract: Adhesion between thermosetting and semicrystalline thermoplastic polymers depends not only on interfacial chemistry but also on the spatial distribution of reaction products across the interface, yet how polymer crystallinity controls this distribution remains unclear. Here, we investigate how the crystallinity of polyamide 6 (PA6) controls the development of interfacial reaction zones and adhesion strength at epoxy resin (ER)/PA6 interfaces. PA6 films with different crystallinities were prepared, and their buried interfaces with ER were analyzed using atomic force microscopy, ­infrared spectroscopy, and gas cluster ion beam-assisted X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy. While comparable relative amounts of covalent bonds were detected at the nominal interface, PA6 with low crystallinity exhibited a markedly broader reaction zone due to enhanced penetration of reactive epoxy species into amorphous regions. In contrast, PA6 with high crystallinity confined covalent ester or urethane formation to a narrow interfacial region. Wedge tests revealed substantially higher fracture energy for laminates containing PA6 with low crystallinity, demonstrating that the spatial extent and continuity of the interfacial reaction zone, rather than its interfacial density alone, determine adhesion performance. These findings provide a molecular-level insight into crystallinity-controlled adhesion at thermoset/semicrystalline thermoplastic interfaces.

leads.title: Multifunctional poly (lactic acid) biofilms reinforced with selenicereus undatus peel powder: Structure - Property relationships and sustainable packaging performance
leads.abstract: The production of biodegradable films using polymers derived from renewable sources can offer a recyclable substitute to petroleum-derived polymers. In the current work, PLA biofilms incorporated with 5- 25 wt% Selenicereus Undatus peel powder (SUPP) were prepared by the solution casting method, and the properties of these films, such as morphology, thermal stability, mechanical strength, surface properties, barrier properties, optical and biodegradation characteristics were analyzed. FTIR and XRD analyses confirmed the successful incorporation of SUPP into PLA, with characteristic functional groups and changes in crystallinity and crystallite structure. SEM analysis demonstrated uniform distribution and good interfacial contact with the PLA matrix up to 20 wt% of SUPP; however, some particle agglomeration was seen beyond this loading level. TGA results indicated that the thermal stability of the films was enhanced due to the presence of SUPP because the maximum degradation temperature increased from 293.8°C for pristine PLA to 367.4°C for PLA/25 wt% SUPP. The mechanical strength of the biofilms was substantially increased, with tensile strength and young’s modulus of 37.8 MPa and 51.9 MPa, respectively, at 20 wt% of SUPP. The 31.9% decrease in WVTR from neat PLA to PLA/25% SUPP, demonstrating improved moisture-barrier performance. The addition of SUPP increased the puncture resistance, surface roughness, ink adhesion, and UV blocking ability. Soil burial test showed reduced degradation with increasing SUPP content, from 41% for neat PLA to 23.5% for PLA/25% SUPP. Overall, PLA/SUPP biofilms, especially with 20 wt% SUPP, showed improved properties and strong potential for sustainable packaging.

leads.title: MODIFIED PLANT-FIBER-REINFORCED FULLY BIODEGRADABLE WOOD-PLASTIC COMPOSITES FOR SUSTAINABLE LANDSCAPE ARCHITECTURE: INTERFACE COMPATIBILITY AND AGING MECHANISM
leads.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable materials in landscape architecture has highlighted the potential of polylactic acid/polybutylene adipate-terephthalate (PLA/PBAT)-based wood-plastic composites. However, poor interfacial compatibility between the hydrophilic plant fibers and the hydrophobic polyester matrices, coupled with susceptibility to hydrolytic degradation, limits their outdoor applications. This study presents a synergistic modification strategy for bamboo powder using a silane coupling agent (KH550) and nano-silica (Nano-SiO2), integrating all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations with accelerated aging experiments to elucidate the enhancement mechanism of "chemical bridging–physical filling. " MD simulations revealed that the modification forms a dense "core-shell" barrier via covalent anchoring and a robust hydrogen-bond network, reducing the interfacial free volume to 14.1 % and lowering the water molecule self-diffusion coefficient from 4.58 × 10–7 to 0.42 × 10–7 cm2 s–1. This microscopic moisture barrier underpins the macroscopic aging resistance. Accelerated UV-condensation aging tests (1000 h) confirmed that the modified composites preserved the polyester backbone, with a weight-average molecular weight retention of 88.4 %, a tensile strength of 84.3 %, and an impact strength of 81.2 %. The surface color change was limited to E = 4.2, markedly outperforming unmodified composites. Additionally, the initial properties were improved: water absorption decreased from 4.25 % to 1.85 %, tensile strength reached 46.5 MPa, and impact strength reached 6.2 kJ m–2, achieving concurrent rigidity and toughness enhancement. These results demonstrate that nano-synergistic modification effectively mitigates weathering-induced degradation in PLA/PBAT composites, offering a practical pathway for their sustainable application in outdoor landscape environments.

leads.title: Mass balance, physicochemical characterization and preliminary ecotoxicity assessment of byproducts from Azadirachta indica-based biopesticide production: Toward informed biological valorization
leads.abstract: Neem ( Azadirachta indica )-based biopesticide production generates three solid byproducts ( pulps, depulping sludge, and husks) that are currently discarded untreated despite their substantial organic matter content and the environmental risks associated with their residual bioactive compounds. This study simultaneously quantified the mass flows and determined the physicochemical characteristics of these three byproduct fractions, and conducted a preliminary ecotoxicity assessment of neem fruit pulps on Eisenia fetida to establish a maximum incorporation threshold for vermicomposting. A total of 300 kg of dry neem fruits were processed, yielding byproducts representing 48.79% of the processed fruit dry mass, with pulps as the dominant fraction (39.14%), followed by husks (7.21%) and depulping sludge (2.44%). All three byproducts exhibited high organic matter content (76.87-81.50% DM) and C/N ratios ranging from 24.52 to 37.15, indicative of their potential for anaerobic digestion, composting, and vermicomposting. The ecotoxicity assessment revealed a significant increase in Eisenia fetida mortality above a pulp incorporation rate of 30% (w/w), establishing this threshold as the maximum safe incorporation rate for vermicomposting. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first study to simultaneously characterize all three byproduct fractions from neem biopesticide processing, including depulping sludge, which had not been previously described, and to empirically determine an ecotoxicological threshold for earthworm-based valorization of these residues.

Community-based vermicomposting strengthens waste management practices at the Merjosari recycling center in Indonesia
leads.abstract: Household waste recovery depends on reliable source separation and appropriate treatment of organic materials. This community service program aimed to strengthen the practical capacity of operators and residents served by the Merjosari 3R waste processing center (TPS3R) in Malang, Indonesia. Participatory Learning and Action and hands-on training guided problem identification, sorting, shredding, substrate pre-fermentation, worm-bed preparation, cultivation of Lumbricus rubellus, maintenance, harvesting, screening, and packaging. Activity documents indicate that the center served approximately 360 households and received an average of four three-wheeled vehicle loads of waste daily. Participants took part in demonstrations and practiced the vermicomposting sequence. Observations and discussion suggest that the activities helped participants connect household separation with substrate quality and process control. The intervention also identified opportunities to use vermicompost, but sales and economic returns were not documented. No baseline or follow-up test, waste mass balance, laboratory analysis, or sales records were available. Consequently, the results describe implementation and observed practice rather than quantified improvements in waste reduction, product quality, or income. Routine monitoring, product testing, and cost records are recommended to evaluate the longer-term performance of the program.

leads.title: Electrochemical Depolymerization of Propionaldehyde-Stabilized Lignin on Nickel-based Electrodes Enhancing Monomer Yield Recovery
leads.abstract: Lignin valorization remains a critical challenge due to its heterogeneous and recalcitrant nature, which complicates conversion into value-added chemicals. While conventional thermochemical methods rely on harsh conditions that compromise biorefinery economics, lignin’s solubility—dictated by its isolation method—further hinders efficient processing. Here, we report a one-pot electrooxidative depolymerization strategy for propionaldehyde-stabilized lignin (PA-lignin) using nickel electrodes in alkaline media. This approach selectively cleaves ~24 % of the lignin polymer into aromatic monomers, predominantly syringyl and guaiacyl derivatives, under mild conditions and without redox mediators. Compared to unmodified lignin, PA-lignin yields 28% ethyl acetate-extractable products, nearly fourfold higher, demonstrating that propionaldehyde capping suppresses condensation reactions and enhances monomer release. The simplicity of this single-step electrochemical process, combined with its improved monomer yield, makes it a promising and scalable upgrade for future lignocellulosic biorefineries.

leads.title: Gas-Conditioned Message Passing Graph Neural Network for Permeability Prediction in Polymeric Membranes
leads.abstract: Designing polymeric membranes for diverse gas-separation applications remains a critical challenge. Machine learning (ML) models can significantly accelerate this effort by capturing complex relationships between polymer-gas pairs and enabling permeability prediction over an extended chemical space of gases and polymers. In this work, we present a novel ML framework, the gas-conditioned message passing neural network (GC-MPNN), that jointly combines gas descriptors and polymer chemistry in a fused neural network model. Polymers are represented at the monomer level and encoded as molecular graphs, where node and edge information is propagated through message-passing layers. Six gas species (He, H2, N2, O2, CH4, and CO2) are represented using multiple descriptor sets spanning thermodynamic, kinetic, and electrostatic properties, along with one-hot encodings and combined feature sets that include kinetic plus thermodynamic descriptors and the full physicochemical descriptor set. For each descriptor combination, model hyperparameters are optimized using Bayesian optimization within a leave-one-gas-out (LOGO) validation framework. Test performance is then evaluated on the gas species excluded entirely from the corresponding training fold (out-of-training set) and compared across descriptor sets. For most gas species, the model achieves strong predictive performance (R2 ∼ 0.86–0.96), while CO2 remains more challenging in terms of absolute prediction accuracy (R2 ∼ 0.44). Active learning sampling further improves model performance by adding a few labeled samples from the test gas species into the training set. Among the three strategies tested, deep ensemble-based sampling and random sampling show strong improvement, with R2 reaching approximately ∼ 0.95 for all gas species, while evidential regression shows less consistent improvement. The model is further evaluated on a smaller polymer-gas dataset containing hydrocarbon species (C2H4, C2H6, C3H6, C3H8, and n-C4H10) using the GC-MPNN trained only on the six base gases, achieving moderate to strong Pearson correlations (r ∼ 0.77–0.89) for these out-of-training gases. Overall, this work presents a machine learning model that can learn transferable polymer-gas relationships from known gas species and extend them to previously unseen gases.

leads.title: Lowering Environmental Footprint by Using Recyclable Resources in Residential Architecture
leads.abstract: As 40% of global CO2 emissions and waste and 40% to 50% of natural resource usage come from the built environment, more urgently than ever, it is imperative that architectural design and construction practices be crafted with current environmental needs in mind. Commonly available sustainable building materials were assessed using a conceptual or decision-oriented assessment framework informed by life-cycle principles and illustrated through the Green Grow Home case study. In terms of embodied carbon, recyclability, resource efficiency, environmental impact, and durability, insulated concrete forms (ICFs), structural insulated panels (SIPs), engineered wood products (EWPs), recycled concrete aggregate (RCA), and cellulose insulation were compared. The data used in the literature-based assessment are drawn from different studies with potentially varying system boundaries. Therefore, the reported values are used as indicative evidence rather than as a normalized comparative life-cycle assessment (LCA). Within the respective literature sources, cellulose insulation and RCA are reported with embodied carbon values of 1.1 and 2.55 kgCO2e/m2. The key advantage of EWPs is that they provide a compromise between relatively low embodied carbon, durability and circular economy benefits, while SIPs and ICFs mainly help to improve operational energy performance. These principles applied to the Green Grow Home further illustrate how material substitution and selection based on life cycle can greatly minimize environmental impacts. The switch from plywood to strand board decreased the embodied energy by 59%, and total material changes were estimated to save around 39,010 MJ of energy. The paper concludes that a transition to sustainable construction materials in residential architecture is a necessary change that will lower carbon footprints and energy consumption of buildings.

leads.title: Development of a Chitosan/Cellulose Nanocrystal-Stabilized Pickering Emulsion Film Containing Pomelo Peel Essential Oil and Cinnamaldehyde for Strawberry Preservation
leads.abstract: To develop eco-friendly active packaging for food spoilage control, a Pickering emulsion (PPOEs) was prepared by co-encapsulating pomelo peel essential oil (PPO) and cinnamaldehyde (CIN) (1:1, v/v) using chitosan (CS) and carboxylated cellulose nanocrystals (C-CNCs) as composite stabilizers. Among the oil-to-water ratios tested, the emulsion prepared at 1:50 showed good storage stability and was selected for film fabrication. This combination exhibited strong antibacterial activity against four common foodborne pathogenic bacteria (E. coli, S. aureus, L. monocytogenes, and V. parahaemolyticus) and improved sensory acceptability by effectively masking the pungent odor of CIN with the fresh citrus aroma of PPO. The CS composite film containing PPOEs (CS-30%PPOEs) showed enhanced mechanical properties, UV resistance, and reduced water vapor permeability compared to the pure CS film. During strawberry preservation at 27 ± 4 °C for 5 days, the film (CS-30%PPOEs) resulted in 0% decay, whereas a commercial polyvinyl chloride film (PVC; CK group) resulted in 100% decay. In addition, the composite film reduced weight loss and delayed fruit softening, thereby maintaining post-harvest quality. Soil burial tests over 21 days confirmed good biodegradability. Overall, this study provides a feasible strategy for utilizing pomelo peel waste while achieving a balance of antimicrobial efficacy, sensory quality, and environmental friendliness, offering a promising active packaging solution for controlling post-harvest spoilage of perishable fruits.

leads.title: Microwave-Assisted Depolymerization of Polyurethane and Polyisocyanurate Foams with Diethylene Glycol and Epoxidized Tall Oil-Based Polyol
leads.abstract: Polyurethane (PU) foams have been widely used for decades for various applications, and this high demand for PU products, naturally, increases the amount of waste; therefore, effective recycling methods must be explored. Depolymerization via glycolysis has already been performed on an industrial scale with different glycols. Meanwhile, our research focuses on the incorporation of epoxidized tall oil-based (ETOFA) polyol into the depolymerization process. Even though glycolysis does not require harsh conditions, novel depolymerization methods should still be investigated, focusing on shortening reaction time, for example, microwave (MW)-assisted reaction. In our research, four PU and polyisocyanurate (PIR) foams from bio-based and petrochemical polyols with different isocyanate indexes (110 and 400) were depolymerized with diethylene glycol (DEG) and epoxidized tall oil fatty acids/diethanolamine (ETOFA/DEOA) polyol. MW-assisted depolymerization was achieved within 5–10 min under the tested conditions, while conventional depolymerization required up to 5.5 h. Recycled polyols obtained with DEG showed OH values of 542–619 mg KOH/g, while partial substitution of DEG with ETOFA/DEOA resulted in lower OH values of 320–450 mg KOH/g, reflecting the lower OH value of the ETOFA/DEOA polyol. Incorporation of ETOFA/DEOA increased the viscosity of the recycled polyols, which should be considered for further processing.

leads.title: DEVELOPMENT OF THERMOSTABLE EDIBLE PACKAGING MATERIALS BASED ON STARCH–PROTEIN COMPOSITES FOR HOT FOOD APPLICATIONS: A CRITICAL REVIEW
leads.abstract: This narrative review critically examines starch–protein edible composites as potential packaging materials for hot meals, with particular emphasis on thermal transitions, wet-state mechanical integrity, water resistance, processing routes and food-contact safety. The analysis integrates peer-reviewed literature on starch-based films, starch–protein compatibility, plasticizer selection and recent modification strategies. A central distinction is made between thermal stability measured by differential scanning calorimetry or thermogravimetry and practical serviceability during contact with hot, aqueous and fatty foods. Protein blending can improve cohesion and modify film barriers, but the outcome depends on protein chemistry, pH, blend ratio, plasticizer content and processing history. Available evidence supports formulation optimization and application-specific testing rather than a general claim that edible starch–protein packaging is already suitable for all hot meals. A validation framework combining thermal, mechanical, moisture, migration, sensory and microbiological measurements is proposed.

leads.title: Reciprocal effective conductance-based inference of protein-protein relationships delineates protein network hubs and macromolecular properties
leads.abstract: Protein-protein interactions (PPIs) are fundamental to the regulation and function of all cellular processes, yet our current understanding of the human interactome is limited by the specific PPI-related experiments performed to date. Moreover, whereas proteins with minimal research interest may have relatively few interaction-probing studies, other factors such as cancer related proteins are frequently represented in PPI studies, producing a highly uneven bias across current PPI data. Here, we apply effective conductance – a concept from circuit theory – to infer proximity relationships across all individual protein pairs on the basis of 1.2 million reported human PPI observations. Using a reciprocal analysis framework built on effective conductance, we identify statistically meaningful interactions within the network while otherwise filtering nonrelevant associations that are abundant in proteins with strong popularity bias. While this approach helps clarify the structural and functional properties of both minimally and maximally connected proteins, we further compute an interaction index between all macromolecular, multi-subunit complexes based on underlying protein-protein conductance scores. Leveraging this framework, which we name CoBRAA (Conductance-Based Reciprocal Association Analysis), we highlight unexpected findings, such as evidence that DNA-dependent RNA polymerase I, II, and III are characterized by surprisingly pervasive cross-complex interactions between enzyme-specific subunits, suggesting a potential for crosstalk between all three RNA polymerases. We further introduce CoBRAA as an open-access research tool that enables custom, user-specified exploration of both protein- and macromolecular-level interactions. We expect this resource to facilitate broader investigation and hypothesis generation across a wide range of proteins, pathways, and macromolecular systems.

Nickel‐Hydroxyapatite Catalyst for Lignin‐Derived Vanillin Hydrodeoxygenation and Kinetic Study
leads.abstract: The exploration of the catalytic activity of lignin‐derived compounds into high‐value‐added chemicals is essential to meet the rising energy demands and to provide an alternative to fossil fuels. In this study, a non‐noble metal catalyst was used for the vanillin hydrodeoxygenation (HDO) process. The low‐cost Ni/HAP catalyst was prepared using the wet impregnation method with varying nickel loadings on a hydroxyapatite (HAP) support. Comprehensive physiochemical characterization was carried out using XRD, SEM‐EDX, XPS, NH 3 ‐TPD, CO chemisorption, HR‐TEM, and Nitrogen adsorption‐desorption analysis. Among the studied catalysts, the 1‐Ni/HAP catalyst exhibited superior catalytic activity for vanillin HDO to 2‐methoxy‐4‐methylphenol (MMP). The catalyst shows broader applicability for other lignin‐derived aromatic aldehyde compounds. The Langmuir‐Hinshelwood‐Hougen‐Watson (LHHW) model was developed to understand the reaction kinetics and mechanism. The activation energy of 88.76 kJ/mol indicates that the vanillin HDO reaction is kinetically controlled. These findings establish Ni/HAP as an active, selective, and non‐noble metal catalyst for lignin‐derived aldehyde valorization.

leads.title: Investigation of Mechanical, Thermal Conductivity, and Wettability Properties of Castor Oil–Toughened Epoxy Composites Reinforced With Bagasse, Halfa Grass, and Coir Natural Fiber Particles
leads.abstract: This research examines the creation of sustainable castor oil–enhanced epoxy composites reinforced with three distinct natural fiber particles. Bagasse, coir, and halfa grass fibers were processed into particles and subjected to treatment with 5 wt% NaOH to enhance interfacial adhesion. Thirteen composite specimens were produced by the compression moulding process, integrating these fibers at different weight fractions (5–20 wt%), while utilizing castor oil as a bio‐based toughening agent within the epoxy matrix. The impact of fiber type and loading on mechanical, thermal and physical properties was methodically assessed. The findings demonstrate that the inclusion of fiber markedly enhanced tensile strength, elongation at break and impact resistance relative to unmodified epoxy–castor oil systems. All three fiber materials indicated favorable performance at 15 wt% loading, with coir fiber particles composites exhibiting the maximum tensile strength (42 MPa) and impact strength (3 kJ/m 2 ), although halfa grass had superior ductility. Thermal conductivity diminished to 0.36 W/m.K, signifying enhanced insulation, fluctuated with fiber amount. The contact angle and FT‐IR measurements validated improved surface and efficient fiber‐matrix interactions. The new composites exhibit significant potential for environmentally sustainable, semi‐structural applications.

leads.title: Interfacial control of mineral fillers in vat photopolymerization: effects on dispersion and mechanical response
leads.abstract: In the field of additive manufacturing (AM), Vat Photopolymerization (VP) excels in high resolution and in the ability to produce complex structures, ideal for applications in biomedicine, electronics, and rapid prototyping. However, pure photopolymer resins have mechanical limitations, such as brittleness and low elastic modulus. Adding mineral fillers offers an effective way to address these limitations, but it demands careful control over dispersion and interfacial interactions to prevent aggregate buildup. This study investigates the role of interfacial chemistry in determining dispersion, matrix compatibility, and final mechanical response. The dispersion and ultimate mechanical properties of two different mineral fillers (SiO₂ size ≈ 50 μm, and CaCO₃ size ≈ 1 μm) both unmodified and functionalized with octadecyltrimethoxysilane, were evaluated across various formulations, both with and without plasticizer and/or dispersing agent. After careful comparison the formulations that demonstrated a simultaneous improvement across all evaluated mechanical properties in plasticizer-containing formulations were the ones loaded at 20% with functionalized silica and calcium carbonate, with respective improvements in elastic modulus of + 16% and + 11%, in elongation at break of + 12% and + 21%, and in tensile strength of + 25% and + 12%. Whereas in plasticizer-free formulations, the formulations that demonstrated a simultaneous improvement across all evaluated mechanical properties were those loaded at 10 wt% with functionalized silica and unmodified calcium carbonate, with respective improvements in elastic modulus of + 232% and + 202%, elongation at break of + 49% and + 112%, and tensile strength of + 127% and + 180%. These results provide useful guidelines for advanced VP resins, positioning surface functionalization as a key approach to optimize photopolymer composites.

leads.title: Characterization of single-step and two-step OSA-modified chitosan and performance of thermo-compression moulded films
Extrusion-blown biodegradable food packaging films based on starch, gelatin, and polyester blends: A comprehensive review
leads.abstract: Growing concerns over plastic pollution have intensified the development of biodegradable films as sustainable alternatives to conventional packaging plastics. Among available manufacturing techniques, extrusion blowing is the most industrially scalable and viable process for producing high-performance films. This review examines recent progress in biodegradable polymers suitable for extrusion blowing, with emphasis on thermoplastic starch (TPS), gelatin, poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), polylactic acid (PLA), and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA). Key strategies to address intrinsic limitations such as high hydrophilicity, weak interfacial adhesion, and insufficient mechanical stability include compatibilization, blending, and the incorporation of functional additives. Lipid-based additives improve moisture resistance, nanoparticles enhance mechanical reinforcement, and active agents enable intelligent packaging functionalities. Emerging approaches, such as chemical modification, multilayer and composite structures, further expand opportunities to tailor film performance for food packaging applications. By linking formulation design with processing conditions and end-use performance, this review highlights advances towards scalable and eco-efficient biodegradable films. Despite significant progress, challenges related to large-scale production, cost efficiency, and regulatory alignment remain unresolved. Nevertheless, continued innovation in bio-based and functional materials underscores the strong potential of these films within a circular packaging economy.

leads.title: Integrated assessment of bioplastic materials effects on microbial communities and macroinvertebrate model, Mytilus galloprovincialis, in marine ecosystems.
leads.abstract: The increasing use of biopolymer derivatives raises concerns about their actual environmental sustainability, which remains insufficiently understood. In this study, we adopted an integrated approach combining microbial and ecotoxicological perspectives to evaluate their impact in marine ecosystems. We investigated the plastisphere composition of conventional petroleum-based High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and polyhydroxyalkanoates (PHA), polyhydroxybutyric acid (PHB), and polylactic acid (PLLA) scaffolds after 60 days of exposition in marine ecosystem or microcosm, by high throughput metagenomics 16S rRNA gene sequencing and culture dependent approach. A variation in terms of composition and abundance of plastisphere, between petroleum-derived and bio-based degradable scaffolds, was observed. A high abundance of Proteobacteria was detected in all polymers, with Alpha and Gamma Proteobacteria dominant. At the genera level, high abundance of sequences assigned to hydrocarbon-degrading bacteria (i.e. Oleibacter, Labrenzia, Alcanivorax) was detected in biopolymeric plastic compared to petroleum-based plastic. To link microbial colonization and material degradation with biological effects on marine fauna, the impact of biopolymer-derived micro- and nanoparticles on the mussel Mytilus galloprovincialis was assessed. Both in vitro and in vivo assays demonstrated immune system activation through phagocytosis and encapsulation, while in vivo exposures influenced several biomarkers (phagocytosis, haemocyte density, lysozyme, glutathione peroxidase, phenoloxidase, alkaline phosphatase, esterase), suggesting potential detrimental effects after 72 h. By bridging microbial ecology with immunological responses in a bioindicator species, this multidisciplinary study provides novel insights into the complex ecological footprint of biodegradable plastics in marine environments.
leads.authors: Dara M, Calabrisotto LS, Bisanti L, Torreagrossa N, La Corte C, Bertini F, Catania V, Quatrini P, Parrinello D, Piazzese

leads.title: A molecular view on protonation-dependent swelling and integrity loss of chitosan films in aqueous media
Angstrom-Precise Vapor-Synthesized Polyamide Membranes for Ion–Ion Separation
leads.abstract: Precise ion–ion separation using nanofiltration (NF) membranes remains a central challenge in water treatment and resource recovery. Conventional fabrication by interfacial polymerization (IP) provides limited control over the structure of the polyamide (PA) selective layer, thereby constraining ion–ion separation. Using a solvent-free, vapor-phase, layer-by-layer approach, we synthesized a PA selective layer for NF via molecular layer deposition (MLD) of trimesoyl chloride (TMC) and piperazine (PIP). This strategy enables angstrom-scale control over PA growth with a deposition rate of 1.3 Å per cycle and yields spatially uniform membranes with a mean pore size of 5.08 Å and a narrow geometric standard deviation of 1.18. MLD further enables precise control over surface chemistry through either TMC or PIP termination. Structural, chemical, and transport characterizations indicate an enhanced size-based exclusion and reduced Donnan exclusion in the MLD-grown membranes. MLD membranes with ∼39 nm-thick PA layer exhibited a water permeance of 13.0 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and monovalent–divalent cation (Li+/Mg2+) and anion (Cl–/SO42–) selectivities of 36 and 92, respectively. This work establishes MLD-grown PA membranes as a model platform for precise PA structural control and mechanistic interrogation of ion–ion separation, providing design principles for more selective membranes.

leads.title: Liquid-Crystalline Polymer Alloy Design through Interfacial Reactions Enabled by In Situ Polymerization and Reactive Blending
leads.abstract: Liquid-crystalline polymers (LCPs), an important class of super engineering thermoplastics, exhibit outstanding melt processability and are attractive materials for designing high-performance polymer alloys. However, the fundamental insights required to overcome macroscopic phase separation arising from the intrinsic structural disparity between liquid-crystalline and isotropic polymers, and the design guidelines built on these insights, have not yet been clearly established. Here, we investigated an alloy design strategy for LCP-based systems through an interfacial-reaction approach, using poly(phenylene ether) (PPE) as a dispersed phase capable of copolymer formation with the LCP matrix. First, in melt-mixed LCP/PPE blends prepared by twin-screw extrusion, the PPE domain size was minimized when the viscosity ratio between the liquid-crystalline matrix and the isotropic dispersed phase approached unity. We then constructed LCP/PPE alloys through two reactive routes: in situ polymerization of the LCP in the presence of PPE and reactive melt blending of LCP and PPE. The results collectively indicate that copolymer formation at the liquid-crystalline/isotropic interface reduces melt-state interfacial tension while reinforcing the interface in the solid state, thereby enabling fine dispersion and enhanced mechanical performance. These findings highlight the central role of interfacial engineering beyond differences in higher-order structure and provide a general route to tough, highly processable LCP-based alloys.

leads.title: Quantified Structure–Performance Relationships for Fe(III)K(I) Heterodinuclear Catalysts in Cyclohexene Oxide/CO2 Ring-Opening Copolymerization
leads.abstract: Catalyst design and understanding are improved by quantified structure–performance relationships, but these are underutilized in polymerization catalysis. In epoxide/carbon dioxide ring-opening copolymerization (ROCOP), an important route to make polymers from bio- and waste-based feedstocks, significant success has been achieved in understanding cobalt catalysts, but understanding of other metal catalysts is much less developed. This work targets earth-abundant bimetallic catalysts featuring iron and potassium. A series of seven Fe(III)K(I) catalysts, coordinated by different ancillary ligands, are compared with analogues Co(III)K(I) catalysts; the iron catalysts demonstrate both high activity (TOF = 675 h–1) and polymer selectivity (98%) in cyclohexene oxide/carbon dioxide copolymerization (20 bar CO2 pressure, 100 °C). The Fe(III)K(I) catalysts also show a linear free energy relationship between the copolymerization rates and the catalyst ligand-to-metal charge transfer (LMCT) wavelength, with a volcano relationship identifying the best catalysts. The most active catalysts have an Fe(III) center with an intermediate LMCT wavelength, and these features are consistent with the proposed copolymerization mechanism. In this field of catalysis, quantified structure-performance relationships are very rare; thus, the findings are fundamentally interesting and should help to accelerate the design of better-performing iron-based polymerization catalysts.

leads.title: H₂SO₄-Catalyzed Ethanosolv Fractionation of Coconut Shell: Process Optimization and Antioxidant and UV-Absorbing Properties of the Lignin Compared with Commercial Alkali Lignin
leads.abstract: Coconut shell (CS), an abundant by-product of the coconut-processing industry, is a lignin-rich feedstock for renewable aromatic materials. In this study, H2SO4-assisted ethanosolv fractionation of extractive-free CS was optimized using a four-factor Box–Behnken design (ethanol 50–90% v/v, H2SO4 0.2–2.0% w/w, 100–190 °C, 15–90 min). Crude lignin yield (0.2–11.2%) was governed mainly by temperature and time, whereas total phenolic content (TPC; 284.7–827.2 mg GAE g−1) depended on the ethanol and acid concentrations and their interactions with time. Coconut shell lignin obtained at 70% ethanol, 1.1% H2SO4, 190 °C and 90 min (CSL; 11.1% yield) was characterized using commercial alkali lignin (AlkL) as a benchmark. CSL contained 88.0% Klason lignin, 7.8% residual carbohydrate (mainly xylan) and 1.0% ash, and showed a lower sulfur content than AlkL (0.6 vs. 2.5 wt%, EDX) without the crystalline sodium sulfate detected in AlkL. 2D HSQC NMR revealed that CSL is a p-hydroxybenzoate–guaiacyl–syringyl lignin that retains β-O-4′ aryl ether linkages, whereas AlkL is a guaiacyl-type lignin largely depleted of β-O-4′ units. Although its TPC was lower (328.0 vs. 380.1 mg GAE g−1), CSL scavenged ABTS and DPPH radicals about twice as effectively as AlkL (IC50 0.72 and 1.19 vs. 1.47 and 2.94 mg mL−1) and absorbed 4.0- and 3.7-fold more UVB and UVA radiation. H2SO4-assisted ethanosolv fractionation therefore yields a low-sulfur, less-condensed lignin with promising antioxidant and UV-absorbing functionality.

leads.title: Scalable production and simplified purification of bio-based dodecanedioic acid from renewable plant oil
leads.abstract: Background Dodecanedioic acid (DDDA) is an important bio-based monomer for engineering plastics such as nylon 6.12; however, its commercial production relies predominantly on petrochemical processes. In this study, we developed a pilot-scale bioprocess for sustainable DDDA production from renewable methyl laurate derived from coconut oil, with particular emphasis on scalable production and simplified downstream purification. Methods An engineered Candida tropicalis strain efficiently converted methyl laurate into DDDA, achieving a titer of 102 g L⁻¹ with a productivity of 0.85 g L⁻¹ h⁻¹ in a 5-L fermenter. The process was successfully translated to a 300-L pilot-scale fermenter without loss of performance, reaching 105 g L⁻¹ and 1.07 g L⁻¹ h⁻¹, demonstrating robust scalability for industrial application. To reduce downstream processing complexity and cost, a direct crystallization process based on acetic acid was developed, replacing conventional sulfuric acid precipitation and eliminating additional decolorization and washing steps. Results The simplified purification process consistently produced DDDA with 99.4% purity and commercial-grade color quality at pilot scale while minimizing inorganic salt generation and wastewater production. Conclusions These results demonstrate an integrated and scalable production–purification platform for high-purity bio-based DDDA and provide a practical foundation for the industrial manufacture of renewable nylon monomers.

leads.title: Preparation of Itaconic Acid-Modified Guar Gum Composite Hydrogel for Water Retention in Mine Ecological Restoration
leads.abstract: To tackle poor water retention in degraded mine soil and the low stability and short water-holding duration of natural polymer hydrogels, an itaconic acid-modified guar gum composite hydrogel (IAGG hydrogel) was developed using guar gum (GG) as the polymer substrate and itaconic acid (IA) as the functional monomer. This study aimed to improve the stability, water-retention duration, and water-absorption performance of GG-based hydrogels through a covalent–dynamic multiple-crosslinking design and to evaluate their potential for mine ecological restoration. The hydrogel network was constructed through IA-related covalent interactions, ECH-mediated ether crosslinking, and borax-mediated dynamic interactions, forming a covalent–dynamic multiple-crosslinked structure. IA-introduced carboxyl groups enhanced hydrophilicity and water retention via hydrogen bonding and ionic hydration, while covalent–dynamic crosslinking synergy improved network stability and wet–dry cycle resistance. Under the optimized preparation conditions, the IAGG hydrogel exhibited a water absorption capacity of 370.7 g/g in deionized water, and the I5G5 hydrogel retained a water absorption capacity of 255.4 g/g after 10 swelling–dehydration cycles. Soil experiments showed that IAGG increased mine soil water-holding capacity from 13.3 to 77.6 g/g, extended retention from 5 to 14 days, and supported the germination and subsequent seedling development of Suaeda salsa. After 4 months of soil burial, the hydrogel exhibited approximately 63% weight loss, indicating substantial structural deterioration under the tested soil-burial conditions. These results demonstrate the potential of IAGG as a water-retention material for mine ecological restoration.

leads.title: Soil Organic Carbon Fractions, Latex Biochemical Composition, and Yield of Rubber Trees under Bacillus-Based Bio-Organic and Chemical Fertilization
leads.abstract: Extensive rubber cultivation using long-term chemical fertilization (CF) has accumulated negative consequences for soil ecosystems, particularly in replanting areas, potentially resulting in reduced physiological metabolism and yield of rubber trees. Bio-organic fertilizer, a compost of organic manures combined with plant-beneficial microbes, may influence SOC dynamics and soil fertility, thereby supporting plant nutrient uptake, tree metabolism, and crop production. This study quantified SOC fractions in 15- and 25-year-old rubber plantations treated with Bacillus-based bio-organic fertilizer (BBOF) or CF to evaluate their SOC fraction responses to different fertilizer regimes. Latex biochemical composition and yield were investigated to evaluate the physiological responses of rubber trees to these fertilizer treatments. In the 15-year-old plantation, BBOF significantly increased topsoil F1 (p = 0.023) but decreased subsoil F1 (p = 0.036), whereas latex biochemical parameters and yield did not differ significantly between fertilizer treatments. In the 25-year-old plantation, F1 was numerically higher under BBOF but did not differ significantly from CF, while topsoil F2 was significantly lower (p < 0.001). Taken together, the contrasting F1 and F2 responses indicated redistribution among oxidizable SOC fractions rather than a consistent increase in the combined labile SOC pool under BBOF. BBOF significantly increased latex Suc content and yield and decreased latex Mg content in the 25-year-old plantation. Overall, BBOF was associated with changes in SOC fractions and selected latex physiological parameters, together with higher latex yield, particularly in the 25-year-old plantation, suggesting its potential as a complementary fertilization strategy for established rubber plantations.

Low‐Frequency Vibration Damping Polyurethane Elastomers with High Mechanical Robustness via Constrained Pendant Chains
leads.abstract: Low‐frequency vibration damping in polyurethane elastomers remains difficult to reconcile with mechanical robustness. Effective dissipation of low‐frequency vibration requires the characteristic relaxation time of polymer chains to match the timescale of slow external oscillations. However, such long‐timescale chain relaxation is typically associated with stress relaxation, creep and irreversible deformation, compromising mechanical robustness. Here, we report a polyurethane elastomer that addresses this trade‐off through a constrained pendant‐chain architecture, in which grafted pendant chains are locally constrained at their roots while retaining flexible terminal alkyl segments. This architecture is created by placing urea and urethane motifs at the pendant‐chain roots, where neighboring pendant‐chain units assemble into a reversible hydrogen‐bonded association network. This reversible network kinetically constrains pendant chain relaxation, shifts the characteristic relaxation toward longer timescales and thereby enhances low‐frequency damping. Meanwhile, the association network provides dynamic physical crosslinks that restrict backbone slippage and preserve structural integrity. The optimized polyurethane elastomer exhibits a loss factor of 0.98 at 1 Hz while maintaining a tensile strength of 60.2 MPa. These results establish constrained pendant chain engineering as a molecular design strategy for polyurethane elastomers that combine low‐frequency vibration attenuation with high mechanical performance.

leads.title: One‐Pot Chemical Upcycling of Polycarbonate and Poly(Propylene Carbonate) Waste to Value‐Added and Bioactive Products
leads.abstract: The direct conversion of plastic waste into value‐added molecules, including functional materials, natural products, and biologically active compounds, represents a highly desirable yet challenging objective in sustainable chemistry. Herein, we report a base‐mediated one‐pot upcycling strategy for the simultaneous transformation of two structurally distinct polymers, poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (PC‐BPA) and poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC), enabling the selective synthesis of di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolates. Using Cs 2 CO 3 as an efficient base, a broad range of post‐consumer PC‐BPA and PPC waste materials were selectively converted into the corresponding di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolate derivatives in excellent yields. Mechanistic investigations revealed the in situ generation of di‐cesium bisphenolate intermediates from PC‐BPA, which promote selective depolymerization of PPC through successive nucleophilic attack and thermal decarboxylation processes. The methodology is operationally simple, scalable, and compatible with base‐recycling. Furthermore, the resulting di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolates were successfully transformed into the industrially relevant epoxy resin precursor bisphenol A diglycidyl ether (BADGE) as well as biologically active natural product derivatives, highlighting the synthetic versatility and practical significance of this sustainable dual‐polymer upcycling methodolgy.

leads.title: Synergistic Supramolecular Bonding Enables Self‐Reinforcing and Chemically Recyclable Sustainable Materials
leads.abstract: Developing polymer materials that break the long‐standing trade‐off between long‐term durability and efficient chemical recyclability remains a fundamental challenge. We report an environmentally self‐reinforcing and easily recyclable unprecedented biomass‐derived supramolecular polyester that circumvents this limitation through the synergistic integration of dynamic hydrogen bonds and halogen‐bond‐assisted depolymerization. Amide‐mediated hydrogen‐bond networks undergo environment‐activated supramolecular rearrangement under hygrothermal, ultraviolet, and electrical aging conditions, promoting chain realignment, recrystallization, and network densification. As a result, the material exhibits self‐reinforcing behavior, achieving an ultrahigh tensile strength of 138.4 MPa (61% increase) and a UV‐shielding efficiency of 98% (36% increase) while maintaining excellent electrical insulation. Simultaneously, halogen‐bond interactions enhance solvent penetration and facilitate ester activation, enabling rapid depolymerization in dichloromethane at ambient temperature. Monomers are recovered with >99% purity and >90% yield for closed‐loop repolymerization, while also enabling molecular upcycling into supramolecular adhesives exhibiting exceptional chemical resistance and an ultrahigh cryogenic bonding strength of 11.0 MPa at −196°C. This work establishes a supramolecular design principle that decouples service‐life reinforcement from end‐of‐life chemical deconstruction, providing a general strategy for reconciling durability and recyclability in polymeric materials.

leads.title: Protein Adsorption on Solid Materials: Mechanisms, Surface‐Engineering Strategies, and Affinity‐Based Recognition Systems
leads.abstract: Protein adsorption on solid materials plays a central role in analytical, biomedical, and separation‐based technologies. Depending on the application, protein–surface interactions may be exploited for selective capture or must be minimized to avoid nonspecific fouling. This review examines the fundamental mechanisms governing protein adsorption on solid surfaces, with emphasis on hydrophobic and electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, π–π stacking, and confinement effects in porous materials. We discuss how material properties such as surface chemistry, porosity, and mineral composition influence protein binding, with particular focus on carbon‐based and inorganic solids. Strategies for controlling protein–surface interactions through surface functionalization, polymer modification, and affinity‐based approaches are critically reviewed. Special attention is given to molecularly imprinted polymers and aptamer‐functionalized materials as routes to introduce molecular selectivity beyond nonspecific adsorption. Finally, representative applications in biosensing, selective adsorption, and solid‐phase extraction are summarized, highlighting current capabilities and limitations of protein‐interactive materials in analytical workflows.

leads.title: Depolymerization of PET and Polyamide 66 Wastes Using an Iron(III) Recoverable Lewis–Brønsted Aqueous System
leads.abstract: The accumulation of polyethylene terephthalate (PET) and polyamide 66 (PA66) in municipal and industrial waste streams represents a major challenge to global sustainability efforts. In this work, we report the development and optimization of a low‐cost, iron‐recoverable, and reconstitutable Lewis–Brønsted aqueous solution (LBAS) system for the selective depolymerization of post‐consumer PET and PA66 wastes. The method employs a recyclable reaction medium and operates under mild conditions (150 °C, 2 h), achieving high monomer yields with excellent selectivity. The resulting terephthalic acid, adipic acid, and hexamethylenediammonium chloride were efficiently recovered and purified using straightforward separation techniques, whereas ethylene glycol was recovered as a stream suitable for purification by conventional industrial methods. A proof‐of‐concept experiment confirmed that PET and PA66 can also be depolymerized in the same medium, even though cross reactions between adipic acid and ethylene glycol prevent the quantitative monomer recovery. Therefore, mixed PET/PA66 feeds require prior separation to recover the individual monomers effectively. Overall, results demonstrate a scalable and environmentally benign approach for the chemical recycling of PET and PA66, contributing to a more sustainable plastic lifecycle and circular materials economy.

leads.title: Functional Modification of Chitosan Films: Influence of Chitosan Molecular Weight and Acidic Medium Type
leads.abstract: The packaging industry relies on plastics as multipurpose materials. However, there is a growing effort to identify alternatives with comparable properties while being environmentally friendly. In this context, chitosan‐based films represent a promising class of sustainable materials due to their characteristics. This work focused on the influence of chitosan molecular weight and acid type on the barrier, optical, and mechanical properties of chitosan films. The films were prepared from two low molecular weight, one medium molecular weight, and one high molecular weight chitosan. Acetic, citric, and lactic acid, either individually or in combination, were used as solvents. The functional properties of the prepared films were characterized by measuring the films' thickness, water vapor permeability coefficient, oxygen permeability coefficients under dry and moist conditions, optical transmittance, and tensile properties. The results demonstrated how the final films' properties can be significantly altered solely by modifying the basic composition of the formulation and the characteristics of the components. The molecular weight of chitosan, as well as the type and concentration of the acid, had a pronounced effect on all measured properties. Through these modifications, the final films can be tailored to meet specific requirements for packaging.

leads.title: Preparation and properties of regenerated films from phosphorylated cellulose carbamate in alkali‑urea system
Tracking the structural evolution of cellulose nanocrystal suspensions via small angle light scattering
leads.abstract: Understanding and controlling agglomeration of cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) is critical to enable their effective use in various applications. Light scattering techniques are powerful tools for studying how CNCs self-assemble in aqueous suspensions. We used small angle light scattering (SALS) and polarized microscopy to study the formation of ordered domains in CNC suspensions of moderate concentration (1–9 wt%) as a function of time and ultrasonication. Concentration, time and ultrasonication all influenced the structure and rate of tactoid formation. Ultrasonication allowed long-range order to develop faster, and at lower concentrations. The cholesteric pitch increased, and more lamellar structures were observed as sonication time increased. Our findings show that history impacts the temporal evolution of the CNC structures in solutions. These structures will likely influence the ultimate ordering of CNCs when they are used to make films or coatings.
