Construction of photo-activated berberine-rhein self-assembled nanoparticle/gelatin-chitosan composite films and their antibacterial performance.
leads.abstract: To address the persistent environmental burden of petroleum-based plastics and the intrinsic limitations of natural biopolymer films, this study developed an enhanced active packaging material (GC/BR composite film) via the strategic incorporation of self-assembled berberine-rhein nanoparticles (BR NPs) into a gelatin/chitosan (GC) hybrid matrix. Molecular dynamics simulations coupled with various spectroscopic analyses revealed that the co-assembly of BR NPs was primarily stabilized by robust π-π stacking, electrostatic interactions, and hydrogen bonding. The reinforcement effect of BR NPs is attributed to their uniform dispersion and interfacial interactions with the GC matrix, which facilitate efficient stress transfer. As a result, the composite film exhibits notable mechanical enhancements relative to the pure GC film: tensile strength increases by 62% and elongation at break by 88%, accompanied by an improved water vapor barrier. Notably, the GC/BR film retained the aggregation-induced emission characteristics of the photosensitizer, and exhibited effective photodynamic sterilization upon visible-light irradiation. In vitro antibacterial assays demonstrated 100% inactivation against Staphylococcus aureus and 99% against Escherichia coli within 20 min of visible-light irradiation. Real-food preservation trials using chicken breasts further validated the film's capacity to suppress microbial proliferation. Crucially, migration tests revealed a maximum BR NPs leachate concentration of 0.0032 mg/mL (60-fold lower than the highest concentration in hemolysis assays), suggesting a low migration risk and a favorable preliminary biosafety profile. This work provides a promising strategy for the rational design of robust, biodegradable active packaging materials with integrated photodynamic functionality.
leads.authors: Zhang P, Yao Z, Chen S, Wang Z, Zhu J, Wang H, Yi W.

leads.title: Turning Readily Available Acrylates into Cyclic Xanthates for Radical Ring-Opening Polymerizations
leads.abstract: Cyclic sulfur-containing monomers represent a promising class of comonomers for radical ring-opening polymerization, but only a limited number of examples have been reported to date. Here, the cyclic xanthate tert-butyl 2-thioxo-1,3-oxathiolane-5-carboxylate (Oxa) was synthesized from readily available tert-butyl acrylate via epoxidation and subsequent ring extension with carbon disulfide. While homopolymerization was not observed, efficient copolymerization with vinyl acetate yielded copolymers containing dithiocarbonate units in the polymer backbone. Reactivity ratio analysis revealed a preference for heteropropagation, enabling efficient incorporation of dithiocarbonate units with Oxa contents of up to 40 mol %, at which compositions the copolymers displayed a tendency toward an alternating microstructure. The resulting copolymers were highly transparent and colorless and exhibited molar masses and glass transition temperatures comparable to those of poly(vinyl acetate). The incorporated dithiocarbonate units enabled selective backbone cleavage by aminolysis, base-mediated hydrolysis, or oxidative degradation, whereas acidic conditions (0.5 M HCl) did not affect the polymers. Copolymers containing at least 25 mol % Oxa generated low-molar-mass degradation products, confirming the efficient incorporation of degradable units into the polymer chains. These results establish cyclic xanthates derived from a readily accessible acrylate precursor as a versatile platform for introducing chemically degradable dithiocarbonate functionalities into vinyl acetate-based polymers.

leads.title: Melt-spun HDPE/PLA core–shell fibres: a sacrificial-shell route to capillary moisture transport in polyethylene textiles
leads.abstract: High-performance textiles demand fibre architectures that combine mechanical integrity, efficient moisture transport for wearer comfort, and scalable processing, all while meeting stringent sustainability expectations in one of the world’s most environmentally burdensome industries. Here we present a proof of concept for engineering capillary moisture transport into polyethylene by melt-spinning bicomponent fibres with a high-density polyethylene (HDPE) core and polylactic acid (PLA) shell that was selectively dissolved after weaving. Fibres collected at winding speeds of 1000 and 2000 metres per minute (mpm) exhibited mean diameters of 11.96 ± 0.85 μm and 9.63 ± 0.94 μm, respectively, and HDPE crystallinities of 65.6% and 68.7% by DSC. TGA showed that PLA degraded first, with an onset at 293 °C, compared with 395 °C for the fibres recovered after dissolution (HDPEAD). After selective PLA removal, SEM revealed aligned inter-fibre channels and longitudinal surface ridges consistent with along-the-fibre water transport, and infra-red thermography showed that the resulting woven HDPEAD fabrics wick water, reaching saturation in 7-8 min (n = 3), compared with 4 min for cotton and 2 min for polyester, whereas TyvekTM (a commercial nonwoven of flash-spun HDPE) showed no uptake under the same conditions.

leads.title: Silane-interlayer engineering for electron-beam deposited SiO 2 thin films on polycarbonate for in vitro bioelectronic devices
leads.abstract: Robust integration of silicon dioxide (SiO2) onto polycarbonate (PC) is needed for polymer-based bioelectronic platform devices, yet direct oxide deposition on PC often suffers from weak interfacial adhesion. Two silane coupling agents (3-aminopropyl) trimethoxysilane (APTMS) and (3-glycidoxypropyl) methyldiethoxysilane (GPTMS) were evaluated as intermediate adhesion layers for high-vacuum electron-beam (e-beam) evaporation of 〖"SiO" 〗_2 onto plasma-activated polycarbonate (PC). PC substrates were oxygen-plasma treated, immersed in ethanol-based silane solutions, annealed at 60°C, and coated with SiO2 by e-beam evaporation. Surface spectroscopy (XPS, FTIR) confirmed chemical modification consistent with silane-mediated interfacial coupling, while SEM-based topography estimates indicated lower surface roughness under optimized silane loading. Optical transparency of 85.1% was retained for PC/GPTMS (1.5 mL)/SiO2, whereas higher silane loading reduced transmittance (≈68-70%) and promoted material delamination. Cell attachment screening of bare silane terminated SiO2 surfaces without exogenous extracellular matrix (ECM) coating confirmed that GPTMS (1.5 mL) is non-inhibitory to NIH3T3 fibroblast viability at 24 h. Measured AlamarBlue metabolic activity was significantly higher for GPTMS (1.5 mL) than APTMS (1.0 mL) (~33,000 vs ~11,000 fluorescence counts; p < 0.05, unpaired Student’s t-test), and LIVE/DEAD fluorescence imaging showed 40 attached viable cells covering 8.0% area versus 8 cells covering 1.74% in representative fields-of-view. Overall, GPTMS (1.5 mL) provided an optimal balance of coating continuity, optical transparency (85.1%), and cytocompatibility, establishing a viable PC/silane/〖"SiO" 〗_2 substrate stack for polymer-based bioelectronic devices. This work is scoped as a materials-processing and preliminary cytocompatibility screening study; electrical insulation performance of the stack will be reported separately.

leads.title: Conductive Polymers in Microbial Fuel Cells for Bioelectricity Generation
leads.abstract: Microbial fuel cells (MFCs) offer simultaneous wastewater treatment and electricity generation, but their practical performance is limited by inefficient extracellular electron transfer (EET) and interfacial losses at the electrode–biofilm interface. Conductive polymers (CPs), particularly polyaniline (PANI), polypyrrole (PPy), and poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) (PEDOT), have therefore been investigated as electrode modifiers because their electrical, electrochemical, and surface properties can be tailored to support biofilm development and electron transfer. This review critically evaluates reported evidence for CP-modified MFC electrodes, with emphasis on electrochemical performance, EET-related mechanisms, microbial interactions, real-wastewater applications, stability, and scale-up limitations. Laboratory studies demonstrate substantial performance improvements under controlled conditions. For example, PANI nanofiber-modified carbon cloth reached 1,091 mW m⁻², PPy/MXene-modified graphite felt reached 264 mW m⁻² (vs. 45 mW m⁻² for bare graphite felt), and a PEDOT-modified graphite-felt system treating palm oil mill effluent reported a maximum current density of 3.5 A m⁻² and a Coulombic efficiency of 51%. However, these results are difficult to compare directly because studies differ in electrode architecture, reactor configuration, substrate, inoculum, and performance normalization. Evidence for specific CP-mediated EET mechanisms also remains limited, particularly for distinguishing direct, mediated, and long-distance electron-transfer contributions. More importantly, long-term operation with real wastewater and pilot-scale CP-modified systems remains insufficiently investigated. Existing pilot-scale MFC studies without CP modification demonstrate that performance under real wastewater conditions can differ substantially from laboratory results. Future research should therefore prioritize standardized performance reporting, matched real-wastewater comparisons, long-term stability testing, pilot-scale validation, mechanistic EET characterization, and fabrication-cost assessment. Overall, CPs show considerable potential for improving MFC electrode performance, but their practical and economic advantages over conventional electrodes remain to be established under realistic operating conditions.

leads.title: Microencapsulated Beadlets: A Comprehensive Review
leads.abstract: Microencapsulated beadlets are versatile multiparticulate drug delivery systems designed to incorporate active pharmaceutical ingredients within polymeric matrices, core–shell structures, or functional coatings to achieve improved stability and controlled drug release. These systems combine the advantages of microencapsulation with the flexibility of multiparticulate dosage forms and can be formulated to provide immediate, sustained, delayed, pulsatile, biphasic, or site-specific drug delivery. The present review provides a comprehensive overview of the formulation strategies, preparation techniques, characterization, evaluation, and pharmaceutical applications of microencapsulated beadlets. Various manufacturing methods, including solvent evaporation, coacervation-phase separation, fluid-bed coating, extrusion–spheronization, ionotropic gelation, spray drying, spray congealing, melt-based processes, microfluidics, and electrohydrodynamic atomization, are discussed. Particular emphasis is given to the selection and role of natural, semi-synthetic, synthetic, and biodegradable polymers in controlling drug loading, encapsulation efficiency, particle morphology, mechanical strength, and release behavior. Critical quality attributes, including particle size, size distribution, sphericity, surface morphology, density, porosity, drug content, encapsulation efficiency, swelling behavior, drug–polymer compatibility, solid-state properties, and in vitro drug release, are reviewed. Drug release mechanisms involving diffusion, swelling, erosion, dissolution, pore-mediated transport, and polymer degradation are also examined. Microencapsulated beadlets offer significant advantages, including improved patient compliance, flexible dosing, reduced dosing frequency, enhanced stability, taste masking, and the ability to combine different release profiles within a single dosage form. Despite challenges related to manufacturing reproducibility, scale-up, coating uniformity, and process control, emerging technologies such as quality-by-design, continuous manufacturing, advanced polymeric materials, and microfluidics are expected to further enhance their pharmaceutical applications. Keywords: Microencapsulation; beadlets; microbeads; microspheres; multiparticulate drug delivery; controlled release.
leads.venue: Journal of Drug Delivery and Therapeutics

leads.title: Microstructural, Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy, and Fourier-Transform Infrared Analysis of Inorganic-Platelet Polymer Composites for Sustainable Infrastructure
leads.abstract: Polymer matrix composites used in wet or thermally variable environments may change through moisture diffusion, polymer relaxation, swelling and plasticization, hydrolysis or leaching, microcracking, and progressive weakening of the reinforcement–matrix interface. This paper focuses on understanding the composition and morphology of a reinforcing phase, and determining whether its incorporation produces additional bulk-resolvable chemical features, which is important for interpreting composites used in wet or aggressive environments. The study presents a structural and spectroscopic characterization of a commercial glass-flake-reinforced unsaturated-polyester composite by combining energydispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) with full-range Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) against a neat unsaturated-polyester-resin control. EDS gives a composition consistent with a sodium–calcium silicate glass phase for the flake (17.4 wt% Si, 5.0 wt% Na, 2.2 wt% Ca, 1.1 wt% Al, 1.0 wt% Mg and 55.6 wt% O), whereas the polyester matrix and coat regions are dominated by carbon and oxygen (70–75 wt% C and 23–26 wt% O). Two representative flakes (n = 2) have apparent length-to-width ratios of 21.9 and 43.9. FTIR spectra collected over 428–4500 cm-1 show the same principal polyester-resin-associated bands at essentially identical wavenumbers in the composite and neat resin. Polymer-associated band intensities are 12–28% lower in the composite, while the band near the Si–O–Si network bending region changes by only −0.6%. No additional resolvable bulk absorption bands are observed. The results support a physically dispersed silicate-glass phase within the polyester matrix but do not exclude weak or spatially localized interfacial interactions below the resolution of the measurements. The spectra and elemental tables are released as a reusable dataset.

Synthesis and Characterization of Rigid Polyurethane Foam from Palm Oil-Derived Oleic Acid Polyol via Open Molding Process
leads.abstract: Oleic acid derived from palm oil contains a carbon–carbon double bond that can be converted into a polyol through epoxidation and hydroxylation, making it a promising renewable feedstock for rigid polyurethane foam. Polyurethane was synthesized by an open molding process, varying toluene diisocyanate (TDI) and polyethylene glycol (PEG-400) volumes from 10 to 30 mL each. The resulting polyol was a clear, pale-yellow liquid with a density of 0.9363 g/cm³, a viscosity of 14.03 cSt, a pH of 5.22, an acid value of 174.8 mg KOH/g and a hydroxyl value of 180.7 mg KOH/g. Increasing TDI volume decreased foam density due to exothermic CO? generation but increased compressive strength through higher crosslink density, whereas increasing PEG-400 linearly increased density but lowered compressive strength at high TDI levels, as PEG-400 acts as a soft-segment former. The optimum formulation, satisfying ASTM F1839 Grade 5, was Polyol : TDI : PEG-400 = 10 : 30 : 15 mL, giving a density of 0.0743 g/cm³ and a compressive strength of 0.7089 MPa. SEM showed a predominantly closed-cell structure, and FTIR confirmed urethane-bond formation (N–H, C=O, C–O). These results show that palm-oil-derived oleic acid is a feasible renewable feedstock for bio-based rigid polyurethane foam, supporting SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production) and SDG 13 (Climate Action). Contribution to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):SDG 9 : Industry, Innovation, and InfrastructureSDG 12: Responsible Consumption and ProductionSDG 13: Climate Action

leads.title: From Phosphorus Nutrition to Starch Functionality: Effects of Phosphorus Fertilization on Sorghum Starch Biosynthesis, Multiscale Structure, and Processing Properties
leads.abstract: Phosphorus fertilization can regulate starch accumulation and quality in cereal grains, but its effects on sorghum starch remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated sorghum cultivar Liaoza 82 under four phosphorus levels: 0, 40, 80, and 160 kg P2O5 ha−1. Phosphorus application significantly affected starch accumulation and the activities of starch biosynthesis-related enzymes, including AGPase, GBSS, SSS, and SBE. Moderate phosphorus, particularly 80 kg P2O5 ha−1, increased amylose content, granule size, molecular weight, amylopectin branching degree, and medium-to-long amylopectin chains, whereas the highest phosphorus treatment weakened these effects and caused granule surface depressions. Although the A-type crystalline pattern was unchanged, phosphorus modified crystallinity, short-range order, thermal properties, solubility, swelling power, and pasting behavior. Within the phosphorus range investigated, P2 produced a favorable combination of selected structural and thermal characteristics, including lower crystalline order and lower gelatinization temperature and enthalpy, whereas some pasting parameters were highest under P3. These findings indicate that phosphorus fertilization alters sorghum starch structure and functionality, with the response depending on the specific starch characteristic evaluated.

leads.title: Effect of Screw Speed-Induced Starch Molecular Weight Changes on the Process and Dry Mechanical Properties of 3D-Printed PLA/TPS Stents
leads.abstract: This article investigated the effect of screw speed on the molecular weight of starch during thermoplastic starch (TPS) preparation, as well as the effect of this molecular weight on the 3D printing process, interlayer adhesion, molecular orientation, molecular forces, relative crystallinity, and dry mechanical properties of PLA/TPS stents. The increase in screw speed during the preparing of TPS was found to reduce the molecular weight of starch. The reduction in molecular weight of starch was beneficial for the extrusion of filaments and enhanced continuity and uniformity in the lines of 3D-printed stents but reduced the interlayer adhesion of 3D-printed stents. The molecular orientation of stents diminished with decreasing starch molecular weight, leading to a reduction in molecular forces and short-range ordering. This decline was detrimental in terms of enhancing both axial and radial compression characteristics of 3D-printed stents. Considering the influence of starch molecular weight on both the 3D printing process and molecular conformation, the mechanical properties of the 3D-printed PLA/TPS stent were optimized when the screw speed for preparing TPS was set to 160 r/min. The findings will offer theoretical support for the advancement of 3D-printed stents.
leads.venue: Journal of Manufacturing and Materials Processing

leads.title: Carveol-Derived Cycloaliphatic Epoxy for Bio-Based High-Performance Thermosets
leads.abstract: Carveol, a terpenoid alcohol, was selected as a platform molecule for the development of high-performance bio-based epoxy thermosets. A cycloaliphatic diepoxy monomer, carveol dioxide (CDO), was synthesized and subsequently cured with branched polyethyleneimine (BPEI) to afford epoxy thermosets exhibiting outstanding thermomechanical properties, including a storage modulus of 2.5 GPa at 30 °C and a glass transition temperature (Tg) of 97 °C. The resulting thermoset also exhibited strong adhesion to stainless steel, reaching a lap-shear strength of 10.1 MPa, which compares favorably with previously reported bio-based epoxy adhesives. To further enhance network performance, the pendant secondary hydroxyl group of CDO was exploited to introduce urethane crosslinks prior to epoxy curing. Urethane incorporation markedly increased the crosslink density and raised Tg to 137 °C, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the highest value reported for terpene-based epoxy thermosets. These results highlight carveol as a promising renewable platform for high-performance epoxy thermosets and adhesives because its unique combination of C=C bonds and a secondary hydroxyl group enables both epoxide formation and subsequent network modification.

leads.title: Optimization of Orange Peel Extract Nanoemulsions and Their Incorporation into Chitosan/Gelatin Biodegradable Films: Physicochemical and Functional Properties
leads.abstract: In this study, orange peel extract (OPE), obtained from Citrus sinensis processing by-products, was encapsulated in nanoemulsions and incorporated into chitosan/gelatin-based biodegradable films to enhance their functional performance. A Box–Behnken design combined with response surface methodology was employed to optimize nanoemulsion formulation. Polyphenolic profiling revealed that flavanones, particularly hesperidin and narirutin, were the predominant compounds in both the extract and the optimized nanoemulsion, with retention efficiencies exceeding 80% for major flavonoids. The incorporation of OPE-loaded nanoemulsions into chitosan/gelatin films significantly modified film structure and functionality. Nanoemulsion-containing films showed increased thickness and opacity, reduced solubility and swelling capacity, as well as enhanced UV-visible light barrier properties compared with control films. Furthermore, nanoencapsulation increased polyphenol recovery within the film matrix, preserving up to 80% of total polyphenols after film formation. Both free-extract and nanoemulsion-loaded films exhibited markedly enhanced antioxidant activity compared with control films. Release studies demonstrated that nanoemulsion incorporation promoted a more sustained and controlled release of polyphenols, with the characteristic release time more than doubling relative to films containing the non-encapsulated extract. No antibacterial activity was detected against the tested bacterial strains; this result may be attributed to the relatively low availability of antimicrobial compounds in the film matrix or their limited diffusion into the surrounding medium; nevertheless, the incorporation of OPE-loaded nanoemulsions improved stability, antioxidant performance, and controlled release behavior, highlighting the potential of nanoemulsion-assisted incorporation strategies. The developed chitosan/gelatin films containing OPE-loaded nanoemulsions represent a promising approach for the development of active biodegradable food-packaging systems.

leads.title: Bio-Based Deproteinized Natural Rubber/Alginate/Poly(vinyl alcohol) Films with Ca2+-Mediated and Tannic Acid-Induced Crosslinked Networks for Biodegradable Adhesive Materials
leads.abstract: In this study, biodegradable adhesive composite films based on deproteinized natural rubber/alginate/poly(vinyl alcohol) (DPNR/ALG/PVA) were developed through Ca2+-mediated ionic crosslinking and tannic acid (TA)-induced hydrogen bonding interactions. DPNR/ALG/PVA mixtures were ionically crosslinked through ALG-Ca2+ interactions, cast into films, and subsequently immersed in TA-containing ethanol/water cosolvent systems. Treatment in a 75:25 ethanol/water solution at a PVA/TA weight ratio of 1:7 for 12 h produced stable films with a high gel fraction. The TA-treated DPNR/ALG3/PVA40 film exhibited gel fraction of 91.01 ± 0.79%, higher than that of the untreated film (71.22 ± 1.62%), indicating improved network stability after TA treatment. FTIR analysis confirmed the incorporation of ALG and PVA within the DPNR matrix and suggested the formation of interactions involving TA. Increasing ALG content from 1 to 5 phr enhanced swelling capacity, reaching 241.81 ± 22.30%, whereas increasing PVA content (20–80 phr) improved tensile strength from 3.51 ± 0.10 to 6.39 ± 0.43 MPa. Moreover, the PVA-TA network improved adhesive performance, increasing lap shear strength from 1.23 ± 0.20 to 1.83 ± 0.12 MPa and peel strength from 70.37 ± 15.10 to 280.94 ± 68.45 N/m. Soil burial tests revealed the biodegradability of composite films, with no recoverable residue detected after 180 days. These results demonstrate the potential of the developed composites as biodegradable adhesive materials for biomedical applications.

leads.title: Synthesis and Structural Characterization of Neem Oil-Derived Bio-Polyol as a Sustainable Precursor for Bio-Based Polyurethane Production
leads.abstract: The growing demand for sustainable and environmentally friendly materials has intensified the search for renewable alternatives to petroleum-derived polyols used in polyurethane production. In this study, neem oil (Azadirachta indica), a non-edible and renewable vegetable oil, was chemically modified through a calcium oxide (CaO)-catalyzed glycerolysis process to produce a bio-based polyol suitable for polyurethane applications. The reaction was conducted in a batch reactor at 225 °C for 180 min under controlled operating conditions. The synthesized bio-polyol was characterized using Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FTIR) and Gas Chromatography–Mass Spectrometry (GC–MS) to evaluate its structural and chemical properties. FTIR analysis revealed the presence of hydroxyl functionalities, evidenced by a broad absorption band around 3300 cm⁻¹, confirming successful functionalization of the neem oil. GC–MS analysis showed that alcohols and esters constituted 71.68% of the reaction products, indicating a substantial degree of conversion during glycerolysis. Physicochemical characterization demonstrated significant reductions in acid value and free fatty acid content, accompanied by a marked increase in viscosity, reflecting effective molecular restructuring of the oil. These findings confirm the successful synthesis of a hydroxyl-functionalized neem oil-derived bio-polyol and highlight its potential as a sustainable precursor for the development of bio-based polyurethane materials. The study contributes to ongoing efforts toward the utilization of renewable feedstocks in environmentally responsible polymer production.

leads.title: Endocrine Disruptors in Everyday Life: Plastics, Cosmetics, and Their Impact on Human Hormonal Balance
leads.abstract: Endocrine disruptors (EDs) are chemicals that can disturb the hormonal balance of the body by affecting the endocrine system. These substances are commonly present in everyday consumer products, especially plastics and cosmetic products, resulting in continuous human exposure. This review article summarizes current knowledge about selected endocrine disruptors in these product categories and examines their possible health effects. The article focuses primarily on bisphenols, phthalates, perfluorinated compounds (PFAS), parabens, UV filters, and aluminium salts found in plastics and cosmetics. It also describes the mechanisms through which these substances exert their effects during critical stages of human development. Attention is also paid to their possible consequences for human health, especially in relation to reproductive disorders, metabolic diseases, neuroendocrine dysfunctions, and an increased risk of cancer, the incidence of which in the population has been increasing in recent years. In conclusion, the article highlights the need for legislative reforms, consistent biomonitoring, and interdisciplinary cooperation in prevention and public education.

leads.title: Physical properties of rigid polyurethane foams filled with calendula flowers
leads.abstract: Calendula (Calendula officinalis L.) is a herbaceous plant of significant pharmacological importance, primarily valued for its complex biochemical profile and the therapeutic properties of its floral components. Its economic significance is attributed to its versatile pharmaceutical applications, stemming from a high concentration of phytochemicals with documented health-promoting properties. This article presents the results of research on the use of dried calendula flowers as a natural filler for producing rigid polyurethane foams. To improve fire properties, the foamed compositions were flame-retardant with expanded graphite EG290. Basic physical properties were tested: apparent density, water absorption, dimensional stability, and thermal conductivity. The morphology of the produced foams was assessed. Based on the experimental results, the performance properties of the produced rigid polyurethane foams were assessed. The produced compositions exhibited acceptable functional parameters.

Design of Tamarind Seed Gum‐Graft‐Poly (Acrylamide‐Co‐Itaconic Acid) Hydrogel for the Sustained Delivery of Curcumin Analogue
leads.abstract: The present study focused on the synthesis and characterization of a novel Tamarind seed gum (TSG)‐Graft‐Poly (Acrylamide‐Co‐Itaconic acid) [TSG‐ g ‐poly (AAm‐co‐IA)] hydrogel for the evaluation of a controlled delivery system of 2,5‐bis(4‐fluorobenzylidene) cyclopentanone, a curcumin analogue (CUR‐A). The free radical graft co‐polymerization of acrylamide and itaconic acid (IA) onto the TSG backbone facilitated TSG‐ g ‐poly (AAm‐co‐IA) synthesis. The structural elucidation, morphological studies, and thermal analysis were accomplished using Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, scanning electron microscopy, energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy, thermogravimetric analysis, and powder x‐ray diffraction studies. At pH 7.0, the hydrogel exhibited the highest swelling of 21.12 ± 0.5 g/g. The in vitro release studies revealed the slow and controlled release of 97.95 ± 1.2% of CUR‐A from the hydrogel matrix at pH 5.0 in 32 h. This allows CUR‐A to be delivered in an acidic environment, with minimal release at physiological pH. The drug‐diffusion mechanism seemed to be Fickian, with the Korsmeyer‐Peppas model as the suitable fit. The anticancer activity studies performed on human hepatocellular carcinoma (HepG2) cells confirmed the enhanced anticancer efficacy of the CUR‐A‐TSG‐ g ‐poly (AAm‐co‐IA). The toxicity evaluation on Drosophila melanogaster disclosed no evident signs of toxicity under experimental conditions.

leads.title: Effect of Sequential Heat‐Moisture and Infrared Treatment on the Techno‐Functional Properties of Buckwheat Starch
leads.abstract: This study investigated the effects of infrared heating (IR; 30% moisture, 90 s, 110°C), heat‐moisture treatment (HMT; 30% moisture, 6 h, 110°C), and two sequential dual‐treatment combinations: HMT followed by IR (HMTIR) and IR followed by HMT (IRHMT). All treatments significantly increased amylose content (up to 32.93%) through partial amylopectin debranching and chain realignment, resulting in increased resistant starch content. Dual treatments also increased water absorption capacity (179.95 g/g), despite reduced porosity, suggesting that enhanced water binding was primarily governed by molecular restructuring and increased availability of hydrophilic sites. The gelatinization temperature increased, while the enthalpy declined (7.48–9.52 J/g), indicating enhanced thermal stability accompanied by partial disruption of starch helices. RVA showed 18%–40% reductions in peak and breakdown viscosities, and lower setback values, confirming restricted granule disintegration and reduced retrogradation. XRD revealed crystallinity changes from 19.8% to 48.5% (HMT), 16.5% (IR), and intermediate values for dual treatments, with polymorphic transitions from A‐type to V‐type. SEM micrographs corroborated these findings, revealing the transition from smooth native granules to porous structures under IR treatment, compact morphology after HMT, and fissured yet cohesive surfaces in the dual‐modified starches. Improved powder flow indices were also noted. These findings demonstrate that both single and sequential HMT and IR modifications can strategically tailor buckwheat starch functionality for improved thermal stability, hydration behavior, and slower digestibility in food applications.

leads.title: Utilization of Red Rice‐Derived Starch and Anthocyanin for the Development of Citric Acid Cross‐Linked Films With Gelatin and Beeswax With Enhanced Functionality
leads.abstract: The present study focuses on the utilization of starch from red rice and its anthocyanins in the development of edible films, and a comparison of its various properties was made with those of non‐anthocyanin starch films. The physical, optical, mechanical, barrier, and structural properties were determined to find the suitability for food packaging applications. Anthocyanin‐based films exhibited enhanced antioxidant activity, confirming the functional efficacy of phenolic incorporation. Structural analysis using FTIR and XRD indicated that anthocyanin incorporation altered hydrogen bonding patterns and reduced crystallinity, especially at lower starch concentrations. On the other hand, nonanthocyanin films demonstrated improved mechanical properties, higher crystallinity, better moisture resistance, and more uniform surface morphology. Biodegradability tests confirmed that all films degraded progressively in soil within 10 days, with anthocyanin films degrading slightly faster. Due to their superior performance, only the non‐anthocyanin films were successfully fabricated into stand‐alone pouches, demonstrating real‐world packaging potential. The findings underscore the importance of balancing bioactivity and structural integrity in bio‐based films and promote the use of red rice starch as a sustainable, functional material for future food packaging applications.

leads.title: Rational Engineering of Carboxylic Acid Reductase for Improved Catalytic Efficiency and Substrate Tolerance Enabling Green Vanillin Biosynthesis
leads.abstract: Vanillin is a high-value natural aromatic compound widely used in food, flavor, and pharmaceutical fields. Carboxylic acid reductase (CAR)-catalyzed vanillic acid bioreduction offers a green vanillin biosynthesis route, yet low catalytic activity and severe substrate inhibition limit its industrial application. Herein, we screened 10 bacterial CAR homologues and constructed superior chimeric CAR templates via domain recombination. Combined with structure-guided directed evolution and substrate tunnel remodeling, the optimized quadruple mutant M4 was obtained, exhibiting 4-fold higher catalytic efficiency compared with the wild-type MavCAR (and 1.6-fold higher than the parental chimera M0) and partially relieved activity decline at elevated substrate concentrations. Structural simulations clarified that tunnel expansion and hydrogen bond remodeling synergistically stabilized enzyme–substrate binding. The M4-based whole-cell system achieved 95% vanillin conversion (8.7 g·L–1) from 10 g·L–1 vanillic acid, and a two-step cascade system realized efficient de novo vanillin synthesis from glucose. This work provides a robust engineered CAR biocatalyst for green vanillin preparative-scale biosynthesis.

leads.title: Recyclable Soft Elastomers Derived from Biobased δ -Valerolactones
leads.abstract: Soft elastomers are widely used in applications requiring low modulus and resilience, yet their chemical recyclability, particularly the recovery of original monomers to counteract property degradation from repeated thermal processing, remains a significant challenge. To create recyclable soft elastomers, we integrated the chemical recyclability of polyesters with dynamic boronic ester crosslinking chemistry. Through sequential ring-opening polymerization (ROP) of α-methyl-δ-valerolactone (αMeVL) and α,α-spirocyclohexenyl-δ-valerolactone (αSpiroCyEVL), followed by post-modification and crosslinking, a series of soft elastomers with an outstanding service temperature range from –50 to 116 °C were obtained. Introducing δ-valerolactone (δVL) into the soft segment further enabled tunable mechanical properties (modulus of 0.22–6.42 MPa, tensile strength of 0.06–6.40 MPa, elongation at break of 536–1587%, tensile toughness of 0.44–22.0 MJ m–3). The soft elastomers derived from δVL are comparable to a commercial soft polyolefin elastomer. Moreover, these soft elastomers not only exhibit physical recyclability but also enable chemical closed-loop recycling via an ‘alcoholysis–depolymerization–repolymerization’ pathway after multiple physical recycling cycles, demonstrating potential for biomedical devices, flexible electronics, and soft robotics.

leads.title: Valorization of cotton waste into cellulose nanocrystals and their incorporation into electrospun poly (vinyl alcohol) nanofibrous membranes with enhanced thermal and structural properties
leads.abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) were extracted from cotton waste using alkaline treatment, bleaching, and sulfuric acid hydrolysis. Increasing the sulfuric acid concentration from 40% to 62% was associated with an increase in CNC yield from approximately 19.20 ± 3.9% to 41.30 ± 3.1%, indicating the influence of acid concentration on the recovery of the nanocrystalline fraction under the conditions employed. Energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX) showed carbon and oxygen as the predominant elements, at 62.39 and 34.33 wt%, respectively, with trace amounts of sulfur and sodium. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) revealed snowflake-like aggregated structures composed of branched rod-like features, with an average width of 56.5 ± 8.7 nm . Atomic force microscopy (AFM) showed broadly consistent nanoscale morphological features, with snowflake-like structures ranging from approximately 120–200 nm and protruding branches of approximately 63.2 ± 10.9 nm in diameter. Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR) showed characteristic cellulose bands, including the band at 872.9 cm⁻¹ associated with β-(1→4)-glycosidic linkages. CNCs were incorporated into poly (vinyl alcohol) (PVA) nanofibrous membranes at concentrations of 0–40 wt% via electrospinning. Field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) of the 40 wt% CNC membrane revealed a relatively uniform fibrous network with a mean fiber diameter of 104.3 ± 38.6 nm, with CNCs distributed on the fiber surfaces. FTIR analysis of the prepared nanofibers showed the characteristic 916 cm⁻¹ band, supporting the presence of the cellulose component. Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) showed an increase in residual mass with increasing CNC content, from 1.28% for the neat PVA membrane to 24.88% for the 40 wt% CNC membrane. Derivative thermogravimetry (DTG) indicated changes in thermal degradation behavior with increasing CNC content. The 40 wt% CNC formulation exhibited the highest residual mass among the studied formulations. The study highlights the successful conversion of cotton waste into CNCs and their incorporation into PVA nanofibrous membranes, with potential applications in advanced packaging and biomedical membranes.

leads.title: Controlled functionalization of cellulose nanocrystals directs polymer-specific protein coronas and immune cell interactions.
leads.abstract: Polymer coatings are widely used to suppress nonspecific protein adsorption and modulate nanoparticle-cell interactions. However, the biological outcomes of polymer-functionalized nanoparticles remain difficult to predict in complex biological environments because protein corona formation rapidly alters nanoparticle identity. This challenge is particularly pronounced when hydrophobic moieties are incorporated for imaging or therapeutic applications, as they can promote nonspecific interactions at the nano-bio interface. Herein, we establish a modular grafting-to platform based on cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) that enables systematic comparison of polyethylene glycol (PEG)-based, zwitterionic, and acrylamide-based polymers with controlled grafting density and chain conformation on a common porphyrin-modified surface. We demonstrate that dense polymer brushes reduce nonspecific protein adsorption in single-protein assays. By contrast, all CNC surfaces form dynamic coronas upon exposure to serum proteins, while specific polymer coatings selectively enrich or suppress distinct protein populations. We further demonstrate that polymer-dependent immune cell interactions are substantially reduced following protein corona formation, although differences among polymer chemistries persist. Zwitterionic coatings broadly suppress immune cell interactions, whereas PEG-based coatings preferentially promote interactions with antigen-presenting cells. These findings establish design principles for polymer-functionalized nanoparticles with specific immune cell interaction profiles.

leads.title: Feasibility of biodegradable bags for vacuum-packaging of beef: a small-scale study
leads.abstract: The growing demand for environmentally sustainable food packaging has stimulated interest in biodegradable alternatives to conventional materials, not only at an industrial level but also for small-scale craft productions. This pilot study evaluated the feasibility of using biodegradable and compostable poly-butylene adipate-coterephtalate (PBAT)-based vacuum bags as an alternative to standard polyamide/polyethylene (PA/PE) bags for fresh beef packaging under artisanal conditions. Beef steaks were vacuum-packed, stored at 4 °C for 11 days, and packaging performance was evaluated over time through measurements of pH, water activity, drip loss, microbiological quality, and color of meat. Overall, biodegradable bags showed similar performances to those of PA/PE throughout storage. No relevant differences were observed concerning all parameters under investigation, indicating that the biodegradable packaging adequately preserved the quality of meat under the experimental conditions tested. Results support the feasibility of PBAT-based bags for vacuum-packaging of beef steaks in small-scale production systems.

leads.title: The Impact of Natural Propolis on a Film Forming System of Chitosan in Non-Surgical Treatment of Periodontitis (Randomized Clinical and Biochemical Trial)
leads.abstract: Aim: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of natural propolis incorporated into a chitosan film-forming system as an adjunct to non-surgical periodontal therapy.Patients and methods: In this prospective, randomized controlled clinical trial, 45 patients with stage II periodontitis were allocated into three equal groups: Group I received SRP alone, Group II received SRP plus chitosan film-forming gel, and Group III received SRP plus propolis-loaded chitosan film-forming gel.Results: All treatment groups demonstrated significant improvements in clinical parameters and significant reductions in MPO levels throughout the study period (p < 0.001).At 3 months, Group III showed the greatest reductions in PI, GI, PPD, CAL, and MPO levels compared with Groups I and II.Group II also demonstrated superior outcomes to SRP alone, indicating the beneficial effect of chitosan as a local drug delivery system.Conclusion: Non-surgical periodontal therapy remains the cornerstone of stage II periodontitis management.However, adjunctive intra-pocket application of propolis incorporated into a chitosan film-forming system significantly enhanced clinical and biochemical outcomes compared with SRP alone or chitosan gel alone, suggesting a promising therapeutic approach for improving periodontal treatment success.

leads.title: Performance-Based Evaluation of Eco-Efficient Polyurethane Panels for Sustainable Interior Architecture
leads.abstract: Interior finishing materials contribute significantly to embodied carbon emissions but remain underrepresented in performance-based sustainability assessment frameworks. This study investigates the potential of eco-efficient polyurethane (PU) decorative panels as low-carbon alternatives to conventional interior finishing materials in hot-humid climates. A comparative case study methodology was adopted using secondary life cycle assessment (LCA) datasets, Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs), and peer-reviewed literature to evaluate bio-based PU systems in Dubai and recycled PU panels in Singapore. Four performance criteria—embodied carbon, thermal performance, acoustic performance, and durability—were comparatively assessed through a proposed Performance-Based Interior System (PBIS) framework. To support integrated material evaluation, the study introduces a novel Performance Efficiency Index (PEI), which combines environmental and functional performance into a single comparative metric. Comparative analysis of published performance data indicates that eco-efficient PU panels can achieve approximately 35–40% lower embodied carbon than conventional interior materials while providing improved thermal stability, acoustic performance, and durability under hot-humid environmental conditions. The findings reposition interior materials as active environmental systems rather than passive finishing elements and demonstrate the potential of PBIS as a transferable decision-support framework for sustainable material selection in interior architecture. The proposed framework contributes to the advancement of performance-based and climate-responsive interior design by integrating environmental and functional criteria within a unified assessment methodology

leads.title: Enterovirus D68 infection causing plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia: a case report and literature review
leads.abstract: Background Plastic bronchitis (PB) is a rare disease characterized by the formation of tree-like or tubular mucus plugs within the bronchi, which can lead to severe airway obstruction and respiratory failure, potentially becoming life-threatening if diagnosis and treatment are delayed. Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) is a common pathogen that causes acute respiratory infections in children,which can lead to wheezing, acute flaccid myelitis, and even respiratory failure. Nevertheless, a direct association between EV-D68 infection and plastic bronchitis has not been previously reported. As the first documented case, this report establishes the association between EV-D68 and plastic bronchitis, thereby expanding the clinical spectrum of EV-D68. Methods We report a case of plastic bronchitis and severe pneumonia caused by Enterovirus D68 infection. To identify additional cases and elucidate the clinical characteristics of this condition, a systematic literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases for the period from January 2006 to June 2026. The search strategy employed the following keywords: “Enterovirus D68” “plastic bronchitis” and “severe pneumonia”. Case description This case involved an 11-year-old girl with previously good health. Chief complaints: cough and wheezing for 1 day, chest pain for half a day. Chest CT showed patchy increased-density opacities in the left upper loben with reduced left upper lobe volume, small nodular increased-density opacities in the left lower lobe and right lower lobe, right pleural thickening. Following admission, two flexible bronchoscopic examinations with plastic cast removal and bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) were performed; bronchoscopic findings were consistent with plastic bronchitis and bronchial mucosal inflammation. Targeted next-generation sequencing (tNGS) of bronchoalveolar lavage fluid(BALF) detected Enterovirus D68 and Rhinovirus. Intravenous immunoglobulin support and methylprednisolone anti-inflammatory therapy were also administered. By hospital day 10, the patient's condition had stabilized;Follow-up chest CT demonstrated resolution of the left upper lobe patchy high-density opacities with re-expansion of the left upper lobe, patchy high-density opacities in the left lower lobe and small left pleural effusion. The newly developed lesion in the left lower lobe was considered resolving inflammatory changes rather than new active infection. The patient was discharged with medication. At 6 days post-discharge, follow-up chest CT demonstrated complete resolution of pulmonary infiltrates, pleural effusions, consistent with full clinical recovery. The total duration of treatment was 10 days of hospitalization plus 6 days of oral therapy after discharge, giving a total of 16 days. Conclusion EV-D68 infection should be recognized as a potential etiology of plastic bronchitis or severe pneumonia in children. In addition to direct pathogen-mediated tissue injury, immune-mediated damage warrants careful consideration in the underlying pathophysiological mechanisms. Early bronchoscopic intervention combined with anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory therapy may prove critical in shortening the disease course and improving clinical outcomes.

leads.title: Biopolymer-based coatings for egg preservation: recent advances, current challenges, and future prospects
leads.abstract: Eggs, despite being globally consumed given their nutritional value, remain highly susceptible to storage quality challenges, from physicochemical changes, through microbial contamination, to oxidative deterioration. Moreover, if sustainable preservation outcomes extending egg shelf life were to be steadily achieved, it would require continued literature syntheses about how internal quality and safety (of egg shelf life) are maintained. To supplement existing information, this current review synthesizes biopolymer-based coatings for egg preservation, from recent advances, through current challenges, to future research prospects. Polysaccharide- and protein-based biopolymer matrices are established as important coating platforms for improving egg quality and shelf life. Nanocomposite coatings incorporating nanofillers and natural bioactive compounds provide multifunctional barrier, mechanical, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. Such multifunctional coating systems can enhance preservation performance through combined mechanisms involving moisture regulation, controlled gas transfer, oxidative stabilization, microbial inhibition, and retention and gradual availability of active compounds. Unlike previous reviews that largely dwelt on individual coating materials, the current review synergizes biopolymer matrices, nanocomposite reinforcement, bioactive functionalization, alongside emerging intelligent coating strategies. Besides, consumer acceptance, manufacturing scalability, production cost, and regulatory compliance remain important considerations and potential barriers to commercialization. However, if multifunctional, intelligent, and commercially viable coating technologies are to successfully enhance sustainable egg preservation, more efforts are required. Overall, coating technology has progressed beyond simple protective barriers toward edible multifunctional preservation systems with promising potential to improve egg quality, safety, shelf life, and sustainability.

leads.title: Valorization of Bio- and Coal-Based Ash in Rigid Polyurethane Foams: Thermomechanical Performance and Decomposition Under Pyrolytic Conditions
leads.abstract: This study investigates the pyrolytic processes and thermomechanical properties of polyurethane (PU) foamed composites filled with ashes obtained after sunflower husk combustion and conventional coal combustion, as well as their silanized derivatives. The results indicate that an improvement in thermal stability during the initial stages of pyrolysis was observed only for PU composites containing silanized ash generated from conventional coal combustion (a difference of 5 °C). At later stages of the thermal decomposition, a significant increase in temperature resistance was observed for the remaining composites. Kinetic studies of degradation using isoconversional methods revealed that composites containing sunflower husk ash exhibit degradation mechanisms different from those of the reference material, as observed by the changes in the activation energy particularly within the conversion range of 0.40–0.65. Dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) demonstrated that all composites show improved mechanical response over a broad temperature range, with the highest mechanical performance observed after ash silanization (doubled E′ at the initial stage of the study compared to the reference). The analysis of evolved gases, performed using the Py-GC/MS technique, proved the existence of a different degradation path for composites with sunflower husk ash by a change in the amount of evolved gases during the pyrolysis process.

leads.title: Aging Resistance Improvement of Rubber–Plastic-Based TPE-Modified Asphalt System with Different Plastic Types
leads.abstract: This study evaluated the aging resistance of bitumen modified with integrated rubber–plastic thermoplastic elastomers (TPEs). Surface-activated low-Mooney reclaimed rubber was compounded with recycled high-density polyethylene, low-density polyethylene, or polypropylene by twin-screw reactive extrusion using a maleic anhydride-grafted styrenic block copolymer compatibilizer. Reference binders contained styrene–butadiene–styrene (SBS), rubber alone, or individual polyolefins. Aging comprised the rolling thin-film oven test, pressure aging vessel conditioning of oven-aged residues, and ultraviolet exposure. Dynamic shear rheometry, Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, and atomic force microscopy characterized rheological, chemical, and topographic changes. The largest rutting factor and carbonyl aging indices occurred after sequential oven and pressure aging under the selected conditions. The TPE-modified binders showed lower rutting factor and carbonyl aging indices and smaller relative roughness increases than the SBS reference under each protocol. Among the three TPE formulations, the low-density polyethylene composite had the lowest rutting factor aging indices, whereas the high-density polyethylene composite had the lowest carbonyl aging indices and relative roughness increases after pressure and ultraviolet aging. These findings support the laboratory aging-resistance potential of integrated TPEs, with improved interfacial compatibility providing a plausible explanation. The approach offers a route for the high-value utilization of waste rubber and plastics.

leads.title: Sustainable Approach to Thermoplastic Polyurethanes Stabilization: Vanillin as a Natural Additive in Melt-Processing
leads.abstract: Thermo-oxidative degradation during high-temperature processing remains a major challenge limiting the performance of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs). This study evaluated vanillin (4-hydroxy-3-methoxybenzaldehyde), a bio-based phenolic compound, as a primary thermo-oxidative stabilizer acting as a free-radical scavenger. Bio-based TPU (bio-TPU) was synthesized via a two-step method using a commercial bio-based polyol, a bio-based chain extender, and a mixture of diisocyanates. During processing in an internal mixer, vanillin was incorporated into both bio-TPU and a commercial TPU at concentrations of 0.03, 0.165, and 0.3 wt%. Changes in chemical structure were assessed by Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermal properties were evaluated by thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), including oxidation onset temperature (OOT) measurements, and dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA). Mechanical properties were assessed by tensile test and hardness. FTIR analysis revealed no significant structural changes after vanillin addition. However, changes in thermal properties were observed, including an increase in the OOT for materials containing the highest vanillin content. TGA results also showed a generally improved thermal stability at higher vanillin concentrations, approaching reference-material values at the highest concentration in the commercial TPU. A slight decrease in mechanical properties was observed. These findings demonstrate a pronounced stabilizing effect of 0.3 wt% vanillin on both bio-TPU and commercial TPU, providing new insights into the potential reuse and further recycling of TPU materials stabilized with bio-based additives.

leads.title: Synthetic biology-guided modular engineering of the secreted cutinase FoCut5a with a carbohydrate-binding module improves poly(ester-urethane) depolymerization in Yarrowia lipolytica
leads.abstract: Poly(ester-urethane) bioconversion requires efficient polymer-degrading enzymes and microbial hosts capable of processing the resulting monomers. However, the optimal modular design of secreted cutinases for depolymerizing insoluble polyester-polyurethanes remains largely unexplored. Here, we established a combinatorial synthetic biology strategy in Yarrowia lipolytica based on the fungal cutinase FoCut5a from Fusarium oxysporum. A library of 96 Golden Gate-assembled constructs, combining four secretion signals, four interdomain linkers, and six substrate-binding domains, was integrated site-specifically into the genome and screened for depolymerization of the polyester-polyurethane dispersion Impranil DLN-SD. The best-performing variant fused FoCut5a to the carbohydrate-binding module TrCBM1. LC-MS analysis demonstrated release of adipic acid, 1,6-hexanediol, and neopentyl glycol, confirming ester-bond hydrolysis within the polyester domains of the polymer and additionally detected 6-hydroxycaproate, indicating oxidation of polyurethane-derived 1,6-hexanediol by Y. lipolytica. Purified FoCut5a-TrCBM1 displayed unchanged activity on p-nitrophenyl butyrate but reduced Impranil turbidity 5.6-fold faster and increased release of 1,6-hexanediol and adipic acid by 76-fold and 220-fold, respectively, compared to the unfused enzyme. These results highlight modular enzyme engineering as an effective strategy to enhance polyester-polyurethane deconstruction and support Y. lipolytica as a platform for polymer bioconversion and upcycling.

Robust polyvinyl alcohol based multifunctional films with pH-responsive via electrostatic self-assembly of TOCNF and quaternary ammonium chitosan by loading apple polyphenol.
leads.abstract: Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)-based materials with pH-responsive colorimetric properties have attracted increasing attention for sustainable and intelligent packaging applications. Although numerous studies have reported PVA-based pH-responsive packaging films with antioxidant and antimicrobial activities, further optimization is still required in achieving a balanced integration of multiple functionalities, including antioxidant performance, antimicrobial efficiency, and long-term structural stability. Thus, a new kind of multifunctional PVA based composite film was fabricated via direct solvent casting combined with ultrasonication by mixing PVA with TEMPO-oxidized nanocellulose (TOCNF), quaternary ammonium chitosan (QCS), and apple polyphenol (APP). The effects of APP and QCS incorporation on the structural, mechanical, barrier, biological, and intelligent-responsive properties of the films were systematically investigated. The optimized PT-1.5(QA) film exhibited a balanced mechanical performance, with a tensile strength of approximately 8.1 MPa and an elongation at break of approximately 243%, attributed to the formation of intermolecularly associated polymer networks. Meanwhile, APP incorporation significantly enhanced the antioxidant and UV-shielding properties, achieving approximately 92.8% DPPH and 96.5% ABTS radical scavenging activities. Furthermore, the composite film exhibited enhanced barrier properties, strong antibacterial activity against Escherichia coli and Staphylococcus aureus, and distinct pH-responsive color changes over a broad pH range (1-12). Cytotoxicity evaluation confirmed good in vitro biocompatibility. Importantly, the composite film effectively delayed postharvest senescence and quality deterioration of litchi fruit, while maintaining favorable biodegradability. These findings highlight the potential of TOCNF/QCS/APP/PVA films as sustainable active and intelligent packaging materials for food preservation.
leads.authors: Liu J, Cheng Y, Fang C, Han H, Li M, Zhang X, Jiang Z, Xiang K.

leads.title: Acid-Triggered Cyclization Enables Selective Depolymerization of Robust Polyamides for Recovery of Monomer Derivatives
leads.abstract: The development of polymeric materials that combine practical performance with selective degradability is an important goal in sustainable materials research. Selective degradation into defined small molecules offers a promising strategy for the deconstruction and potential chemical recycling of polymeric materials. However, extending this concept to mechanically robust polyamides remains challenging because of the high stability of their amide backbones. In this study, we used microbially produced poly(ε-lysine) (PLys) as a renewable feedstock to construct biobased polyamides that undergo rapid acid-mediated depolymerization. The amino groups at the α-carbons of PLys were modified with isothiocyanates bearing different side groups to afford thiourea-functionalized PLys derivatives. These thiourea moieties were selectively cleaved through an acid-mediated cyclization reaction, yielding the corresponding cyclic lysine derivatives as discrete depolymerization products. Structural analyses revealed that the thiourea-modified PLys underwent complete depolymerization in the presence of acids such as hydrochloric acid, and that the cyclic lysine derivatives could be recovered without specialized purification. Moreover, thiourea modification converted PLys into amorphous polyamides that formed robust films and exhibited a high storage modulus at ambient temperature. The polyamides could also be cross-linked using multifunctional isothiocyanates, and the resulting network materials exhibited shape-memory behavior together with a high storage modulus. Overall, this study establishes a molecular design strategy for mechanically robust biobased polyamides that undergo rapid acid-triggered depolymerization into defined cyclic lysine derivatives, opening a route toward selectively deconstructable polyamides for sustainable materials applications.

leads.title: Rational Design of Molecularly Imprinted Nanozymes for Selective Degradation of Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC)
leads.abstract: Poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (BPA-PC) is an engineering thermoplastic whose recycling is hindered by its Code-7 classification and environmental BPA leaching. Here, we report water-soluble molecularly imprinted nanozymes for the selective depolymerization of BPA-PC under mild alkaline conditions. Synthesized within cross-linked surfactant micelles, the optimized nanozyme combines shape-complementary BPA-matched pockets with surface basicity, achieving a 72-fold rate enhancement over porcine pancreatic lipase. Fluorescence titrations with a soluble dansyl-labeled BPA-PC dimer confirm strong substrate recognition (Ka ~106 M−1). Gel permeation chromatography reveals uniform reductions of 52–55% across Mn, Mw, and Mz, indicative of a random endo-chain cleavage mechanism. On macroscopic BPA-PC films, the nanozyme induces pronounced cracking and surface erosion, whereas polyethylene terephthalate (PET) control films remain undamaged. Furthermore, the aqueous nanozyme retains ~75% of its initial catalytic activity across five consecutive degradation cycles following simple phase extraction. This study demonstrates that tailored, shape-complementary nanozymes provide a generalizable, selective biocatalytic alternative for the circular chemical recycling of recalcitrant engineering plastics.

leads.title: Design and Thermal Performance Analysis of a Multilayer Coolbox with Polyurethane as the Primary Insulation for Portable Fish-Hold Applications
leads.abstract: Post-harvest handling of fresh fish by small-scale fishermen is highly dependent on effective temperature control to minimize quality deterioration during storage and transportation. This study aimed to design, fabricate, and evaluate the thermal performance of a 70-L portable coolbox using rigid polyurethane foam as the primary thermal insulation material. The coolbox was constructed using a 3-cm-thick multilayer composite wall consisting of fiberglass (1.0 cm), meranti plywood (0.5 cm), aluminum foil (0.5 cm), and rigid polyurethane foam (1.0 cm). A rubber sealing strip and clamp locks were incorporated to reduce heat infiltration through the lid interface. Thermal performance was evaluated experimentally over 168 h under two loading conditions: 30 kg of block ice and a combination of 30 kg of block ice and 20 kg of fresh fish. A one-dimensional steady-state heat conduction model was also applied to estimate the thermal resistance and equivalent thermal conductivity of the composite wall. The results yielded a total thermal resistance of 0.4291 K/W and an equivalent thermal conductivity of 0.0606 W/(m·K). Polyurethane contributed approximately 84.15% of the total thermal resistance, indicating that it was the dominant insulating layer in the composite structure. During the first 72 h, the internal temperature remained within approximately 0–4 °C under both loading conditions. After 72 h, the internal temperature gradually increased as the ice load decreased, reaching 18–19 °C by the seventh day. The total material cost for fabricating one prototype was IDR 1,445,000. These findings indicate that the multilayer polyurethane-based coolbox can provide effective passive thermal insulation for short-term chilled fish storage in small-scale fishing operations.
leads.venue: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH AND ANALYSIS

leads.title: Poloxamer-Enabled Thermoresponsive Biobased Controlled-Release Fertilizer for On-Demand Nutrient Delivery.
leads.abstract: Synchronizing nutrient release of fertilizers with crop uptake remains a central challenge in precision agriculture. Here, we present a novel temperature-responsive biobased controlled-release fertilizer (TRBFs) incorporating Poloxamer 407 (F127) as a thermal switch within a castor oil-derived polyurethane coating. The optimized TRBF10 (3 wt.% coating rate, 10 wt.% F127 in coating) exhibits a sharp, reversible phase transition at ∼20°C, matching the phenological requirements of overwintering crops. As quantified by digital refractometry, the 30-day cumulative nitrogen release is suppressed to 9.22% at 10°C (crop dormancy) and increases 8.7-fold to 80.32% at 30°C (active growth). This scalable technology overcomes intrinsic limitations of conventional diffusion-controlled coated fertilizers and offers potential for on-demand nutrient delivery with reduced environmental loss. Our work establishes sustainable strategies for climate-adaptive precision agriculture and offers new insights and design paradigms for intelligent controlled-release materials.
leads.authors: Liu J, Li J, Li Z, Zhao X, Fang F, Liu Y, Wang S, Su B, Yao Y, Gao B, Zhang S, Yang Y.

leads.title: Scuffing Resistance of Castor Oil and Aminolyzed Castor Oil Enhanced with MoS₂ Nanoparticles
leads.abstract: The transition toward sustainable industrial practices has led to the development of eco-friendly vegetable oils (biolubricants) as alternatives to traditional petroleum-based lubricants. However, vegetable oils are inherently susceptible to oxidative and thermal degradation at high temperatures. To overcome this, chemical modification of the pure oil is commonly employed, which not only enhances thermo-oxidative stability but also improves intrinsic lubricity. To further boost lubrication under severe conditions, dispersing solid nanoparticles into the oil has emerged as a highly effective strategy. Therefore, this study investigates the scuffing behavior of MoS₂-based nanofluids formulated with castor oil (CO) and a chemically modified vegetable oil (aminolyzed castor oil—ACO). Scuffing tests were performed in a block-on-ring tribometer. Nanofluids containing 0.10, 0.15, and 0.20 wt.% MoS₂ were compared to their additive-free base oils. Friction force evolution was quantitatively analyzed to identify characteristic scuffing phases. Results demonstrated that MoS₂ increases severe scuffing resistance, with this resistance strongly depending on the base oil and nanoparticle concentration. Among the formulations, ACO with 0.10 wt.% MoS₂ exhibited the best performance, increasing the Weibull characteristic life (α) by approximately 36.7% compared with additive-free ACO. Furthermore, the nanofluids exhibited a more stable friction response during severe scuffing, in contrast to the pronounced friction instabilities observed with the additive-free base oils. SEM/EDS analyses revealed molybdenum oxides on worn surfaces, indicating tribochemical reactions and protective tribofilm formation activated by high temperature. Overall, chemical modification of the base oil (i.e., ACO) enhances the beneficial effects of MoS₂ nanoparticles, highlighting ACO-based nanofluids as promising lubricants for severe tribological applications.

leads.title: Physicochemical and Weibull statistical analysis of Parkinsonia aculeata fibers as biocomposite reinforcements
leads.abstract: The paper gives the first complete physicochemical and mechanical description of fibers obtained from the known woody plant called Parkinsonia aculeata, which is an underutilized plant in the Skikda region of Algeria, in order to assess its suitability as a reinforcement in biocomposite materials. The isolation of the fibers was carried out via 15 days of water retting, and the properties of the fibers were studied systematically using morphological, water absorption, and mechanical tests. The morphological analysis showed an average fiber diameter of 321 µm and a linear density of 2.15 g·m −1 , while the Weibull statistical analysis highlighted the existence of considerable variability in the diameter, which is characteristic of this natural fiber. Peleg’s equations of water absorption showed a lower equilibrium uptake in seawater than in distilled water because of the lower osmotic potential. Tensile tests were performed to check for the presence of a brittle failure mode that is typical of lignocellulosic fibers. Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) showed that the fiber was highly oriented and had a compact fibrillar structure, whereas energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) identified a high carbon (44.35 wt%) and oxygen (45.20 wt%) composition, confirming its lignocellulosic nature. The results confirm that Parkinsonia aculeata is a strong and viable natural fiber source that is locally available, with good potential for use as reinforcement in polymeric composite materials; however, the variability of the results means that it should be carefully statistically treated in material development.

leads.title: Interfacial engineering, processing, and microstructure relationships in PLA/Diss fiber biocomposites for improved mechanical performance
leads.abstract: This study reports the development of fully bio-based polylactic acid (PLA) biocomposites reinforced with short Ampelodesmos mauritanicus (Diss) fibers using a powder-based processing route. To improve fiber-matrix compatibility, the fibers were subjected to sequential HCl/NaOH treatment to modify their surface morphology. A fixed concentration of 10 wt.% was selected to isolate the effect of surface treatment on fiber-matrix interaction rather than to optimize the reinforcement level. Multiscale characterization using SEM, AFM, FTIR, Raman spectroscopy, and DSC showed that the treatment improved interfacial adhesion by promoting mechanical interlocking and molecular interactions between PLA and the exposed cellulose-rich fiber surface. AFM observations confirmed a marked increase in surface roughness, while DSC analysis revealed that treated fibers influenced PLA crystallization through the combined effects of heterogeneous nucleation and restricted chain mobility at the interface. These microstructural changes enhanced load transfer, with the treated-fiber composite reaching a Young’s modulus of 4.24 GPa and a tensile strength of 46.8 MPa. The powder-processing route also promoted homogeneous fiber dispersion and may help reduce thermal and shear-induced degradation compared with conventional melt processing. Overall, the results demonstrate that combining interfacial engineering with powder processing provides an effective strategy for designing lightweight, high-performance, and sustainable PLA/Diss biocomposites.
