Highly Permeable Polyamide Membranes Based on Hexafluoroisopropylidene Molecular Scaffold for Efficient Organic Solvent Nanofiltration
leads.abstract: Developing highly permeable polyamide (PA) thin‐film composite (TFC) membranes is a critical pathway for advancing organic solvent nanofiltration (OSN) in industrial chemical separations. Herein, we reported a dual‐regulation strategy utilizing a molecular scaffold to construct PA TFC membrane with enhanced solvent permeance. Acting as a “molecular scaffold”, the –C(CF 3 ) 2 – group of the 2,2‐bis (4‐aminophenyl) hexafluoropropane (BAFP) effectively modulates the packing behavior of PA chains through steric hindrance. Simultaneously, the fluorinated moieties reduce transport resistance by weakening solvent‐membrane interactions. The prepared TFC‐BAFP membrane exhibited an excellent methanol permeance of 20.3 L m −2 h −1 bar −1 , a 3.4‐fold increase over conventional TFC membrane prepared with 4,4'‐diaminodiphenylmethane (MDA). Furthermore, the enhanced rigidity of the BAFP monomer imparted great structural stability and solvent resistance, even under harsh chemical conditions. The TFC‐BAFP membrane also demonstrated efficient sieving for photosensitizer/precursor mixture system and exhibited significantly higher concentration efficiency than the commercial oNF‐2 OSN membrane. This work proposes a molecular engineering strategy for developing highly permeable polyamide OSN membranes by regulating monomer steric hindrance and surface properties, contributing to the advancement of sustainable separation technologies in the chemical and pharmaceutical industries.

leads.title: Tunable Acidity of Sulfated Zr–Sn Mixed Oxides for Solvent‐Free Sorbitol Dehydration to Isosorbide
leads.abstract: One of the most important processes in creating sustainable monomers for high‐performance polymers is the catalytic dehydration of sorbitol obtained from biomass to isosorbide. This study investigated a series of sulfated Zr x Sn 1 − x O 2 ( x = 0.1–0.9) mixed oxides prepared by coprecipitation method for sorbitol dehydration under solvent‐free conditions. Comprehensive evaluation of different characterization techniques, i.e., X‐ray diffraction, Fourier transform infrared, transmission electron microscope, N 2 physisorption, and NH 3 ‐TPD demonstrated that surface acidity, textural characteristics, and catalytic activity were greatly affected by catalyst composition. Catalyst with intermediate Zr content (0.4–0.6) had an ideal balance of weak, medium, and strong Brønsted acid sites, which resulted in complete conversion of sorbitol and higher isosorbide selectivity. 100% sorbitol conversion and 87% isosorbide selectivity were achieved with sulfated (S)‐Zr 0.5 Sn 0.5 O 2 at 220 °C within 3 h, exceeding many reported heterogeneous solid acids catalyst. A minor loss in catalyst activity was observed after four cycles, showing its potential for long‐term isosorbide production.

leads.title: Citric acid-treated lignin as a functional regulator for PBS/PBAT biodegradable films
Lignin-based microcarriers for controlled fungicide release
leads.abstract: The excessive and inefficient use of agrochemicals generates severe environmental and health concerns, urging the development of sustainable delivery systems. Herein, we report the encapsulation of the fungicide difenoconazole within kraft lignin microcarriers prepared by spray drying. The process yielded spherical particles ranging from 1 to 10 μm, with high encapsulation efficiency. Structural analysis by Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy evidenced chemical interactions between lignin and difenoconazole, confirming the incorporation of the fungicide into the polymer structure. Release studies under different pH conditions revealed a biphasic profile, characterized by an initial burst followed by a slower, sustained release, with strong pH dependence. Kinetic modeling using singular value decomposition (SVD) and a first-order model showed excellent correlation ( R > 0.99), suggesting that the release process is governed by the partial solubilization of lignin and the release of difenoconazole located in the outer regions of the microcarriers. Furthermore, in vivo phytotoxicity trials demonstrated that the developed microcarriers are highly biocompatible at lower doses; formulations at a concentration of 0.01% triggered a significant biostimulant response, as evidenced by an increased germination index (GI). Overall, our results demonstrate that a precise dosage configuration optimizes the safety profile of the encapsulated matrix, highlighting the potential of these lignin-based microcarriers as a scalable and eco-friendly platform for controlled fungicide delivery, capable of extending field persistence, reducing application frequency, and mitigating environmental impact.

leads.title: Hyper-Cross-Linked Ionic Polymer Bearing Phosphate and Hydroxyl for Catalytic Cycloaddition of CO2 with Epoxide under Atmospheric Pressure
leads.abstract: Converting CO2 to valuable chemicals under mild conditions remains a significant challenge. Herein, we accomplish a solvent-, metal-, and additive-free catalytic transformation of epoxides with CO2 under atmospheric pressure using an ionic polymer (H-IPyBPOH) as the catalyst. This polymer is synthesized via Friedel–Crafts alkylation between a phosphate-bearing hydrogen-bond donor and an imidazolium-based ionic linker. The resulting material contains potent hydrogen-bonding sites (P–OH), imidazolium cations, and bromide anions as nucleophiles. It exhibits excellent catalytic activity and recyclability for the cycloaddition of CO2 to epoxides. Combined DFT calculations and experimental results reveal that the high performance arises from the synergistic cooperation of hydrogen-bonding sites for epoxide activation, basic pyridine sites for CO2 activation, and bromide ions for the ring-opening attack. Moreover, the catalyst shows broad substrate compatibility and an outstanding structural stability. It can be easily recovered by filtration and reused for at least six cycles without a significant loss of activity.

leads.title: Grafted β-Cyclodextrin Methoxy Polyethylene Glycol Copolymers as Superplasticizing Admixtures for Cement Mortar
leads.abstract: Synthetic-based plasticizers are often used in the masonry industry to improve the rheological and mechanical properties of mortar, but these systems are neither sustainable nor eco-friendly. In this study, several copolymers were prepared that contain grafted β-cyclodextrin (βCD) and its modified forms (HprβCD, FβCD, SucβCD, and CarβCD) were grafted onto methoxy polyethylene glycol (MPEG) and were evaluated as hybrid bio-based plasticizing admixtures for cement mortar. The grafted copolymers were characterized by IR/1H NMR spectroscopy, powder XRD, TGA, and DSC. Their performance as admixtures were evaluated based on flowability, consistency, rheological parameters, and mechanical properties of mortar in fresh and hardened states. Spectral (27Al and 29Si NMR, XRD) measurements of the cementitious samples provided insight on the intermolecular interactions of the mortar components. At low concentrations, 1.0 wt %, the copolymers were effective plasticizers, increasing the mortar fluidity in comparison to the control sample without admixtures. At a 0.30: 1 water-to-cement ratio, the water reduction capacity was up to 20%, keeping the mortar flow within an appropriate range. Besides, hydration-related behavior was indirectly assessed through strength development and spectroscopic analyses. The mortar sample with HprβCD-MPEG had a higher compressive strength when the admixture concentration was changed from 1% (31 MPa) to 2% (40 MPa) showing the capacity of the copolymer as a strength enhancer. The copolymers CarβCD-MPEG (35 MPa) and FβCD-MPEG (42 MPa) also reached the compressive strength typical for a 28 day mortar sample, whereas a lower value was noted for the 7 day control (30 MPa). Relative to commercial superplasticizers, the graft copolymers showed high potential as suitable alternatives for conventional fully non-renewable admixtures.

leads.title: Cross-Linking Simulation at Metal Oxide-Thermoset Interfaces Using Quantum Chemical and Molecular Dynamics Methods
leads.abstract: Understanding how oxidized metal surfaces catalyze the curing of epoxy resins is essential in improving the reliabilities of epoxy-metal oxide interfaces in multimaterial systems. The catalytic effects of hydroxylated oxidized tin metal (SnO2) surfaces on the cross-linking of epoxy resins were investigated using a hybrid approach that combined quantum chemical calculations with molecular dynamics simulations, wherein the reaction kinetics were modeled using Monte Carlo techniques. Analyzing the reaction pathways and spatial distributions at different hydroxylation levels revealed that fully hydroxylated SnO2 surfaces promoted surface-initiated curing, whereas partially hydroxylated surfaces led to more dispersed reaction propagation. These results highlight the critical roles of the interfacial OH groups in regulating the reaction kinetics, cross-linking density, and polymer network structure. In addition to these mechanistic insights, this study establishes a generalizable methodology for use in probing curing reactions at epoxy-metal oxide interfaces, and it clarifies how metal oxidation states govern interfacial catalysis. Critically, it bridges atomic-scale mechanisms with macroscopic interfacial reliability, addressing the broader question of how the interfacial chemistry dictates the formation and performance of a thermoset network. The conclusions further indicate that surface hydroxylation can be used to regulate the curing efficiency and cross-link distribution, which is critical in rationally designing epoxy formulations and surface treatments.

leads.title: Castor Oil as a Renewable Reaction Medium for Sustainable Domino Synthesis of Functionalized Epoxyisoindolyl Ureas
leads.abstract: The development of renewable reaction media that can replace conventional organic solvents without affecting reaction performance is highly desirable for the advancement of sustainable chemical processes. In this study, the properties of Castor oil as a bio-based solvent were investigated in the context of a domino multicomponent synthesis of functionalized epoxyisoindolyl ureas. This synthesis involved a tandem condensation/Diels–Alder sequence, with the use of furfurylamine, phenyl isocyanate, and various N-substituted maleimides. In the absence of a catalyst and under mild reaction conditions, the desired products were obtained in satisfactory yields and with generally high diastereoselectivity without the need for chromatographic purification. In the course of the investigation, it was established that among the vegetable oils under consideration, Castor oil demonstrated the highest reaction efficiency. Furthermore, it was ascertained that this oil could be easily recovered and reused. Its superior performance is attributed to its high hydrogen-bonding capability and favorable Hansen solubility parameter profile, which enhance substrate solubilization and facilitate hydrogen bond-assisted organization of the reacting species. The use of Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) monitoring and DFT calculations has provided support for a proposed mechanism in which the rapid formation of a urea intermediate occurs prior to the intermolecular cycloaddition reaction. In comparison with conventional stepwise protocols, the present methodology integrates multiple bond-forming events into a single operation, thereby reducing purification requirements while employing a renewable and recyclable reaction medium. The findings of this study demonstrate that Castor oil provides an effective platform for sustainable domino synthesis and highlight the potential of vegetable-oil-based solvents for greener multicomponent transformations.

leads.title: PAZy: an expanded and actively maintained database of experimentally validated plastic-active enzymes
leads.abstract: The Plastics-Active Enzyme Database (PAZy) is a manually curated resource for enzymes experimentally shown to act on synthetic or bio-based plastics. It was developed to distinguish experimentally verified plastics-active enzymes from computationally predicted or insufficiently supported candidates. Here, we present an expanded version of PAZy, implemented as a relational database containing >450 plastics-active enzymes with more detailed metadata, broader substrate coverage, and large language model-assisted curation of activity data. The redesigned web interface now enables browsing by protein or plastic substrate, detailed inspections of individual protein entries as well as programmatic access through a public representational state transfer (REST) application programming interface (API). This functionality enables scientists to freely implement PAZy into their own research workflows. By using evidence-based manual curation, PAZy provides a high-confidence resource for both comparative analyses and enzyme discovery in the rapidly growing field of enzymatic plastic degradation. PAZy is freely available at https://www.pazy.eu.

leads.title: Tailoring the structural, optical, and electrical properties of PVDF/Ppy/MWCNT nanocomposites through synergistic hybrid reinforcement
leads.abstract: Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based nanocomposites incorporating polypyrrole (Ppy) and multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) were systematically developed with the objective of enhancing their structural, surface, optical, and electrical characteristics for advanced multifunctional applications. The nanocomposites were developed by a solution mixing and casting method, in which Ppy and MWCNTs were incorporated into the PVDF matrix at different loading i.e., 2, 4, 6, and 10 wt%. The prepared nanocomposite films were systematically characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM), UV-Vis-NIR spectroscopy, and dielectric and impedance measurements to evaluate their structural, morphological, optical and electrical characteristics. XRD analysis revealed a predominantly semi-crystalline structure with increasing amorphous character and controlled crystallite evolution governed by the increased loading of nanofiller. UV-Vis-NIR spectroscopic analysis demonstrated enhanced optical absorption, progressive bandgap narrowing, and increased disorder-induced localized states with increasing MWCNT loading, indicating enhanced electronic interactions. FTIR analysis confirmed strong interfacial interactions between the constituents without significant alteration of their chemical structures. Dielectric and impedance studies confirmed that interfacial polarization dominates at low frequencies, whereas hopping conduction governs the high-frequency response, resulting in enhanced dielectric constant (400 to 1000) and electrical conductivity (1.76 × 10 −5 to 5.46 × 10 −5 ) and reduced impedance with increasing loading of nanofiller. FESEM analysis revealed a heterogeneous yet interconnected morphology, with relatively well-dispersed fillers at 4 wt% facilitating the formation of a partial conductive network. The hybridization of conductive polymer and carbon nanofillers within the PVDF matrix promotes strong interfacial interactions, leading to improved charge transport, interfacial polarization, and formation of efficient conductive networks. Thus, the synergistic effects of Ppy and MWCNTs significantly improved the multifunctional performance of the PVDF-based nanocomposites, demonstrating their potential for applications in flexible electronics, energy-storage devices, and advanced sensing systems.

leads.title: Experimental study on shockwave protection of aerogel sandwich polycarbonate composite structures
leads.abstract: To address the anti-blast demands of military equipment such as armoured vehicles and naval vessels, lightweight sandwich structures with silica aerogel core and polycarbonate (PC) panels are experimentally investigated via shock tube tests under four blast pressures (P1 = 105 kPa, P2 = 180 kPa, P3 = 227 kPa, P4 = 275 kPa). Codes “1” and “0” stand for aerogel sandwich and pure PC sheet; “10” denotes aerogel-fronted double-layer arrangement and “01” the PC-first counterpart. Single-layer, double-layer (10) and triple-layer (110) structures achieve peak overpressure attenuation of 45.68%, 54.32% and 64.20% under low-medium loads. Structural protection degrades with rising load beyond the critical threshold P3, and aerogel-fronted layouts outperform PC-first schemes throughout tests. This study supplies experimental basis for optimizing lightweight anti-shock structures.

leads.title: Nano-encapsulation of peppermint essential oil in chitosan nanoparticles improves salinity tolerance in lettuce
Analysis of structural transformations in biodegradable polymer composites as a function of film-forming components and functional additives
leads.abstract: The use of polylactic acid (PLA) and polycaprolactone (PCL) as film-forming components in composites with thermoplastic starch (TPS) was investigated. An optimal composition of the functional additive in TPS was developed using chitosan and lactic acid (chitosan lactate, LC). The physical and mechanical properties of the PLA/TPS and PCL/TPS composites were determined. The structure of the composites and its changes following thermomechanical treatment were studied using FT-IR spectroscopy. Mass spectrometric analysis was performed, and the characteristic mass spectra of ion fragments resulting from the thermal decomposition of PLA, LC, and PLA/TPS were analyzed; their intensities at the peak region were measured. Structural changes in the compositions were studied using DSC and TGA methods, and the mass loss and rate of mass loss during thermal decomposition were quantitatively determined.

leads.title: Cellulose microfibril interactions with water: A density functional theory study of H2O incorporation into the cellulose microfibril structure
leads.abstract: Periodic density functional theory calculations were performed on the 234432 model of primary plant cell wall cellulose microfibrils. Energy minimization calculations of dry, water external, water internal and water internal+external were carried out to explore the structure of cellulose hydration and energetics of H-bonding. Results indicate that the cellulose structure can accommodate a significant amount of H 2 O without disrupting the XRD-determined structure. H 2 O-cellulose H-bonds form in the interior that strengthen the cellulose microfibril. The external H-bonding was also analyzed to assess potential pathways for C-O-C linkage hydrolysis. The potential for D 2 O to diffuse into the structure and lead to H-D exchange between water and cellulose was also tested.

leads.title: A Comprehensive Review on Diverse aspects of Natural and Synthetic Mosquito Repellents
leads.abstract: The present review was based on the diverse aspects of natural and synthetic mosquito repellents.Every year, 2.5 million cases of dengue & chikungunya are caused by the Aedes aegypti mosquito.Avoiding direct human-mosquito contact is the primary way to reduce mosquitoborne illnesses.It is highly advised that susceptible people who live in places where mosquitoes are still a possible threat apply insect repellents to all exposed skin areas.Warm-blooded animal's sweat contains lactic acid and CO2, which are attractive chemicals to mosquitoes.Essential oils, which are utilized as natural repellents, are mostly derived from plants.For instance, citronella oil, clove, eucalyptus, rosemary, peppermint, and lemon grass can deter mosquitoes.The most powerful synthetic repellent is N, N-diethyl-meta-toluamide (DEET), a toxic chemical that may produce carbon monoxide and a natural odor that resembles that of the human body.Moreover, 3-[N Butyl-N-acetyl]-amino propionic acid (IR3535) is the best mosquito repellent which is more effective than DEET for longer time.In conclusion, natural and synthetic mosquito repellents are effective in managing the insect's spread diseases.However, other methods including physical methods i.e., mosquito net, medicated net, non-medicated net, mosquito trap and mechanical methods i.e., electric zipper and mosquito's magnet are promising as strong mosquito repellent without any side effects to the host cell/body....

leads.title: Sparking Nanometal Oxides for Modifying Surface Properties of Thermoplastic Starch/Carboxymethyl Cellulose Blends
leads.abstract: A thermoplastic starch (TPS) was developed by blending cassava starch in a 70/30% wt/wt ratio. Carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) 5% wt/wt was added during TPS solution mixing at 80 °C. Sparking technology was applied to deposit nanometal particles onto polymer surfaces. Nanometal oxide particles of Ag, Zn, and Cu were sparked on the surface of TPS and TPS/CMC samples to investigate the effects of the metal type and polymer surface chemistry on the resulting material properties. The surface morphology, element distribution, mechanical properties, color characteristics, wettability, and thermal behavior were evaluated. The tensile strength of TPS/CMC increased from 2.2 MPa to 5.0 MPa with Ag sparking, while the contact angle of TPS/CMC increased from 41.3° to 91.6°, 89.3°, and 95.1° after Ag, Zn, and Cu sparking, respectively. SEM–EDS confirmed the deposition and distribution of the nanometal types on the polymer surfaces. The sparked TPS/CMC samples exhibited higher contact angles than the sparked TPS sample due to the strong interactions between the deposited nanometal particles and –COOH functional groups of CMC. The thermal analysis showed that the deposited metal type influenced the degradation behavior of the TPS and TPS/CMC samples. Sparking technology provided effective surface modification via depositing nanometal particles onto TPS/CMC, resulting in uniform particle distribution and enhanced mechanical and surface wettability properties, with potential applications in the sustainable packaging industry.

Hyperbranched Epoxy Topology Enables Covalent Interphases and Penetration‐Locking Thermoset Networks
leads.abstract: The inherent trade‐off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide‐containing dual‐role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual‐phase “penetration‐locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross‐link density. At the fiber‐matrix interface, thiol‐terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol‐ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost‐effective T300‐based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800‐based composites, while T800‐based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.

leads.title: Lignin‐Based Green Soil Stabilizer for Haul Roads in Mining Areas: Development, Performance, and Mechanism
leads.abstract: Dust from haul roads in open‐pit mines is one of the primary pollution sources in mining areas, whereas conventional soil stabilizers have limited environmental friendliness and durability. A composite soil stabilizer is prepared with renewable lignin as the main component, combined with hydroxyethyl cellulose (HEC), sodium dodecyl sulfonate (SDS), and alkyl polyglucoside (APG). Two haul‐road soils with different properties are used, and the optimal formulation within the investigated factor levels (2% lignin, 2.25% HEC, 0.05% SDS, and 0.09% APG) is determined by an orthogonal experimental design. The 7‐day unconfined compressive strength of stabilized soil is approximately 5–8 times that of the corresponding untreated soil and further increases with curing age. After 7 wet–dry and 5 freeze–thaw cycles, the water stability coefficient and strength retention rate of the 28‐day‐cured specimens remain above 80%. After 72 h of wind erosion, the mass retention rate remains above 95%. X‐ray diffraction results show no obvious changes in the major crystalline phase composition. Scanning electron microscopy shows that surface coverage and interparticle connections gradually increase with curing age, and the soil structure becomes more continuous and dense. These results provide experimental evidence for soil stabilization and wind erosion control on mine haul roads.

leads.title: Promoter Editing of Starch Branching Enzyme IIb and Granule-Bound Starch Synthase I Balances Resistant Starch Content and Amylose Content in Rice
Robust bio-based epoxy vitrimers with dual dynamic boronic ester and β-hydroxy ester bonds: self-healing, weldability and recyclability
leads.abstract: Development of bio-based epoxy vitrimers faces a persistent trade-off between high mechanical/thermal performance and efficient dynamic reversibility for self-healing and recycling. Herein, we report a series of furan-based epoxy vitrimers (DGFB-x) that integrate dual dynamic covalent bonds, boronic ester and β -hydroxy ester, within a single network. These materials are synthesized by curing a bio-based diglycidyl furan-2,5-dicarboxylate (DGF) monomer with an aminophenylboronic acid-derived crosslinker ( di -BONH 2 ). The chemical structures are confirmed by FTIR and NMR, and the crosslinked nature is verified by swelling tests. By adjusting the crosslinker ratio, the tensile strength can be tuned from 48.5 to 75.4 MPa and the Young’s modulus from 137.3 to 512.5 MPa, while the elongation at break decreases correspondingly. Thermal analysis shows excellent stability with initial decomposition temperatures ( T 5% ) above 270 °C and heat-resistant indices ( T s ) up to 163.3 °C. Owing to the dual dynamic exchange mechanisms, the optimized DGFB-1.0 exhibits outstanding self-healing efficiency (98.2% at 90 °C for 60 min), high welding efficiency (>94%), remarkable reprocessability (81.3% tensile strength retention after three cycles), and effective chemical recycling via alcoholysis (recovery >90%). Furthermore, DGFB-1.0-based carbon-fiber-reinforced composites are successfully recycled with preserved carbon fiber quality and mechanical properties. This work proposes a tentative molecular design approach aimed at alleviating the performance-recyclability conflict in sustainable thermosets.
